stem: When did the Financial Advisers Act come into force in Singapore?

options.A: 26 November 2010
options.B: 1 October 2002
options.C: 2 December 2005
options.D: 1 January 2012

explanation: The FAA came into force on 1 October 2002. The 2010 date relates to the Representative Notification Framework, 2005 to structured deposits becoming investment products, and 2012 to FAA-N16 taking effect.

stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the principles underlying the FAA and FAR?

options.A: Protecting the interests of customers
options.B: Accountability of financial advisers for their representatives
options.C: Safeguarding the independence of advice
options.D: Maximising the profitability of the financial advisory industry

explanation: Industry profitability is not a legislative principle. The framework is built on customer protection, consistency of regulation, accountability of advisers for their representatives and independence of advice.

stem: Which type of entity may apply for a financial adviser's licence under the FAA?

options.A: A corporation only
options.B: Any individual with the required qualifications
options.C: A partnership of licensed representatives
options.D: A sole proprietorship registered with ACRA

explanation: Only a corporation may hold a financial adviser's licence. Individuals act as representatives of a principal; partnerships and sole proprietorships cannot be licensed as financial advisers.

stem: An unlicensed company describes itself in marketing materials as a licensed financial adviser. Which provision does it contravene?

options.A: Section 36, for lacking a reasonable basis
options.B: Section 45, for failing to disclose interests
options.C: Section 18(1), for holding out as a licensed financial adviser
options.D: Section 73, for omitting the public register entry

explanation: Holding oneself out as a licensed financial adviser without a licence breaches the holding-out prohibition. The reasonable basis and interest disclosure provisions govern conduct of licensed advisers, and the register provision concerns representatives.

stem: Which of the following is an exempt financial adviser under Section 20(1) of the FAA?

options.A: A law firm giving incidental investment advice
options.B: A financial journalist
options.C: A bank licensed under the Banking Act
options.D: A person advising 30 accredited investors

explanation: Banks are among the institutions exempted from holding a financial adviser's licence under Section 20(1). Lawyers and journalists are excluded persons under the First Schedule, and the 30 accredited investors exemption arises under Regulation 27(1)(d).

stem: What is the effect of being an exempt financial adviser under Section 20(1)?

options.A: Exemption from licensing but continued compliance with FAA conduct of business requirements
options.B: Complete exemption from the FAA and all MAS Notices
options.C: Exemption from conduct rules but not from licensing
options.D: Exemption only from paying licence fees

explanation: Exempt financial advisers need not hold a licence but remain bound by the conduct of business provisions and applicable MAS Notices. The exemption is from licensing, not from regulation.

stem: An accountant occasionally comments on investment matters strictly as part of preparing clients' accounts. Under the FAA she is most likely:

options.A: An exempt financial adviser under Section 20(1)
options.B: A provisional representative
options.C: Required to hold a financial adviser's licence
options.D: An excluded person under the First Schedule

explanation: Professionals such as accountants and lawyers whose advice is incidental to their practice are excluded from the definition of financial adviser under the First Schedule. The Section 20(1) exemptions cover institutions like banks and insurers.

stem: Which of the following is a financial advisory service under the Second Schedule to the FAA?

options.A: Arranging a contract of motor insurance
options.B: Arranging a contract of insurance in respect of life policies
options.C: Providing custody services for securities
options.D: Dealing in capital markets products as principal

explanation: Arranging life policies (other than reinsurance) is a listed financial advisory service. Arranging general insurance such as motor cover, custody services and dealing as principal are not financial advisory services.

stem: Which activity does NOT fall within the financial advisory services regulated under the FAA?

options.A: Issuing research reports on investment products
options.B: Advising a client on the purchase of a general insurance fire policy
options.C: Marketing a collective investment scheme
options.D: Advising others concerning life policies

explanation: Advice on general insurance such as fire policies is not a financial advisory service. Issuing research on investment products, marketing collective investment schemes and advising on life policies are all within the Second Schedule.

stem: From which date were structured deposits prescribed as investment products under the FAA?

options.A: 1 October 2002
options.B: 1 March 2006
options.C: 8 October 2018
options.D: 2 December 2005

explanation: Structured deposits became prescribed investment products with effect from 2 December 2005. The 2006 date is when the Dual Currency Investments Notice took effect, and 2018 relates to overseas-listed product risk warnings.

stem: Since 26 November 2010, what is the position on renewal of a financial adviser's licence?

options.A: The licence no longer requires periodic renewal and remains in force until revoked, suspended or surrendered
options.B: The licence must be renewed every year
options.C: The licence must be renewed every three years
options.D: The licence lapses automatically unless business volume targets are met

explanation: Licences granted under the FAA ceased to require periodic renewal from 26 November 2010; they continue in force until revoked, suspended or surrendered. There is no annual or triennial renewal cycle.

stem: Under Regulation 27(1)(d) of the FAR, a person is exempt from holding a financial adviser's licence if he provides financial advisory services concerning investment products (other than life policies) to not more than how many accredited investors?
explanation: The exemption is capped at not more than 30 accredited investors. Exceeding that number, or advising retail investors, takes the person outside the exemption.

stem: Which product type can NEVER be advised on under the Regulation 27(1)(d) exemption?

options.A: Securities
options.B: Life policies
options.C: Units in collective investment schemes
options.D: Exchange-traded derivatives

explanation: The exemption covers advice on investment products other than life policies. Advice on life policies to accredited investors cannot rely on Regulation 27(1)(d).

stem: Mr Tan earned S$320,000 in the preceding 12 months but has net personal assets of only S$800,000. Does he qualify as an accredited investor?

options.A: No, because his net personal assets are below S$2 million
options.B: No, because he must satisfy both the income and asset tests
options.C: Only if MAS grants an individual waiver
options.D: Yes, because his income in the preceding 12 months is not less than S$300,000

explanation: The tests are alternatives. Income of at least S$300,000 in the preceding 12 months qualifies him even though his assets fall short of the S$2 million net personal asset and S$1 million net financial asset thresholds.

stem: A private company has total assets of S$18 million and liabilities of S$9 million. Does it meet the accredited investor test for corporations?

options.A: No, because its net assets of S$9 million do not exceed S$10 million
options.B: Yes, because total assets exceed S$10 million
options.C: Yes, because any incorporated company is an accredited investor
options.D: No, because only listed companies can be accredited investors

explanation: The corporate test looks at net assets exceeding S$10 million. Net assets here are S$18 million minus S$9 million, which equals S$9 million, so the company does not qualify even though gross assets exceed the threshold.

stem: What is the maximum penalty under Section 17 for improper use of the title 'financial adviser' or 'life insurance broker'?

options.A: S$25,000 and S$2,500 per day for a continuing offence
options.B: S$50,000 and S$5,000 per day for a continuing offence
options.C: S$12,500 and S$1,250 per day for a continuing offence
options.D: S$100,000 or 2 years imprisonment

explanation: Misuse of the restricted titles attracts a fine up to S$12,500 with a further S$1,250 for each day of a continuing offence. The larger figures relate to other offences such as Notice breaches and officer liability.

stem: Under Regulation 21, a financial adviser may use the word 'independent' only if, among other conditions, it:

options.A: Has been licensed for at least ten years
options.B: Receives no commission or other benefit from product providers that creates product bias, and operates free of any restriction or conflict of interest from its connections with product providers
options.C: Advises only accredited investors
options.D: Is a member of an industry association for independent advisers

explanation: 'Independent' may be used only where there is no commission or benefit creating product bias, no restriction on the products advised upon, and no conflict of interest arising from connections with product providers. Tenure, clientele and association membership are irrelevant.

stem: A licence applicant aggrieved by an MAS refusal wishes to appeal. What is the correct route?

options.A: Apply to the High Court within 6 months
options.B: Request arbitration through the industry association
options.C: Submit a fresh application to MAS within 14 days
options.D: Appeal to the Minister within 30 days, whose decision is final

explanation: Appeals against MAS decisions under the FAA are made to the Minister within 30 days, and the Minister's decision is final. There is no appeal to the courts or arbitration route.

stem: Which of the following is a ground on which MAS may refuse to enter an individual's appointment as a representative?

options.A: The individual is an undischarged bankrupt
options.B: The individual is above 50 years of age
options.C: The individual previously worked for a competitor
options.D: The individual holds only a polytechnic diploma

explanation: Undischarged bankruptcy, unsatisfied judgment debts, compromises with creditors and convictions involving fraud or dishonesty are refusal grounds. Age, prior employers and holding a polytechnic diploma are not.

stem: In which situations may a representative act for more than one principal?

options.A: Whenever the representative discloses the arrangement to clients
options.B: Only where the principals operate in different product markets
options.C: Where MAS approves it in writing, or where the principals are related corporations
options.D: Never - the one-principal rule has no exceptions

explanation: Section 27(1) allows multiple principals only with MAS written approval or where the principals are related corporations. Client disclosure or serving different markets does not create an exception.

stem: What is the maximum penalty for a representative who breaches the one-principal rule in Section 27(1)?

options.A: A fine of S$12,500 only
options.B: A fine up to S$25,000 or imprisonment up to 12 months or both, with up to S$2,500 per day for a continuing offence
options.C: A fine up to S$100,000 or imprisonment up to 2 years
options.D: Suspension of the principal's licence

explanation: Contravening the one-principal rule attracts a fine up to S$25,000 or up to 12 months imprisonment or both, plus up to S$2,500 for each day the offence continues. The S$100,000 and 2 years figures apply to officer liability offences.

stem: A principal permits an individual who is not an appointed representative to provide financial advisory services on its behalf. What is the principal's maximum liability under Section 22(9)?

options.A: A fine up to S$25,000 or 12 months imprisonment
options.B: A fine up to S$12,500 plus S$1,250 per day
options.C: A written warning for a first offence
options.D: A fine up to S$50,000, with a further S$5,000 per day for a continuing offence

explanation: The principal faces a fine up to S$50,000 plus up to S$5,000 per day for a continuing offence - double the penalty faced by the individual who acts without appointment.

stem: A principal is charged under Section 32(1) with providing false information to MAS in a representative's appointment lodgment. Which defence is available?

options.A: It had made all reasonable inquiries and believed on reasonable grounds the statement was true
options.B: The representative supplied the information, so only he is liable
options.C: The error was corrected within 30 days
options.D: The false information caused no loss to any client

explanation: Section 32 provides a defence where the person made all reasonable inquiries and reasonably believed the statement to be true. Blaming the representative, later correction or absence of client loss is not a defence.

stem: Under Regulation 8A, an appointed representative must commence business within what period of his appointment, and the principal must notify MAS of cessation of business within what period?

options.A: 3 months to commence; 14 days to notify
options.B: 12 months to commence; 3 months to notify
options.C: 6 months to commence; 1 month to notify
options.D: 1 month to commence; 6 months to notify

explanation: The representative must commence business within 6 months of appointment, and cessation of business must be notified within 1 month. Other timelines - next business day for particulars changes and 14 days for Form 18 - govern different events.

stem: When a representative ceases to act for his principal, the principal must lodge Form 18 with MAS within:

options.A: 1 month of cessation
options.B: 14 days of cessation
options.C: 6 months of cessation
options.D: The next business day

explanation: Form 18 notifying cessation of appointment must be lodged within 14 days. The next business day timeline applies to changes in particulars, and the other periods relate to commencing and ceasing business operations.

stem: Which statement about a provisional representative is correct?

options.A: His status is valid for up to 12 months
options.B: He may meet clients alone once he passes one CMFAS module
options.C: He need not have been licensed overseas if he has a degree
options.D: His status is valid for up to 3 months, and his principal undertakes that he will be accompanied at client meetings

explanation: Provisional representative status lasts at most 3 months, and the principal gives undertakings including accompaniment at client meetings, copying the supervisor on emails and no unaccompanied telephone communications. Twelve months refers to the required continuous overseas licensing period, not the validity.

stem: Under Section 34(1), a licensed financial adviser recommending a designated investment product must disclose to the client:

options.A: Only the projected returns of the product
options.B: Only the fees payable to the adviser
options.C: All material information, including terms and conditions, benefits, risks, and fees and charges
options.D: Only information the client specifically requests

explanation: The disclosure duty covers all material information on the product - its terms, benefits, risks and charges - not merely returns, fees or items the client happens to ask about.

stem: A representative highlights a product's bonus features but stays silent on its surrender charges. This most directly breaches:

options.A: The obligation to disclose material product information under Section 34
options.B: The premium account rules under Section 41
options.C: The one-principal rule under Section 27
options.D: The register of interests requirement under Regulation 20A

explanation: Surrender charges are material information that must be disclosed when recommending the product. The premium account, one-principal and register of interests provisions deal with different obligations.

stem: What is the maximum penalty under Section 35 for a licensed financial adviser who makes false or misleading statements in providing financial advisory services?

options.A: A fine up to S$12,500
options.B: A fine up to S$25,000 only
options.C: Revocation of licence with no criminal penalty
options.D: A fine up to S$50,000 or imprisonment up to 12 months or both

explanation: False or misleading statements attract a fine up to S$50,000 or up to 12 months imprisonment or both. The smaller amounts apply to title misuse and to representations about insurance proposals.

stem: Can a licensed financial adviser be liable under Section 35 for omitting information rather than stating something untrue?

options.A: No, only affirmative false statements are caught
options.B: Yes, where the omission of material facts makes what was said misleading
options.C: Only if the client suffers actual loss
options.D: Only if the omission was in a written document

explanation: Liability extends to statements rendered misleading by the omission of material facts. Actual client loss and written form are not preconditions for the offence.

stem: To satisfy Section 36, a recommendation must be based on:

options.A: The client's investment objectives, financial situation and particular needs
options.B: The commission payable on the product
options.C: The adviser's quarterly sales targets
options.D: The most popular product among other clients

explanation: A reasonable basis requires considering the client's objectives, financial situation and particular needs. Commissions, sales targets and product popularity are irrelevant to suitability.

stem: A client loses money after acting on a recommendation made without a reasonable basis. Under Section 36(3), the client may:

options.A: Only lodge a complaint with MAS
options.B: Demand automatic cancellation of the licence
options.C: Bring a civil action to recover the loss as damages
options.D: Claim from the Policy Owners' Protection Fund

explanation: Section 36(3) creates a civil remedy allowing the client to sue for damages for loss caused by the breach. It operates in addition to, not instead of, any regulatory action.

stem: Under Section 37, a lien claimed by a licensed financial adviser over a client's property is:

options.A: Always valid if disclosed in the client agreement
options.B: Void unless it is for fees, charges or other amounts properly due from the client
options.C: Valid for up to 90 days only
options.D: Valid only with the approval of the client's bank

explanation: A lien or claim on client property is void except to the extent of fees, charges or amounts properly owing. Disclosure in an agreement does not validate a wider lien.

stem: A licensed financial adviser mortgages securities belonging to its clients to secure its own bank borrowing. The mortgage is:

options.A: Valid if the bank acted in good faith
options.B: Valid up to the value of fees owed by clients
options.C: Voidable at the adviser's option
options.D: Void

explanation: Any charge or mortgage over client's money or property to secure the adviser's own obligations is void. Good faith of the lender does not save it.

stem: How must a licensed financial adviser carrying on insurance broking hold premium moneys received from clients?

options.A: In a separate insurance broking premium account with a bank
options.B: In its general operating account, with proper bookkeeping
options.C: In cash in a company safe
options.D: In an overseas account earning higher interest

explanation: Premium moneys must be paid into a separate insurance broking premium account maintained with a bank, keeping them segregated from the adviser's own funds.

stem: Which withdrawal from an insurance broking premium account is permitted?

options.A: Payment of staff salaries during a cash flow shortage
options.B: Payment of premiums to the insurer for the client's policies
options.C: Investment in the adviser's own unit trust
options.D: A short-term loan to a director

explanation: Withdrawals are restricted to prescribed purposes such as paying premiums over to insurers or refunding clients. Using the account for salaries, investments or loans is prohibited.

stem: Under Section 42, a licensed financial adviser may place a risk with an unlicensed insurer in which situation?

options.A: Whenever the premium quoted is lower
options.B: Whenever the client signs a consent form
options.C: For any risk located in Singapore
options.D: For reinsurance, for risks outside Singapore, or with MAS permission for an exceptional risk

explanation: The only exceptions are reinsurance, risks outside Singapore and MAS-permitted exceptional risks that cannot be placed with licensed insurers. Price advantage or client consent does not authorise placement with unlicensed insurers.

stem: The main purpose of the Section 42 prohibition on negotiating or placing contracts with unlicensed insurers is to:

options.A: Increase premium income for local insurers
options.B: Reduce paperwork for MAS
options.C: Protect policy owners from dealing with insurers outside MAS supervision
options.D: Encourage advisers to sell only life policies

explanation: The prohibition protects policy owners by keeping insurance placements within the regulated, supervised sector. It is a consumer protection measure, not a revenue or administrative one.

stem: What is the maximum penalty under Section 43 for false or misleading representations concerning insurance proposals or claims?

options.A: A fine up to S$50,000 or 2 years imprisonment
options.B: A fine up to S$25,000 or imprisonment up to 12 months or both
options.C: A fine up to S$12,500 only
options.D: A fine up to S$100,000

explanation: The Section 43 offence carries a fine up to S$25,000 or up to 12 months imprisonment or both - lower than the Section 35 penalty for false statements in advisory services generally.

stem: A licensed financial adviser sends clients a circular recommending a Specified Product in which it holds an interest. Under Section 45 it must:

options.A: Include a concise statement of the nature of that interest in the circular
options.B: Refrain from sending the circular at all
options.C: Obtain MAS approval before sending the circular
options.D: Send the circular only to accredited investors

explanation: The adviser may make the recommendation but must disclose in the circular a concise statement of its interest (and those of associated persons). No MAS pre-approval or investor restriction applies.

stem: Which person has a defence to a Section 45 charge concerning a circular?

options.A: The author who forgot about his shareholding
options.B: The research head who approved the circular
options.C: A director who signed off on the recommendation
options.D: A person who merely distributed the circular in the ordinary course of business without knowledge of the non-disclosure

explanation: Section 45(2) protects those who only distribute the document in the ordinary course of business without knowledge. Authors and approvers who held undisclosed interests cannot rely on it.

stem: Under Regulation 20A, changes to interests in Listed Specified Products must be entered in the register within how many days, and entries retained for how long?

options.A: 14 days; 3 years
options.B: 30 days; 7 years
options.C: 7 days; 5 years
options.D: 7 days; 3 years

explanation: Particulars of changes must be entered within 7 days and each entry kept for 5 years. Confusing these with the 14-day misconduct reporting or other retention periods is a common error.

stem: Where must a representative who is an individual keep his register of interests in Listed Specified Products?

options.A: At his principal place of business, with a copy kept in Singapore where required
options.B: Deposited with MAS
options.C: At the Singapore Exchange
options.D: With his personal bank

explanation: An individual keeps the register at his principal place of business; a corporation keeps it at a place of business in Singapore. It may be electronic provided MAS has full access - it is not lodged with MAS or the SGX.

stem: A licensed financial adviser has already granted an unsecured loan of S$2,000 to a representative. What further unsecured credit may it extend to him under Regulation 18?

options.A: Up to S$3,000 more
options.B: Any amount, if his supervisor guarantees it
options.C: Nothing further under any circumstances
options.D: Up to S$1,000 more, keeping the aggregate within S$3,000

explanation: Unsecured loans and credit facilities are capped at S$3,000 in aggregate per person. With S$2,000 outstanding, only another S$1,000 may be extended; a guarantee from a supervisor is not security for this purpose.

stem: For the Regulation 18 unsecured loan cap, a loan to a director who is not an employee includes:

options.A: Only loans documented in the director's own name
options.B: Loans made to the director's family members
options.C: Only loans exceeding one year in tenor
options.D: Only interest-free loans

explanation: Loans to a director's family members are treated as loans to the director, preventing circumvention of the S$3,000 aggregate cap through relatives.

stem: Before appointing a new chief executive officer, a licensed financial adviser must:

options.A: Notify MAS within 14 days after the appointment
options.B: Publish the appointment in the Gazette
options.C: Obtain the prior approval of MAS, applying via Form 11
options.D: Obtain shareholder approval only

explanation: Section 63(1) requires prior MAS approval for the appointment of a CEO or director, sought via Form 11 and assessed against Regulation 13(2) criteria. Post-appointment notification is not sufficient.

stem: A firm knowingly employs an individual who is subject to an MAS prohibition order. Under Section 69(2) the firm faces:

options.A: No liability, since the order binds only the individual
options.B: A written caution
options.C: A fine up to S$25,000
options.D: A fine up to S$50,000

explanation: Employing a person known to be under a prohibition order is itself an offence with a fine up to S$50,000. The order's effect is not confined to the prohibited individual.

stem: A person aggrieved by an MAS prohibition order may:

options.A: Appeal to the Minister within 30 days
options.B: Apply for judicial review within 7 days
options.C: Ignore the order pending review
options.D: Appeal to the Monetary Authority's board of directors

explanation: The appeal lies to the Minister within 30 days of the decision. The order remains effective in the meantime, and there is no internal board appeal route.

stem: Under Section 112(1), an officer of a licensed financial adviser who fails to take all reasonable steps to secure the company's compliance faces:

options.A: A fine up to S$25,000 only
options.B: Disqualification for 6 months only
options.C: A fine up to S$100,000 or imprisonment up to 2 years
options.D: No personal liability

explanation: Officers who fail to secure compliance are personally liable to a fine up to S$100,000 or imprisonment up to 2 years - the same maximum as for falsification of records.

stem: When a corporation commits an offence under the FAA, which officers may also be prosecuted under Section 111?

options.A: None - only the corporation is liable
options.B: Officers who consented to, connived in, or were negligent in relation to the offence
options.C: Only the company secretary
options.D: All shareholders holding more than 5 percent

explanation: Personal liability attaches to officers whose consent, connivance or neglect contributed to the corporate offence. Shareholding alone does not create liability.

stem: When did FAA-N16, the Notice on Recommendations on Investment Products, take effect?

options.A: 1 January 2012
options.B: 1 March 2006
options.C: 1 April 2024
options.D: 8 October 2018

explanation: FAA-N16 took effect on 1 January 2012. The other dates belong to FAA-N11 on dual currency investments, FAA-N26 on competency, and the overseas-listed product risk warning requirement.

stem: A corporate client wishes to purchase an unlisted Specified Investment Product. What does FAA-N16 require by way of a Customer Knowledge Assessment?

options.A: A CKA must be conducted on the company's authorised signatory
options.B: No CKA is required, because for CKA purposes a client means a natural person only
options.C: A CKA must be conducted on every director of the company
options.D: A CKA is required but the company may waive it in writing

explanation: For CKA and CAR purposes, client is defined as a natural person only. Corporate clients fall outside the assessment requirement entirely, so there is nothing to conduct or waive.

stem: Which of the following on its own satisfies the knowledge or experience test in a Customer Knowledge Assessment?

options.A: At least 1 year of relevant working experience in the past 10 years
options.B: A pass in any two CMFAS modules
options.C: At least 6 transactions in unlisted SIPs in the preceding 3 years
options.D: At least 3 transactions in unlisted SIPs in the preceding 6 years

explanation: The transaction route requires at least 6 transactions in unlisted SIPs within the preceding 3 years. The working experience route requires at least 3 consecutive years in the past 10 years, and CMFAS passes are not one of the four qualifying routes.

stem: Rachel has no finance diploma and has never transacted in an unlisted SIP, but she worked as an investment analyst for 4 consecutive years, ending 5 years ago. What is her CKA outcome?

options.A: She passes only if she also completes 6 transactions
options.B: She fails, because the experience must be current
options.C: She fails, because 4 years is short of the 5-year requirement
options.D: She passes, having at least 3 consecutive years of relevant working experience in the past 10 years

explanation: The working experience route needs at least 3 consecutive years of relevant experience within the past 10 years. Four years ending 5 years ago sits inside that window, and the routes are alternatives rather than cumulative requirements.

stem: How long does a Customer Knowledge Assessment outcome remain valid?

options.A: 1 year
options.B: 3 years
options.C: 6 months
options.D: 5 years

explanation: A CKA outcome is valid for 1 year from the assessment. The 3-year period applies to the Customer Account Review, and 5 years is a common record retention period rather than a validity period.

stem: A client passed his Customer Account Review two years ago and has transacted in listed SIPs several times since. What is the position on his CAR?

options.A: It expired after 1 year and must be redone
options.B: It remains valid, and continues where he transacts in listed SIPs at least once in each subsequent 3-year period
options.C: It must be refreshed every time he places a trade
options.D: It lapsed the moment he transacted, and a CKA is now required instead

explanation: A CAR outcome is valid for 3 years and continues to apply where the client transacts in listed SIPs at least once in each subsequent 3-year period. The 1-year validity belongs to the CKA.

stem: Which assessment must be conducted before a client opens an account to trade listed Specified Investment Products?

options.A: Fit and Proper assessment
options.B: Balanced scorecard review
options.C: Customer Account Review
options.D: Customer Knowledge Assessment

explanation: The Customer Account Review is the assessment for listed SIPs and is done before the account is opened. The Customer Knowledge Assessment applies to unlisted SIPs, and the other two are not client assessments at all.

stem: A client is assessed as not having the relevant knowledge or experience but still wants to buy the unlisted SIP. What must the financial adviser do?

options.A: Refer the client to another financial adviser
options.B: Proceed on an execution-only basis once the client signs a waiver
options.C: Decline the transaction in all circumstances
options.D: Inform the client of the outcome, offer to provide advice, and obtain senior management approval before proceeding

explanation: The adviser must tell the client the outcome and offer advice. If the client still wishes to proceed, approval from senior management, or a designated person acting under a board-approved written framework, is required, and the trade cannot be done execution-only.

stem: Why can a client who fails the CKA not simply sign a waiver and transact on an execution-only basis?

options.A: Because FAA-N16 requires an offer of advice and senior management approval, and rules out the execution-only route for such a client
options.B: Because the client must first complete 6 qualifying transactions
options.C: Because MAS must approve each such transaction individually
options.D: Because execution-only business is prohibited under the FAA

explanation: FAA-N16 closes the execution-only route for a client who fails the assessment. The safeguard is an offer of advice plus senior management approval, not a client waiver, and MAS does not approve individual transactions.

stem: A client refuses to provide the information needed for the Customer Knowledge Assessment. How must the financial adviser treat him?

options.A: As an accredited investor
options.B: As not possessing the relevant knowledge or experience
options.C: As exempt from the assessment
options.D: As possessing the relevant knowledge, since he declined to be assessed

explanation: Declining to provide the information produces a deemed fail. The client is treated as not having the relevant knowledge or experience, which triggers the offer of advice and senior management approval safeguards.

stem: Two spouses open a joint account to transact in unlisted SIPs. How is the CKA applied?

options.A: The couple is assessed as a single client
options.B: A pass by either spouse covers both
options.C: Each client is assessed individually
options.D: Only the primary account holder is assessed

explanation: For joint transactions each client is assessed individually. There is no concept of a combined assessment or of one holder's pass carrying the other.

stem: A client is switching from one investment product to another. What must the financial adviser specifically disclose?

options.A: The adviser's total commission for the year
options.B: Nothing beyond the usual first-purchase disclosures
options.C: Only the charges on the new product
options.D: Whether the switch is disadvantageous to the client, considering matters such as new charges incurred and benefits lost

explanation: Switching requires disclosure of whether the switch is disadvantageous, taking into account factors such as fresh charges and benefits given up. It is not treated like an ordinary first-time purchase.

stem: Under FAA-N16, what must be documented for every recommendation made to a client?

options.A: The basis for the recommendation, together with records of CKA and CAR outcomes
options.B: The representative's balanced scorecard grade at the time
options.C: Only the product name and the amount invested
options.D: Only the client's signature on the application form

explanation: The adviser must document the basis for each recommendation and keep records of the CKA and CAR outcomes. Transaction particulars and signatures alone do not evidence the reasoning behind the advice.

stem: A client transacts in an overseas-listed investment product for the first time. What is required of the intermediary?

options.A: Require the client to appoint an overseas custodian
options.B: Provide the prescribed risk warning statement and obtain the client's acknowledgement
options.C: Obtain MAS approval before executing the trade
options.D: Conduct a fresh CKA for each overseas market

explanation: For a first transaction in an overseas-listed investment product on or after 8 October 2018, the intermediary must give the prescribed risk warning statement and obtain the client's acknowledgement.

stem: For how long must the acknowledgement of the overseas-listed investment product risk warning be kept?

options.A: Not less than 1 year
options.B: Not less than 3 years
options.C: Not less than 5 years
options.D: Not less than 7 years

explanation: The acknowledgement must be retained for not less than 5 years, which matches the general record keeping standard applied across the FAA regime.

stem: A financial adviser contravenes a MAS Notice such as FAA-N16. Under Section 58(5) of the FAA, what is the penalty?

options.A: A fine not exceeding S$50,000 or imprisonment up to 12 months
options.B: Immediate revocation of the licence
options.C: A fine not exceeding S$100,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years
options.D: A fine not exceeding S$25,000, and up to S$2,500 for every day the offence continues after conviction

explanation: Section 58(5) provides for a fine not exceeding S$25,000, with a further fine of up to S$2,500 for each day a continuing offence persists after conviction. No imprisonment term attaches to breach of a Notice.

stem: A financial adviser is convicted of breaching a MAS Notice and continues the contravening conduct for a further 10 days. What is the maximum additional fine for the continuing offence?

options.C: There is no additional fine once convicted

explanation: The daily continuing fine is up to S$2,500, so 10 days gives a maximum of 10 x S$2,500 = S$25,000. This sits on top of the original fine of up to S$25,000.

stem: How often must disclosure documents be reviewed under FAA-N03?

options.A: At least once every 3 years
options.B: At least annually
options.C: Only when MAS requests a review
options.D: Only when a product feature changes

explanation: FAA-N03 requires disclosure documents to be reviewed at least once a year. Reviewing only on a product change or on request would leave stale information in circulation.

stem: Which of the following must a financial adviser disclose about itself under FAA-N03?

options.A: Its audited financial statements
options.B: Only its licence number
options.C: Its name, the services it offers, the products it advises on, any unregulated activities, and its product providers
options.D: Only the names of its representatives

explanation: FAA-N03 requires disclosure of the adviser's identity, the scope of its services and products, any activities not regulated under the FAA, and the product providers it deals with.

stem: For a life policy, what satisfies the remuneration disclosure requirement under FAA-N03?

options.A: A separate written commission statement signed by the client
options.B: An annual statement of the representative's total earnings
options.C: No disclosure is required for life policies
options.D: Disclosure of the distribution cost in the policy illustration

explanation: For a life policy, showing the distribution cost in the policy illustration is sufficient. A separate commission statement is not required, but some disclosure is.

stem: Which of these is NOT among the product disclosures required for a designated investment product under FAA-N03?

options.A: The historical trading volume of the product provider's shares
options.B: The fees and charges payable
options.C: The benefits and risks of the product
options.D: The free-look or cancellation period

explanation: Required disclosures cover the nature and provider of the product, the client profile it suits, benefits and risks, pricing basis, fees and charges, reports the client will receive, the free-look or cancellation period, and warnings. The provider's own share trading volume is not part of the list.

stem: A representative wants to market a fund by quoting a 'targeted return of 6 percent per annum'. Is this permitted under FAA-N03?

options.A: Yes, if the target is based on the manager's internal modelling
options.B: No, because predictions or forecasts using terms such as targeted or expected returns are prohibited
options.C: Yes, if the client signs an acknowledgement of the risk
options.D: Yes, provided the word targeted is used rather than guaranteed

explanation: FAA-N03 prohibits predictions or forecasts of future performance, and expressly catches language such as targeted or expected returns. Labelling a projection carefully does not make it permissible.

stem: How must past performance be presented under FAA-N03?

options.A: Over at least 6 months, using simulated data where actual data is unavailable
options.B: Over any period chosen by the adviser, on a bid-to-bid basis
options.C: Over at least 1 year ending not earlier than 3 months before use, on an offer-to-bid basis with dividends reinvested
options.D: Over at least 5 years, excluding dividends

explanation: Past performance must cover at least 1 year ending not earlier than 3 months before use, be computed offer-to-bid with dividends reinvested, and use average annual compounded returns for periods over 1 year. Simulated or hypothetical performance is not allowed.

stem: A feeder fund wishes to show the track record of its underlying fund. What conditions apply?

options.A: The underlying fund's track record must be at least 3 years, with at least 50 percent invested in it
options.B: Underlying fund performance may never be shown
options.C: Any track record may be shown if labelled as the underlying fund's
options.D: The underlying fund's track record must be at least 1 year, with at least 90 percent invested in it

explanation: The underlying fund must have a track record of at least 1 year and at least 90 percent of the feeder's assets must be invested in it before its performance may be used.

stem: To which of these clients does FAA-N11 on dual currency investments NOT apply?

options.A: An accredited investor
options.B: A client who has passed the CKA
options.C: A client aged over 62
options.D: A retail client with 20 years of trading experience

explanation: FAA-N11 does not apply in respect of accredited investors, expert investors and institutional investors. Retail clients remain covered regardless of experience, age, or CKA outcome.

stem: When did FAA-N11, the Notice on Dual Currency Investments, take effect?

options.A: 1 January 2012
options.B: 1 March 2006
options.C: 1 April 2024
options.D: 1 January 2011

explanation: FAA-N11 took effect on 1 March 2006. The other dates correspond to FAA-N14 on reporting of misconduct, FAA-N16 on recommendations, and FAA-N26 on competency.

stem: How must a dual currency investment NOT be described?

options.A: As an investment product
options.B: As carrying currency risk
options.C: As a deposit or a structured deposit
options.D: As having an enhanced yield

explanation: FAA-N11 prohibits describing a DCI using the terms deposit or structured deposit, because the label would imply capital safety that the product does not have.

stem: What is the correct explanation of the enhanced interest a client earns on a dual currency investment?

options.A: It is a government subsidy on foreign currency holdings
options.B: It is guaranteed additional interest with no associated risk
options.C: It is a bonus paid by the bank for maintaining a minimum balance
options.D: It is the premium the client receives for the currency option embedded in the product

explanation: A DCI embeds a currency option written by the client, and the enhanced yield is the option premium. The adviser must explain this and illustrate scenarios where currency movements cause a loss, rather than presenting the yield as risk-free interest.

stem: Under FAA-N02, which person is disqualified from acting as an introducer?

options.A: A person whose sole business or full-time occupation is introducing clients
options.B: An employee of the financial adviser
options.C: A person who is remunerated for referrals
options.D: A part-time property agent who occasionally refers clients

explanation: Introducing must not be the introducer's sole business or full-time occupation. Part-time referrers, employees and paid introducers are all permitted, subject to the other conditions.

stem: What must a financial adviser put in place before using an introducer?

options.A: A performance bond lodged by the introducer
options.B: A written agreement with the introducer, and a script for use with clients
options.C: MAS approval of the introducer
options.D: A CMFAS pass for the introducer

explanation: FAA-N02 requires a written agreement with the introducer and the provision of a script to be used with clients. Introducers are not licensed or examined, since they do not advise.

stem: An introducer is asked by a prospective client whether a particular unit trust is suitable for retirement. What may the introducer do?

options.A: Give a general view, provided he does not recommend a specific fund
options.B: Explain the fund's risk rating from the fact sheet
options.C: Confine himself to the referral and the approved script, and refer the question to the financial adviser
options.D: Answer freely, since the client asked the question

explanation: An introducer must not give advice on investment products. Any discussion of suitability crosses into advising, so the question must be passed to the financial adviser.

stem: What must an introducer disclose to a client?

options.A: The financial adviser's total commission on the product
options.B: His own income for the preceding year
options.C: Only that he is an introducer
options.D: That he is an introducer, whether he is remunerated, and the amount of remuneration if the client asks

explanation: The introducer must disclose his status, whether he is remunerated for the referral, and the amount of that remuneration if the client asks for it.

stem: What details must a financial adviser maintain in its register of introducers?

options.A: Names, contact particulars, registration or identity numbers, and appointment and termination dates
options.B: Names and the total commissions paid to each
options.C: Names and the number of clients referred each quarter
options.D: Only the introducers' names

explanation: The register must record each introducer's name, contact particulars, registration or identity number, and the dates of appointment and termination.

stem: FAA-N10 applies to persons exempted under Regulation 27(1)(d). Which activity does that exemption cover?

options.A: Marketing collective investment schemes to the public
options.B: Advising not more than 30 accredited investors on investment products other than life policies
options.C: Advising an unlimited number of retail clients on life policies
options.D: Advising institutional investors on any product

explanation: Regulation 27(1)(d) exempts a person advising not more than 30 accredited investors on investment products other than life policies.

stem: Which statement may a Regulation 27(1)(d) exempt person make about its standing with MAS?

options.A: That it is supervised by MAS
options.B: That it is registered with MAS
options.C: None of these representations may be made
options.D: That it is regulated by MAS

explanation: FAA-N10 prohibits such persons and their representatives from representing that they are licensed, regulated, supervised or registered by MAS. All four descriptions are off limits.

stem: Which of the following is an entry requirement for a provisional representative under FAA-N12?

options.A: A pass in all CMFAS modules before arrival in Singapore
options.B: Singapore citizenship or permanent residence
options.C: At least 5 years of relevant working experience
options.D: At least 3 years of relevant working experience and a Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional qualification

explanation: A provisional representative must be at least 21, be relocating or have relocated to Singapore, have at least 3 years of relevant working experience, and hold a Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional qualification.

stem: For how long is provisional representative status valid, and what is the position on prior overseas licensing?

options.A: Up to 3 months, with overseas licensing continuous for 12 months and ceased not more than 12 months earlier
options.B: Up to 6 months, with overseas licensing continuous for 6 months
options.C: Up to 12 months, with no overseas licensing requirement
options.D: Up to 3 years, with overseas licensing continuous for 3 years

explanation: The status lasts up to 3 months. The individual's overseas licensing must have been continuous for 12 months and must have ceased not more than 12 months before.

stem: Which of the following is NOT reportable misconduct under FAA-N14?

options.A: Failure to satisfy the Guidelines on Fit and Proper Criteria
options.B: Failure to meet continuing education requirements
options.C: Acts involving fraud or dishonesty
options.D: Inappropriate advice, misrepresentation or inadequate disclosure

explanation: FAA-N14 covers fraud or dishonesty, inappropriate advice or misrepresentation or inadequate disclosure, failure to satisfy fit and proper criteria, and other misconduct. A shortfall in continuing education is not reportable misconduct.

stem: A representative is found to have misappropriated a client's premium payment. Beyond reporting to MAS, what else is required?

options.A: The representative must be given 14 days to make restitution before any report
options.B: Nothing further, as the MAS report discharges the obligation
options.C: A police report must be lodged, because the act involves fraud or dishonesty
options.D: The client must be asked to sign a settlement agreement

explanation: For misconduct involving fraud or dishonesty, a police report must be lodged in addition to the report to MAS. Restitution or settlement does not displace either obligation.

stem: Within what period must a financial adviser lodge a misconduct report with MAS under FAA-N14?

options.A: Within 14 days of completing the internal investigation
options.B: Within 30 days of the end of the quarter
options.C: Within 7 days of discovery of the misconduct
options.D: Within 14 days of discovery of the misconduct

explanation: The report is due within 14 days of discovery of the misconduct. The clock starts at discovery, not at the conclusion of any internal investigation.

stem: A financial adviser has no misconduct to report for the year. What must it do?

options.A: Submit a nil annual declaration not later than 14 days after 31 December
options.B: Submit a nil declaration within 30 days of its financial year end
options.C: Notify MAS only if MAS asks
options.D: Nothing, since there is nothing to report

explanation: Where there is no misconduct to report, a nil annual declaration must be submitted not later than 14 days after 31 December each year.

stem: Which arrangement for the Independent Sales Audit Unit is NOT permitted under FAA-N20?

options.A: Using the internal audit or risk management function
options.B: Placing the unit within the sales function under a senior sales manager
options.C: Outsourcing the checks to an external party
options.D: Using the compliance function to perform the checks

explanation: The ISA Unit must be independent of sales. It may sit in compliance, internal audit or risk management, or be outsourced, but it cannot be part of or report to the sales function.

stem: How often and to whom does the Independent Sales Audit Unit report its findings?

options.A: Monthly to the head of sales
options.B: Only when a Category 1 infraction is found
options.C: Quarterly to the board and CEO, or an independent unit, by the end of the two calendar quarters after the measurement quarter
options.D: Annually to MAS only

explanation: ISA Unit findings go quarterly to the board and CEO, or to an independent unit, by the end of the two calendar quarters following the measurement quarter.

stem: A representative is remunerated solely by variable income. What proportion of his variable income from sales in the measurement quarter is subject to the balanced scorecard?

options.A: 75 percent
options.B: 100 percent
options.C: 40 percent
options.D: 60 percent

explanation: For a representative on variable income only, 60 percent of the variable income from sales in the measurement quarter is the specified variable income. Representatives on fixed plus variable pay have all of their variable income measured.

stem: A representative earns a fixed salary plus commission. She earned S$40,000 in commission in the measurement quarter. What is her specified variable income?
explanation: Where a representative is on fixed plus variable remuneration, all of the variable income is measured, so the full S$40,000 is the specified variable income. The 60 percent reduction applies only to variable-income-only representatives.

stem: A representative's measured income from the first quarter is paid out in instalments over the following year. How is the deferred portion treated?

options.A: It is re-measured in the quarter it is paid
options.B: It is measured only once, so deferred payments of measured income are not re-measured
options.C: It is measured at half weighting when paid
options.D: It falls outside the framework entirely

explanation: Income is measured once. Deferred payments of income that has already been measured are not measured again, which prevents the same earnings being scored twice.

stem: A representative advises only on rollovers of dual currency investments. What form do his post-transaction checks take?

options.A: No checks are required for rollovers
options.B: Documentation review and client surveys
options.C: Call-log reviews
options.D: Mystery shopping only

explanation: Post-transaction checks for representatives who only advise on rollovers of dual currency investments or structured notes are call-log reviews. Documentation review plus client surveys apply to other representatives.

stem: By when must post-transaction checks on sampled transactions be completed, and how many rounds are contemplated?

options.A: By the end of the measurement quarter itself, with up to 2 rounds
options.B: Within 14 days of each transaction, with a single round
options.C: By the end of the financial year, with unlimited rounds
options.D: By the end of the calendar quarter after the measurement quarter, with up to 3 rounds

explanation: Checks must be completed by the end of the calendar quarter following the measurement quarter, and the framework contemplates up to 3 rounds of checks.

stem: What makes a representative a 'selected representative' for sampling purposes under FAA-N20?

options.A: Being graded B or worse for two consecutive quarters
options.B: Any Category 2 infraction in the quarter
options.C: Being newly appointed within the past 3 months
options.D: Any single quarter graded B or worse

explanation: A selected representative is one graded B or worse for two consecutive quarters. That status raises round 1 sampling to at least 10 percent of his transactions.

stem: An ordinary representative who is not a selected representative and does not deal only in DCI rollovers had 60 transactions in the measurement quarter. What is the minimum round 1 sample?

options.A: 2 transactions
options.B: 3 transactions
options.C: 6 transactions
options.D: 1 transaction

explanation: The round 1 sampling rate for such a representative is 5 percent, so 5 percent of 60 = 3 transactions, comfortably above the minimum of one transaction.

stem: A financial adviser wishes to change from basing its sampling population on historical average to actual transaction count. What must it do?

options.A: Wait until the start of the next financial year
options.B: Nothing, as the choice is entirely at its discretion
options.C: Give MAS 7 days written notice of the change
options.D: Obtain MAS approval before the change

explanation: A change of method requires 7 days written notice to MAS. Actual transaction count is mandatory for representatives appointed for less than 3 months or with no transactions in the past 12 months.

stem: Which of the following is a Category 1 infraction?

options.A: An incomplete file note that was later corrected
options.B: A minor typographical error in a client's contact details
options.C: A late filing of an internal report
options.D: A clearly unsuitable recommendation causing material impact on the client

explanation: Category 1 infractions have a material impact on the client's interests or impinge on fitness and propriety, and include clearly unsuitable recommendations, detrimental switching, failure to disclose decisive information, misrepresentation and gross negligence. Administrative lapses are Category 2 or may be disregarded as minor.

stem: A single case is found to contain four separate infractions. How is it counted for grading?

options.A: As one case, regardless of the number of infractions in it
options.B: As two cases, since infractions are paired
options.C: As one case per client affected
options.D: As four cases

explanation: A case is counted once regardless of how many infractions it contains. Grading is based on cases, not on a tally of individual breaches.

stem: A representative has one Category 1 case in the measurement quarter, and only 2 percent of his cases contain infractions. What grade does he receive?

options.A: Grade C
options.B: Grade E
options.C: Grade A
options.D: Grade B

explanation: Any Category 1 case results in grade E regardless of the percentage of cases with infractions. The percentage route cannot rescue the grade.

stem: A representative has 3 Category 2 cases, representing 25 percent of his sampled cases. What grade applies?

options.A: Grade E
options.B: Grade B
options.C: Grade C
options.D: Grade D

explanation: Grades are assigned by percentage or by absolute number of Category 2 cases, whichever gives the better grade. The 25 percent figure points to grade D, but 3 Category 2 cases points to grade C, so grade C applies.

stem: What is the specified variable income entitlement for a representative graded D?

options.A: 100 percent
options.B: 75 to below 100 percent
options.C: 50 to below 75 percent
options.D: 25 to below 50 percent

explanation: Grade D carries an entitlement of 25 to below 50 percent. Grade A is 100 percent, grade B is 75 to below 100 percent, grade C is 50 to below 75 percent, and grade E is 0 to below 25 percent.

stem: By when must specified variable income that a representative is not entitled to be recovered?

options.A: By the end of the 2 calendar quarters after the measurement quarter
options.B: Within 14 days of the grading
options.C: By the end of the following financial year
options.D: By the end of the measurement quarter

explanation: Recovery must be made by the end of the 2 calendar quarters after the measurement quarter, except where the representative is in financial difficulty.

stem: A substantiated complaint relates to a sale made in an earlier quarter. How does it affect the representative's specified variable income?

options.A: The full current quarter income is forfeited
options.B: The unentitled amount is prorated by the proportion of specified variable income earned in the past quarter
options.C: It is carried forward and applied to the next year's income
options.D: It is disregarded because the sale was in a past quarter

explanation: For incidents from past quarters the unentitled amount is prorated by the proportion of the specified variable income earned in that past quarter. Substantiated complaints and mystery shopping results for incidents on or after 1 January 2016 count as cases.

stem: How is a supervisor's entitlement to specified variable income determined under the balanced scorecard framework?

options.A: By his own sales performance only
options.B: By the average tenure of the representatives he supervises
options.C: It mirrors the percentage entitlements of the representatives he supervises
options.D: It is fixed at 100 percent unless MAS directs otherwise

explanation: A supervisor's entitlement mirrors the percentage entitlements of the representatives under his supervision, which aligns his pay with the quality of their sales conduct.

stem: Which set of grades applies to supervisors under the balanced scorecard framework?

options.A: Pass and Fail
options.B: Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3
options.C: A, B, C, D and E
options.D: Good, Satisfactory, Fair and Unsatisfactory

explanation: Supervisors are graded Good at 75 to 100 percent, Satisfactory at 50 to below 75 percent, Fair at 25 to below 50 percent, and Unsatisfactory below 25 percent. Letter grades A to E are used for representatives.

stem: How long must balanced scorecard framework records be kept, and when must performance records be given out?

options.A: At least 5 years, with records issued to each representative and supervisor within two quarters after the measurement quarter
options.B: At least 3 years, with records issued annually
options.C: At least 7 years, with records issued on request
options.D: At least 1 year, with records issued at the next appraisal

explanation: BSF records must be kept for at least 5 years, and each representative and supervisor must receive a balanced scorecard performance record within two quarters after the measurement quarter.

stem: When did FAA-N26, the Notice on Competency Requirements, take effect, and which notice did it cancel?

options.A: 1 March 2006, cancelling FAA-N11
options.B: 1 April 2024, cancelling FAA-N13
options.C: 1 January 2012, cancelling FAA-N16
options.D: 1 January 2011, cancelling FAA-N14

explanation: FAA-N26 took effect on 1 April 2024 and cancelled the earlier competency notice FAA-N13.

stem: Which academic qualification satisfies the entry requirement for an appointed representative under FAA-N26?

options.A: A pass in RES5 alone
options.B: Four GCE O Level passes
options.C: A GCE A Level certificate with three H2 and two H1 passes
options.D: Completion of secondary education in any form

explanation: The minimum academic requirement is a GCE A Level certificate with three H2 and two H1 passes, an International Baccalaureate Diploma, a polytechnic diploma, or an equivalent qualification. Examination passes are a separate requirement.

stem: An individual passed RES5 but did not commence as an appointed representative. When does the pass lapse?

options.A: It never lapses
options.B: After 1 year
options.C: After 2 years
options.D: After 3 years

explanation: A pass in RES5 lapses if the individual does not commence as an appointed representative within 3 years of passing, or ceases and does not recommence within 3 years.

stem: What are the annual CPD requirements for an appointed representative advising on life policies?

options.A: 6 Core CPD hours plus 24 Supplementary CPD hours
options.B: 24 Core CPD hours plus 6 Supplementary CPD hours
options.C: 30 hours of product training
options.D: 10 hours in total

explanation: Each calendar year requires 6 Core CPD hours in ethics or rules and regulations, plus 24 Supplementary CPD hours. The Supplementary requirement drops to 10 hours for representatives advising only on mortgage reducing term assurance or group term life policies.

stem: A representative is appointed for 219 days of a calendar year, which is not his first year of appointment. What is his pro-rated Supplementary CPD requirement, given a full-year requirement of 24 hours?

options.A: 12.0 hours
options.B: 14.4 hours
options.C: 18.0 hours
options.D: 24.0 hours

explanation: Supplementary CPD is pro-rated by days appointed over 365. That gives 219 / 365 = 0.6, and 0.6 x 24 = 14.4 hours. The exemption for a partial year applies only to the first calendar year of first appointment.

stem: Under which provision is FAA-N06 on AML and CFT issued, and who falls outside its scope?

options.A: Section 27B of the MAS Act; advisers that only issue or promulgate research analyses or research reports are excluded
options.B: Section 58 of the FAA; all insurance brokers are excluded
options.C: Section 321 of the SFA; all exempt persons are excluded
options.D: Section 29(1) of the FSM Act; all licensed financial advisers are excluded

explanation: FAA-N06 is issued under Section 27B of the MAS Act. It applies to licensed financial advisers, registered insurance brokers exempt from FA licensing, and Regulation 27(1)(d) exempt persons, but not to advisers whose only advisory activity is issuing research analyses or reports.

stem: Which of the following is one of the three underlying principles of FAA-N06?

options.A: Maximising customer confidentiality above all other duties
options.B: Assisting and cooperating with Singapore law enforcement authorities to the fullest extent possible
options.C: Reporting only transactions above a prescribed monetary threshold
options.D: Delegating all AML responsibilities to a third party service provider

explanation: The three principles are exercising due diligence on customers and connected parties, conducting business in conformity with high ethical standards while guarding against money laundering and terrorism financing, and assisting and cooperating fully with law enforcement. Confidentiality does not override these obligations.

stem: Which of the following must a financial adviser assess under the risk-based approach in FAA-N06?

options.A: Only the profile of each individual customer
options.B: Only the products it distributes
options.C: Its customers, the countries its customers are from or in, the countries it operates in, and its products, services, transactions and delivery channels
options.D: Only the countries subject to FATF countermeasures

explanation: The risk assessment must span customers, geographies both of the customers and of the adviser's operations, and products, services, transactions and delivery channels.

stem: What are the requirements for a financial adviser's money laundering risk assessment?

options.A: It must be submitted to MAS for approval before use
options.B: It must be refreshed only when the business model changes
options.C: It may be informal, as long as senior management is briefed verbally
options.D: It must be documented, kept up to date, and made available to MAS

explanation: Risk assessments must be documented, kept current and available to MAS. Mitigation policies require senior management approval, with enhanced measures where risks are higher. MAS does not pre-approve the assessment.

stem: When must a financial adviser assess the money laundering risks of a new product or delivery technology?

options.A: Before its launch or use
options.B: Within 30 days of launch
options.C: At the next annual review
options.D: Only if a customer complains

explanation: The assessment must be made before the new product, business practice, delivery mechanism or technology is launched or used, with special attention to features that favour anonymity.

stem: A prospective customer's circumstances arouse suspicion of money laundering before any business relationship is established. What must the financial adviser do?

options.A: Establish the relationship and review it after 6 months
options.B: Not establish relations or undertake the transaction, and file an STR with a copy to MAS
options.C: Ask the customer to provide a written declaration of the source of funds
options.D: Establish the relationship but apply enhanced monitoring

explanation: Where suspicion exists before relations are established, the adviser must decline the business and file a suspicious transaction report, copied to MAS. Proceeding with monitoring is not an available course.

stem: Which of the following triggers customer due diligence under FAA-N06?

options.A: Only transactions above S$20,000
options.B: Only the annual review of a customer file
options.C: Establishing business relations, suspicion of money laundering or terrorism financing, or doubts about the veracity or adequacy of information previously obtained
options.D: Only the opening of a new account

explanation: CDD is required when establishing business relations, where there is suspicion, or where the adviser doubts the truthfulness or sufficiency of information already held. Anonymous or fictitious accounts may never be opened or maintained.

stem: Which particulars must a financial adviser obtain as part of customer identification?

options.A: Name and contact number only
options.B: Name, address and estimated annual income
options.C: Name, identification number and a credit bureau report
options.D: Full name including aliases, unique identification number, residential or registered address, date of birth or incorporation, and nationality or place of incorporation

explanation: These are the minimum identification particulars, and identity must then be verified using reliable, independent source data. Income and credit data are not part of the identification set.

stem: Two individuals open a joint investment account. How is CDD applied?

options.A: To each holder, as if each were individually a customer
options.B: To the holder contributing the larger share of funds
options.C: To the account as a single customer
options.D: Only to the first-named holder

explanation: Joint account holders are each treated as customers, so CDD is performed on all of them rather than on a primary holder alone.

stem: Who is a beneficial owner for the purposes of FAA-N06?

options.A: The largest creditor of the customer
options.B: The natural person who ultimately owns or controls the customer, or on whose behalf the transaction is conducted
options.C: Any shareholder holding more than 5 percent of the customer
options.D: The person who signs the account opening form

explanation: A beneficial owner is the natural person with ultimate ownership or control, or on whose behalf a transaction is conducted. For legal persons the cascade runs from ultimate owners, to those with ultimate effective control, to persons with executive authority.

stem: A customer is a company listed on the SGX, so the adviser does not normally inquire into its beneficial owners. In which circumstance must it nonetheless do so?

options.A: Never, as listed entities are permanently exempt
options.B: Where the company changes its auditor
options.C: Where the adviser has doubts about the CDD information or suspects money laundering or terrorism financing
options.D: Where the company's share price falls sharply

explanation: The exemption from beneficial ownership inquiry for SGX-listed entities, certain listed foreign entities, and regulated financial institutions falls away where the adviser has doubts about the information or suspects money laundering or terrorism financing.

stem: For a customer that is a trust, whose identities must be established?

options.A: Only beneficiaries who have received a distribution
options.B: The trustees only
options.C: The settlor and the beneficiaries only
options.D: The settlor, trustees, protector, beneficiaries and controllers

explanation: For trusts the adviser must identify the settlor, the trustees, the protector, the beneficiaries and any controllers, since control and benefit can sit with any of them.

stem: When must verification of a customer's identity normally be completed?

options.A: Before establishing business relations
options.B: Within 30 days of the first transaction
options.C: At the first annual review
options.D: Before the customer's first withdrawal

explanation: Verification must be completed before business relations are established. It may be deferred only where essential to avoid interrupting normal business and where the risks can be effectively managed, with completion as soon as reasonably practicable.

stem: An existing customer refuses to provide documents needed to complete CDD. What must the financial adviser do?

options.A: Continue the relationship but apply enhanced ongoing monitoring
options.B: Not commence or continue business relations or undertake transactions, and consider filing an STR
options.C: Refer the customer to another financial adviser
options.D: Continue the relationship with transaction limits imposed

explanation: Where CDD cannot be completed, the adviser must not commence or continue the relationship or undertake transactions, and must consider filing a suspicious transaction report. Heightened monitoring is not a substitute.

stem: In which situation is simplified customer due diligence prohibited?

options.A: Where the customer is introduced by an existing client
options.B: Where the customer is a Singapore resident
options.C: Where the customer or beneficial owner is from a country subject to FATF countermeasures, or where money laundering is suspected
options.D: Where the customer invests less than S$10,000

explanation: Simplified CDD requires a documented low-risk analysis and is prohibited where the customer or beneficial owner is from a country subject to FATF countermeasures or known to have inadequate AML measures, or where money laundering or terrorism financing is suspected.

stem: Which of the following is a politically exposed person under FAA-N06?

options.A: Only a serving head of state
options.B: Any person holding a government job
options.C: Any person who has served in the armed forces
options.D: A person entrusted with prominent public functions, whether domestically, in a foreign country or in an international organisation, and their family members and close associates

explanation: The definition covers persons entrusted with prominent public functions domestically, in a foreign country, or in an international organisation, and extends to family members and close associates.

stem: What must a financial adviser do before establishing a relationship with a foreign politically exposed person?

options.A: Obtain senior management approval, establish source of wealth and source of funds, and apply enhanced ongoing monitoring
options.B: Apply a risk-based approach and document the decision
options.C: Obtain MAS approval for the relationship
options.D: Nothing beyond standard CDD if the customer is resident in Singapore

explanation: Enhanced CDD is mandatory for foreign PEPs, requiring senior management approval, establishment of source of wealth and funds, and enhanced ongoing monitoring. A risk-based approach may be taken for domestic PEPs, international organisation PEPs, and PEPs who have stepped down, unless the relationship is higher risk.

stem: A financial adviser relies on a regulated third party to perform CDD. Which element can it NOT delegate?

options.A: Collection of identification documents
options.B: Ongoing monitoring of business relations
options.C: Identification of beneficial owners
options.D: Verification of the customer's identity

explanation: Ongoing monitoring can never be outsourced. Reliance is permitted for CDD elements where the third party is supervised for FATF-consistent compliance and will provide the data without delay, but the adviser remains responsible for compliance.

stem: How long must CDD records and transaction records be kept under FAA-N06?

options.A: Both for 1 year after the relationship ends
options.B: CDD records for 3 years after termination and transaction records for 3 years after completion
options.C: CDD records for at least 5 years after termination of business relations, and transaction records for at least 5 years after completion of the transaction
options.D: CDD records for 7 years and transaction records for 5 years

explanation: Both retention periods are at least 5 years, running from termination of the business relationship for CDD records and from completion of the transaction for transaction records.

stem: A financial adviser detects a suspicious transaction of S$800. What is the reporting obligation?

options.A: An internal file note is sufficient for amounts under S$1,000
options.B: No report is needed as the amount is below the reporting threshold
options.C: A report to STRO is needed only if the transaction completes
options.D: The transaction must be reported promptly to STRO, with a copy to MAS, regardless of amount

explanation: Suspicious transactions, including attempted ones, must be reported promptly to the Suspicious Transaction Reporting Office regardless of the amount, with a copy to MAS. There is no minimum threshold.

stem: Performing further CDD on a customer would alert him that he is under suspicion. What does FAA-N06 permit?

options.A: Stopping the CDD process and filing a suspicious transaction report instead
options.B: Informing the customer that a report is being made
options.C: Closing the account without any report
options.D: Completing the CDD anyway, since the Notice requires it

explanation: Section 48 of the CDSA prohibits tipping-off. Where performing CDD would tip off the customer, the adviser may stop and file an STR instead.

stem: Which governance measures does FAA-N06 require of a financial adviser?

options.A: An annual AML certification issued by MAS
options.B: An AML compliance officer at management level, an independent audit function, screening of prospective employees and representatives, and regular staff training
options.C: An external AML consultant appointed annually
options.D: A board committee comprising only independent directors

explanation: The Notice requires a management-level AML and CFT compliance officer, an independent audit function, pre-employment screening of staff and representatives, and regular training. Personal data may be collected, used and disclosed for compliance without the individual's consent.

stem: What does FAA-N17 require a licensed financial adviser to report to MAS?

options.A: All staff resignations from the compliance function
options.B: All customer complaints received in a quarter
options.C: Suspicious activities and incidents of fraud that are material to its safety, soundness or reputation
options.D: All transactions above S$20,000

explanation: FAA-N17, issued under section 58 of the FAA 2001, requires reporting of suspicious activities and incidents of fraud that are material to the adviser's safety, soundness or reputation. This is in addition to, not instead of, filing STRs with STRO.

stem: Within what period must Form F1 be submitted to MAS under FAA-N17?

options.A: Not later than 14 days after the internal investigation concludes
options.B: Not later than 30 days after the end of the quarter
options.C: Not later than 1 working day after discovery
options.D: Not later than 5 working days after discovery

explanation: Form F1 must be submitted not later than 5 working days after discovering the suspicious activity or fraud incident. The clock runs from discovery, not from the completion of any investigation.

stem: A financial adviser discovers a material fraud on a Monday and completes its internal investigation three weeks later. When was the Form F1 due?

options.A: Within 5 working days of the Monday discovery
options.B: Within 5 working days of completing the investigation
options.C: Within 14 days of the Monday discovery
options.D: At the next quarterly reporting date

explanation: The 5-working-day period runs from discovery. Waiting for the investigation to conclude would breach the timeline by around three weeks.

stem: A financial adviser discovers a material incident of fraud. What does FAA-N17 expect beyond the Form F1 submission?

options.A: A press release describing the incident
options.B: A police report, with a copy submitted to MAS
options.C: Notification to all affected clients within 24 hours
options.D: Nothing further, as Form F1 covers all obligations
