explanation: The adviser is expected to lodge a police report and give MAS a copy, in addition to Form F1 and any STRs filed with STRO, CAD or the Police. The police report does not replace the Form F1.

stem: A financial adviser assesses a suspicious activity as not material to its safety, soundness or reputation and decides not to report it to MAS. What should it do?

options.A: Seek written confirmation from MAS that no report is needed
options.B: Report it anyway at the next annual return
options.C: Document the reasons for not reporting
options.D: Nothing, as no obligation arises

explanation: Where the adviser concludes the matter is not material and does not report, it should document the reasons for that decision. Non-materiality removes the report, not the record.

stem: Under FSM-N23, what is the limit on unscheduled downtime for a critical system?

options.A: Not more than 24 hours in total per calendar year
options.B: Not more than 1 hour per month
options.C: Not more than 4 hours per incident
options.D: Not more than 4 hours in total within any period of 12 months

explanation: The maximum unscheduled downtime for each critical system must not exceed a total of 4 hours within any 12-month period. It is a cumulative cap per system, not a per-incident allowance.

stem: Under which statutory provision is FSM-N23 on Technology Risk Management issued, and when did it take effect?

options.A: Section 29(1) of the FSM Act 2022, effective 10 May 2024
options.B: Section 321 of the SFA, effective 30 August 2019
options.C: Section 58 of the FAA 2001, effective 1 April 2024
options.D: Section 27B of the MAS Act, effective 1 January 2012

explanation: FSM-N23 is issued under section 29(1) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2022 and took effect on 10 May 2024, the same date as the Cyber Hygiene notice FSM-N24.

stem: What does FSM-N23 require in respect of the recovery time objective for a critical system?

options.A: The RTO is set at the adviser's discretion with no validation requirement
options.B: The RTO must not exceed 4 hours, and the ability to meet it must be validated and documented at least once every 12 months
options.C: The RTO must not exceed 24 hours, validated once at implementation
options.D: The RTO must not exceed 1 hour, validated monthly

explanation: The RTO of each critical system must not exceed 4 hours, and the adviser must validate and document that the RTO can be met at least annually. Setting the objective once is not enough.

stem: Under FSM-N23, how quickly must MAS be notified of a relevant system malfunction or IT security incident?

options.A: Within 14 days of discovery
options.B: At the next quarterly report
options.C: As soon as possible but not later than 1 hour after discovery
options.D: Within 5 working days of discovery

explanation: Notification must be as soon as possible and no later than 1 hour after discovery of the incident. A separate root cause and impact analysis report follows within 14 days.

stem: An IT security incident is discovered at 9am. By when must the root cause and impact analysis report be submitted to MAS?

options.A: Within 30 days of the incident discovery
options.B: By 10am the same day
options.C: Within 5 working days
options.D: Within 14 days of the incident discovery

explanation: The 1-hour deadline applies to the initial notification. The root cause and impact analysis report is due within 14 days of the incident discovery.

stem: Through which channels may direct purchase insurance products be distributed under FAA-N19?

options.A: Through a representative or customer service officer, or through an online direct channel
options.B: Only through licensed representatives
options.C: Only through an online direct channel
options.D: Through any channel the insurer chooses

explanation: FAA-N19 permits distribution through a representative or customer service officer, or through an online direct channel.

stem: A Tier 1 life insurer proposes to satisfy its minimum DPI distribution obligation using a mobile branch that visits neighbourhoods weekly. Is this acceptable?

options.A: Yes, provided it visits at least once a week
options.B: No, a mobile branch does not count as a branch for this purpose
options.C: Yes, if MAS is notified of the schedule
options.D: Yes, a mobile branch is treated as a branch

explanation: A Tier 1 life insurer must at a minimum offer DPI through a representative or customer service officer at its principal place of business or a branch, and a mobile branch does not count as a branch.

stem: Which alert must be given to a client purchasing a direct purchase insurance product?

options.A: That DPI is a form of savings deposit protected under the deposit insurance scheme
options.B: That all benefits under the policy are guaranteed
options.C: That DPI is not a savings account or deposit, and that premiums may not be recovered if the policy is terminated early
options.D: That the policy may be cancelled at any time with a full refund

explanation: Clients must be alerted that DPI is not a savings account or deposit, that premiums paid may not be recovered on early termination, that some benefits are not guaranteed, and that a 14-day free-look period applies.

stem: What is the free-look period that must be highlighted to a client buying a direct purchase insurance product?

options.A: 21 days
options.B: 30 days
options.C: 7 days
options.D: 14 days

explanation: FAA-N19 requires clients to be alerted to a 14-day free-look period for direct purchase insurance products.

stem: A customer service officer distributing DPI is asked to review the client's whole insurance portfolio and recommend changes. What is the position?

options.A: He must not provide any financial advisory service that is not solely incidental to the distribution of DPI
options.B: He may do so if the client signs a waiver
options.C: He may do so if he holds a CMFAS pass
options.D: He may do so, as DPI distribution includes advisory work

explanation: A customer service officer must not provide financial advisory services beyond what is solely incidental to distributing DPI. A portfolio review and recommendation goes well beyond that boundary.

stem: Under section 58(5) of the FAA, what fine may be imposed for failing to comply with a notice such as FAA-N19?

options.A: A fine not exceeding $25,000 with no daily continuing penalty
options.B: A fine not exceeding $25,000, plus up to $2,500 for each day a continuing offence persists after conviction
options.C: A fine not exceeding $2,500 only
options.D: A fine not exceeding $250,000

explanation: Section 58(5) provides for a fine of up to $25,000, with a further fine of up to $2,500 for every day the offence continues after conviction.

stem: When did the FAA-N19 Amendment 2019 take effect?

options.A: 1 April 2024
options.B: 1 January 2011
options.C: 30 August 2019

explanation: The FAA-N19 Amendment 2019 took effect on 30 August 2019. The 2024 dates belong to the FSM Act notices and the competency notice FAA-N26.

stem: Which of the following is one of the six practices mandated by FSM-N24 on Cyber Hygiene?

options.A: Storage of all data within Singapore
options.B: Annual penetration testing by an external firm
options.C: Encryption of all customer emails
options.D: Network perimeter defence

explanation: The six mandated practices are securing administrative accounts, applying security patches, having written security standards, network perimeter defence, malware protection, and multi-factor authentication.

stem: To which accounts does FSM-N24 require multi-factor authentication to be applied?

options.A: All administrative accounts of critical systems, and all accounts used to access customer information through the internet
options.B: All employee accounts of any kind
options.C: All administrative accounts of critical systems only
options.D: All accounts used to access customer information through the internet only

explanation: MFA is required both for administrative accounts of critical systems and for any account used to access customer information over the internet, not for administrative accounts alone.

stem: Under which provision is FSM-N24 on Cyber Hygiene issued?

options.A: Section 321 of the SFA
options.B: Section 29(1) of the FSM Act 2022
options.C: Section 58 of the FAA 2001
options.D: Section 27B of the MAS Act

explanation: FSM-N24 is issued under section 29(1) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2022 and took effect on 10 May 2024, alongside FSM-N23 on technology risk management.

stem: Which part of MAS Notice 307 on Investment-Linked Policies is mandatory?

options.A: Part I only
options.B: Part II only
options.C: Both parts are mandatory
options.D: Neither part, as the whole Notice is guidance

explanation: Part I of MAS 307 is mandatory. Part II sets out non-mandatory best practice standards. The Notice is issued under section 64(2) of the Insurance Act, took effect on 1 October 2011 and was last revised on 28 June 2021.

stem: How far in advance must an insurer notify MAS before launching a new ILP sub-fund?

options.A: At least 14 days
options.B: At least 21 days
options.C: At least 1 month
options.D: At least 7 days

explanation: MAS must be notified at least 21 days before a new ILP sub-fund is launched. The 1-month period applies to notifying policyholders of significant changes.

stem: An insurer intends to raise the annual management fee of an ILP sub-fund by 0.15 percent of NAV. What must it do?

options.A: Notify MAS 21 days before the change and say nothing to policyholders
options.B: Nothing, as the increase is below 0.2 percent
options.C: Notify policyholders no later than 1 month before the change takes effect
options.D: Notify policyholders within 1 month after the change takes effect

explanation: A fee increase of 0.1 percent or more of NAV is a significant change, so policyholders must be notified no later than 1 month before it takes effect. The same applies to changes in an underlying fund into which the sub-fund feeds 30 percent or more of its NAV.

stem: How must units in an ILP sub-fund be priced?

options.A: At the insurer's declared offer price plus a spread
options.B: At the average of bid and offer prices of the underlying assets
options.C: At historical cost adjusted for inflation
options.D: At the sub-fund's NAV divided by the number of units outstanding

explanation: Units must be priced at the sub-fund's net asset value divided by the number of units outstanding.

stem: A capital guaranteed ILP sub-fund reaches maturity. The guaranteed amount is $1.05 per unit and the NAV per unit is $1.18. At what price must units be redeemed?

options.B: The insurer may choose either figure

explanation: Units of a capital guaranteed sub-fund must be redeemed at maturity at the higher of the guaranteed amount and the NAV per unit, which here is $1.18.

stem: An insurer wishes to change from the first audit method to the second method for its ILP sub-funds. What is required?

options.A: No notification is required, as the choice is the insurer's
options.B: MAS must be notified before the first change to the second method
options.C: MAS must be notified within 30 days after the change
options.D: MAS approval must be obtained in writing

explanation: Notification to MAS is required before the first change to the second method, which is an audit of internal controls rather than of financial statements.

stem: By when must the inaugural audit under the second method be completed, and what is the minimum review period?

options.A: Within 30 days of the financial year end, with a review period of not less than 3 months
options.B: Within 12 months of the financial year end, with no minimum review period
options.C: Within 3 months of the financial year end, with a review period of not less than 12 months
options.D: Within 6 months of the financial year end, with a review period of not less than 6 months

explanation: The first audit under the second method must be completed within 3 months of the financial year end, and the review period must not be less than 12 months.

stem: An ILP sub-fund is terminated. When must the audit certificate be obtained and the copy sent to MAS?

options.A: Certificate within 6 months of termination; copy to MAS within 30 days of the termination date
options.B: Certificate within 12 months of termination; copy to MAS at the next annual return
options.C: Certificate within 3 months of termination; copy to MAS within 14 days of the audit's completion
options.D: Certificate within 6 months of termination; copy to MAS within 30 days of the audit's completion

explanation: The audit certificate must be obtained within 6 months of termination or maturity, with a copy to MAS within 30 days of the audit's completion. Records are retained for 5 years and a copy given to a policyholder within 30 days of request.

stem: For ILPs issued on or after 8 October 2021, which term must insurers use and which is prohibited?

options.A: Use a single 'premium charge'; the term 'premium allocation rate' is prohibited
options.B: Both terms may be used interchangeably
options.C: Neither term may be used in policy documents
options.D: Use 'premium allocation rate'; the term 'premium charge' is prohibited

explanation: Insurers must use a single premium charge and must not use the term premium allocation rate. The requirement applies to ILPs issued on or after 8 October 2021 rather than retrospectively to all in-force policies.

stem: How often must statements be sent for a specified ILP under MAS 307?

options.A: Quarterly
options.B: Annually, within 30 days of the policy anniversary
options.C: Only on request by the policyholder
options.D: Monthly

explanation: Specified ILPs receive annual statements within 30 days of the policy anniversary. All other ILPs require monthly statements.

stem: Which policies fall within the definition of a specified ILP?

options.A: Only ILPs included under CPFIS
options.B: ILPs with death benefits of at least 100 percent of premiums
options.C: Regular premium ILPs, and single or recurrent single premium ILPs whose death and critical illness benefits are at least 150 percent of premiums
options.D: Only single premium ILPs

explanation: Specified ILPs are regular premium ILPs, and single or recurrent single premium ILPs where death and critical illness benefits are at least 150 percent of premiums.

stem: Within what periods must insurers send the Semi-Annual Report and the Relevant Audit Report to policyholders?

options.A: 3 months and 6 months respectively
options.B: 30 days for both
options.C: 1 month and 2 months respectively
options.D: 2 months and 3 months respectively

explanation: The Semi-Annual Report is due within 2 months and the Relevant Audit Report within 3 months of the relevant period end.

stem: When may an insurer substitute the underlying fund's reports for the ILP sub-fund reports?

options.A: Only where the minimum subscription is a single premium of at least USD50,000 or annualised regular premiums of at least USD5,000, the policy is not CPF-included, and the policyholder consents in writing
options.B: Where the policyholder is an accredited investor
options.C: Where MAS grants prior approval
options.D: Whenever the sub-fund feeds wholly into a single underlying fund

explanation: All three conditions must be satisfied: the minimum subscription threshold, the policy not being CPF-included, and written policyholder consent.

stem: Where ILP reports are provided electronically, what are the policyholder's hardcopy rights?

options.A: Hardcopies on request at the policyholder's cost only
options.B: At least one month to opt for hardcopies, with a hardcopy provided within two weeks of a request
options.C: Two weeks to opt in, with a hardcopy provided within one month
options.D: No right to hardcopies once electronic delivery is chosen

explanation: Policyholders must be given at least one month to elect hardcopies, and a hardcopy must be supplied within two weeks of a request. Reports posted on a website must remain available for at least 12 months.

stem: Which of the following is prohibited by MAS 307 in relation to ILP sub-fund expenses?

options.A: Charging the investment management fee to the sub-fund
options.B: Charging the sub-fund's audit fee to the sub-fund
options.C: Charging marketing and promotion expenses to the sub-fund
options.D: Charging custodian fees to the sub-fund

explanation: Marketing and promotion expenses may not be charged to the sub-fund. Also prohibited are retaining cash rebates from brokers, receiving travel, accommodation or entertainment benefits, and charging the costs of failed CPF trades to the sub-fund.

stem: What is the position on soft dollar arrangements under MAS 307?

options.A: They are permitted only with policyholder consent
options.B: They are banned outright
options.C: They are permitted without restriction
options.D: They are permitted only under strict conditions, such as assisting in the provision of advice and being consistent with best execution

explanation: Soft dollars are not banned outright. They are allowed only under strict conditions, including that they assist in the provision of advice and do not compromise best execution.

stem: An ILP sub-fund invests in an underlying CIS that ceases to be an Excluded Investment Product. Which timelines apply?

options.A: Dispose of the underlying EIP-CIS within 3 months, extendable to 12 months, or reclassify the ILP as a Specified Investment Product within 4 months
options.B: Dispose within 4 months, or reclassify within 3 months
options.C: Dispose within 12 months, or reclassify within 12 months
options.D: Dispose within 30 days, with no reclassification option

explanation: The disposal route allows 3 months, extendable to 12 months with monthly re-satisfaction of the conditions. The reclassification route allows 4 months, after which the Customer Knowledge Assessment applies.

stem: Under the non-mandatory standards in MAS 307, when should redemption proceeds be paid for an ILP sub-fund that feeds into a collective investment scheme?

options.A: T+6 business days
options.B: T+7 business days
options.C: T+10 business days
options.D: T+4 business days

explanation: Feeder sub-funds should pay within T+7 business days. Bond and money market sub-funds should pay within T+4, and other sub-funds within T+6.

stem: How long should a suspension of dealing in an ILP sub-fund last under the best practice standards?

options.A: It may continue indefinitely at the insurer's discretion
options.B: It should cease within 7 days, with no review requirement
options.C: It should cease within 21 days, subject to weekly review
options.D: It should cease within 30 days, subject to monthly review

explanation: Any dealing suspension should cease within 21 days and is subject to weekly review. Sub-funds should also deal at least once a month.

stem: A policyholder redeems 10,000 units when the true price is $1.224 but the dealing price is rounded to $1.22. How is the $40 difference treated?

options.A: Retained by the insurer as an administration fee
options.B: Paid to the policyholder as a rounding adjustment
options.C: Written off against the insurer's shareholder fund
options.D: Credited to the sub-fund

explanation: Rounding differences arising from pricing should be credited to the sub-fund. Here 10,000 x $0.004 = $40 goes to the sub-fund rather than to the insurer or the policyholder.

stem: How often should ILP sub-fund units be valued?

options.A: Every business day, or at least monthly where dealing is not daily, with property valued yearly
options.B: At least weekly in all cases
options.C: At least quarterly in all cases
options.D: Only when a redemption request is received

explanation: Units should be valued every business day, or at least monthly where dealing is not daily. Property holdings should be valued yearly.

stem: A valuation error of 0.7 percent of NAV per unit occurs. One affected policyholder's loss is $15. What should the insurer do?

options.A: Compensate the policyholder but not the sub-fund
options.B: Compensate the sub-fund, but the policyholder need not be compensated as the amount does not exceed $20
options.C: Compensate both, since the error exceeds 0.5 percent
options.D: Compensate neither the policyholder nor the sub-fund, as the amounts are small

explanation: Where the error is 0.5 percent or more of NAV per unit, the sub-fund must always be compensated. Compensation to an individual policyholder is not required where the amount does not exceed $20.

stem: Which requirement applies to past performance shown in an ILP advertisement?

options.A: A period of at least 3 years, ending no more than 1 month before the advertisement
options.B: Any period, provided a disclaimer is added
options.C: A period of at least 1 year, ending no more than 3 months before the advertisement, with no simulated results
options.D: A period of at least 6 months, with simulated results allowed if labelled

explanation: Past performance must cover at least 1 year ending no more than 3 months before the advertisement, and simulated results may not be used. Text should be no smaller than 10-point Times New Roman, with a 5-second display for broadcast statements.

stem: What is the page limit for a Product Highlights Sheet for an ILP?

options.A: Eight pages in all cases
options.B: There is no page limit, but disclaimers are mandatory
options.C: Two pages in all cases
options.D: Four pages, or eight pages including diagrams and a glossary

explanation: The PHS should not exceed four pages, extending to eight only where diagrams and a glossary are included, and it must not contain disclaimers.

stem: Under FAA-G01, which type of applicant may be granted a financial adviser's licence?

options.A: A corporation with a physical presence in Singapore
options.B: Any entity registered with ACRA
options.C: An individual sole proprietor with relevant experience
options.D: A partnership of at least two licensed representatives

explanation: The licence is granted only to a corporation with a physical presence in Singapore. Individuals and partnerships do not qualify.

stem: What is the minimum number of full-time appointed representatives an FA licence applicant must have?
explanation: An applicant must have a minimum of 2 full-time appointed representatives.

stem: What experience should the CEO and executive directors of an FA licence applicant have?

options.A: At least 3 years of relevant experience in any capacity
options.B: At least 10 years in the financial industry
options.C: At least 5 years of relevant working experience, including 3 years in a managerial capacity
options.D: At least 5 years of relevant experience plus a further 3 years in a managerial capacity

explanation: Each should have at least 5 years of relevant working experience, of which 3 years are in a managerial capacity. The managerial years sit inside the 5 years rather than on top of them.

stem: What are the residency and board composition requirements for an FA licence applicant?

options.A: At least 3 directors, all resident in Singapore
options.B: At least 2 directors, with no residency requirement
options.C: At least 1 director resident in Singapore, with the CEO permitted to be overseas
options.D: At least 2 directors, one resident in Singapore, and the CEO resident in Singapore

explanation: The board must have at least 2 directors, at least one of whom is resident in Singapore, and the CEO must also be resident in Singapore.

stem: An FA licence applicant intends to advise on life policies only. What is the minimum paid-up capital?
explanation: The minimum paid-up capital is $150,000 for advising on or arranging life policies. The $300,000 tier applies where activities include futures contracts, leveraged spot foreign exchange, or over-the-counter currency derivatives.

stem: Which activity triggers the higher minimum paid-up capital requirement of $300,000?

options.A: Advising on collective investment schemes
options.B: Advising on futures contracts or spot foreign exchange for leveraged trading
options.C: Arranging health insurance
options.D: Advising on life policies

explanation: The $300,000 tier applies where the applicant's activities include advising on futures contracts, spot foreign exchange for leveraged trading, or over-the-counter currency derivatives.

stem: What is the minimum professional indemnity insurance an FA licensee must maintain?
explanation: An FA licensee must maintain professional indemnity insurance of at least $500,000.

stem: An FA licensee has a net asset value of $800,000. What is the maximum permitted deductible on its professional indemnity policy?
explanation: The deductible must not exceed 20 percent of net asset value, so 20 percent of $800,000 = $160,000. The 20 percent cap relates to net asset value, not to the sum insured.

stem: An FA licensee is covered under a group professional indemnity policy. What quantum of cover is expected?

options.A: Five times the required amount
options.B: Ten times the required amount
options.C: The same $500,000 minimum
options.D: Twice the required amount

explanation: Where cover is provided under a group policy, the group PII quantum should be 5 times the required amount.

stem: An FA licence applicant has no 3-year corporate track record. On what basis might MAS still consider the application?

options.A: If the applicant restricts itself to accredited investors
options.B: If the CEO holds at least 20 percent of the shares and the CEO and executive directors together hold at least 50 percent
options.C: If the applicant doubles its paid-up capital
options.D: If the applicant appoints an independent director

explanation: The shareholding route is an alternative for applicants lacking the 3-year track record. It requires the CEO to hold at least 20 percent of the shares, with the CEO and executive directors together holding at least 50 percent.

stem: Which of the following is a minimum entry requirement for an appointed representative?

options.A: Passing the relevant CMFAS examinations, and nothing further
options.B: Being at least 18 years old and passing the relevant examinations
options.C: Being at least 21 years old, passing the relevant CMFAS examinations, and satisfying MAS's fit and proper criteria
options.D: Holding a degree in finance

explanation: All three limbs apply: minimum age of 21, the relevant examination passes, and satisfaction of the fit and proper criteria. Examination passes alone are not sufficient.

stem: Which of the following is one of the three fit and proper criteria in FSG-G01?

options.A: Volume of business generated
options.B: Membership of a professional body
options.C: Length of service with the current employer
options.D: Competence and capability

explanation: The three criteria are honesty, integrity and reputation; competence and capability; and financial soundness. The onus is on the relevant person to demonstrate fitness and propriety.

stem: A representative fails to satisfy one of the three fit and proper criteria. What follows?

options.A: MAS considers the circumstances in the round rather than refusing automatically
options.B: The representative is given 14 days to remedy the failure
options.C: The principal may waive the criterion internally
options.D: Automatic refusal, as each criterion is an absolute bar

explanation: Failure to meet one criterion does not lead automatically to refusal. MAS considers the circumstances as a whole, with the onus on the person to demonstrate fitness and propriety.

stem: Under Circular CMI 01/2011, what lookback period applies to written self-declarations by prospective representatives?

options.A: 7 years
options.B: 10 years
options.C: 3 years
options.D: 5 years

explanation: The self-declaration covers a 10-year lookback. Due diligence also includes reference checks with previous employers, checks of the MAS Public Register, and probity searches.

stem: Which probity searches does CMI 01/2011 expect when onboarding a prospective representative?

options.A: Tax residency confirmation from IRAS
options.B: A medical fitness certificate
options.C: Bankruptcy checks with IPTO, and CPF contribution arrears checks for the self-employed
options.D: Credit card spending analysis

explanation: Probity searches include bankruptcy checks with the Insolvency and Public Trustee's Office and, for self-employed candidates, checks for CPF contribution arrears.

stem: A person makes a false statement in a declaration lodged with MAS through his principal. What is the maximum fine?
explanation: A false statement in a declaration lodged with MAS through the principal attracts a fine of up to $50,000. It is also an offence to employ a person subject to a prohibition order.

stem: A representative changes his residential address. Within what period must MAS be notified?

options.A: 14 days
options.B: 30 days
options.C: At the next annual declaration
options.D: 7 days

explanation: MAS must be notified of changes in a representative's particulars within 14 days. Declarations themselves should be renewed annually.

stem: For a life policy, where should the distribution cost be disclosed under the FAA-G04 standards of conduct?

options.A: On the financial adviser's website
options.B: In the Benefit Illustration
options.C: In a separate commission letter
options.D: In the annual policy statement only

explanation: FAA-G04 identifies disclosure of the distribution cost in the Benefit Illustration as the means of disclosing remuneration for a life policy.

stem: A representative cannot justify a recommendation on suitability grounds, so he offers to rebate part of his commission to the client. Is this acceptable under FAA-G04?

options.A: Yes, provided the rebate is disclosed
options.B: Yes, provided the client agrees in writing
options.C: No, a commission rebate is not a substitute for having a reasonable basis for the recommendation
options.D: Yes, if the client is an accredited investor

explanation: FAA-G04 requires a reasonable basis for every recommendation. Offering to rebate commission does not cure an unsuitable recommendation.

stem: Which complaints handling arrangements does FAA-G04 expect?

options.A: Referral of all complaints directly to MAS
options.B: Handling by the representative who made the sale
options.C: An external ombudsman appointed by the financial adviser
options.D: A designated officer to handle complaints and a complaints register

explanation: FAA-G04 expects a designated officer for complaints handling together with a complaints register, as part of standards covering integrity, competence, disclosure, knowing the client, record keeping and managing conflicts of interest.

stem: Under FAA-G05 and Regulation 21 of the FAR, when may a financial adviser describe itself as 'independent'?

options.A: When it operates free from commission bias, is not restricted in the range of products it advises on, and has no conflicts of interest from links with product providers
options.B: When it advises only accredited investors
options.C: When it is not owned by a product provider, regardless of its commission arrangements
options.D: When it satisfies any one of the three independence conditions

explanation: All three conditions must be satisfied. Product providers should not use the term at all, and a breach is an offence.

stem: Which commission situation does FAA-G05 treat as significant when assessing commission bias?

options.A: Commission rate differences of more than 5 percent between providers
options.B: Commissions from a single product provider exceeding 20 percent of total annual revenue
options.C: Commissions from a single product provider exceeding 50 percent of total annual revenue
options.D: Any commission received from a product provider

explanation: Commissions from one product provider exceeding 20 percent of total annual revenue, and differences of more than 20 percent in commission rates between providers, are treated as significant for assessing commission bias.

stem: A financial adviser advises on life policies from three product providers and receives evenly spread commissions. Can it call itself independent for that product class?

options.A: Yes, because there is no commission bias
options.B: Yes, because three providers is a reasonable range
options.C: No, because advising on products from fewer than four product providers in a class would generally not be considered independent for that class
options.D: Yes, provided it discloses the number of providers

explanation: Fewer than four product providers in a product class generally defeats independence for that class, even where no commission bias exists.

stem: To whom do the FAA-G09 Guidelines on structured deposits NOT apply?

options.A: Accredited, expert and institutional investors
options.B: Clients who decline financial advice
options.C: Clients transacting through an execution-only platform
options.D: Retail clients aged 62 and above

explanation: FAA-G09 carves out structured deposits sold to accredited investors, expert investors and institutional investors. Age, refusal of advice and the transaction channel do not remove the Guidelines' protection for a retail client.

stem: A bank sells a structured deposit to a retail client who signs a declaration that she does not want advice. What is the position under FAA-G09?

options.A: Only the disclosure paragraphs continue to apply
options.B: The Guidelines continue to apply in full because she is a retail client
options.C: The Guidelines apply only if the deposit exceeds S$50,000
options.D: The Guidelines cease to apply once advice is declined

explanation: The only carve-out in FAA-G09 is by investor class, covering accredited, expert and institutional investors. A retail client keeps the full protection of the Guidelines whether or not she takes advice, and warnings must in fact be given where no advice is provided.

stem: Which statement about structured deposits must be disclosed to clients under FAA-G09?

options.A: They may be described as a deposit regardless of whether they meet the definition
options.B: They are protected under the Deposit Insurance Act up to S$100,000
options.C: They are not insured under the Deposit Insurance Act
options.D: The principal is guaranteed at all times, including on early withdrawal

explanation: Clients must be told that structured deposits are not covered by deposit insurance, unlike conventional deposits, and that early withdrawal may mean the loss of part of the principal. A product must not be labelled a deposit unless it meets the definition.

stem: Under which MAS Notice do dual currency investments fall?

options.A: Notice FAA-N06
options.B: Notice FAA-N16
options.C: Notice FAA-N20
options.D: Notice FAA-N11

explanation: FAA-G09 states that dual currency investments fall under Notice FAA-N11. The others deal with anti-money laundering, the basis of recommendations and the balanced scorecard remuneration framework respectively.

stem: Which CMFAS modules should a representative marketing structured deposits have passed under FAA-G09, absent equivalent firm training?

options.A: Modules 5 and 8
options.B: Modules 9 and 9A
options.C: Modules 6A and 8A
options.D: Modules 1A and 6

explanation: FAA-G09 points to CMFAS Module 5 and Module 8, or equivalent training provided by the financial adviser, as the competency expectation for representatives marketing structured deposits.

stem: A bank sets up a booth in a shopping mall that accepts completed structured deposit applications. What follows under FAA-G09?

options.A: It requires only internal compliance sign-off
options.B: It constitutes a new place of business requiring MAS approval under section 12 of the Banking Act
options.C: It is permitted only if staffed by bank tellers
options.D: Nothing, since a temporary booth is never a place of business

explanation: A booth that accepts applications is a new place of business needing MAS approval under section 12 of the Banking Act. A booth that merely distributes brochures is different. Separately, bank tellers should not be marketing structured deposits at all.

stem: Under FAA-G10, which combination of steps is required when a financial adviser recommends a switch?

options.A: A cooling-off period of 14 days with no further documentation
options.B: Verbal disclosure of charges and a supervisor's review only
options.C: Written disclosure of fees, charges and disadvantages with a prescribed warning, a client declaration, a representative declaration on free switching entitlement, and supervisor review
options.D: A client declaration alone, since the client bears the decision

explanation: FAA-G10 requires all four elements together: written disclosure with the prescribed warning, the client's written declaration on whether he was advised to switch, the representative's declaration of any free switching entitlement, and supervisor review in line with paragraph 42 of FAA-N16.

stem: A representative argues that the client's signed switching declaration also covers the representative's and supervisor's obligations. Is this correct?

options.A: No, but only where the switch involves a life policy
options.B: Yes, a single client signature discharges the firm's switching duties
options.C: Yes, provided the supervisor countersigns within 30 days
options.D: No, the client, representative and supervisor each have a distinct declaration or review role

explanation: The client declares whether he was advised to switch, the representative declares any free switching entitlement, and the supervisor separately reviews the transaction. One signature cannot discharge three distinct roles, and this applies across switching recommendations generally.

stem: What does FAA-G10 expect of a financial adviser at the firm level in relation to switching?

options.A: Back-end monitoring of switching trends to detect undesirable practices
options.B: Monthly reporting of every switch to MAS
options.C: A prohibition on all switching within the first policy year
options.D: Front-end supervisor review only, since post-sale review would duplicate it

explanation: Back-end monitoring of switching trends is expected at firm level in addition to front-end supervisor reviews. FAA-G10 also says representatives should not be remunerated solely on sales volume.

stem: Which remuneration practice does FAA-G10 caution against?

options.A: Linking part of remuneration to client satisfaction
options.B: Remunerating representatives solely on the basis of sales volume
options.C: Deferring a portion of commission
options.D: Paying representatives a fixed salary

explanation: Remunerating representatives solely on sales volume is what the Guidelines warn against, because it drives the switching behaviour the safeguards are designed to catch.

stem: Which of these is one of the five fair dealing outcomes under FSG-G04?

options.A: Customers pay no more than a prescribed maximum fee
options.B: Customers achieve positive investment returns over the long term
options.C: Customers receive clear, relevant and timely information
options.D: Customers are guaranteed access to a dedicated relationship manager

explanation: Clear, relevant and timely information to customers is one of the five outcomes. The others are fair dealing central to corporate culture, products suitable for their target segments, competent representatives, and independent, effective and prompt complaints handling. Investment returns and fee caps are not outcomes.

stem: Fair dealing Outcome One under FSG-G04 is primarily directed at which level of the organisation?

options.A: The independent sales audit unit
options.B: External auditors reviewing the annual accounts
options.C: Front-line representatives dealing with customers
options.D: The board and senior management, as corporate culture

explanation: Outcome One concerns fair dealing being central to corporate culture, driven by the board and senior management. Reading it as a front-line conduct rule misses its point.

stem: What remuneration mix does FSG-G04 cite as good practice?

options.A: 40% sales and 60% non-sales measures
options.B: 50% sales and 50% non-sales measures
options.C: 100% non-sales measures for all representatives
options.D: 60% sales and 40% non-sales measures

explanation: The Guidelines cite 40% sales and 60% non-sales measures as good practice. It is presented as good practice rather than a mandated ratio.

stem: Under FSG-G04, how long must complaints records be kept and how much notice is expected for fee changes?

options.A: 3 years of records, at least 14 days' notice
options.B: 5 years of records, at least 30 days' notice
options.C: 6 years of records, at least 60 days' notice
options.D: 5 years of records, at least 14 days' notice

explanation: Complaints records are kept for 5 years and fee changes require at least 30 days' notice. Unresolved complaints may be referred to FIDReC, and all Specified Investment Products are treated as complex products.

stem: Under FAA-G14, a client is 64 years old and holds a university degree, but is proficient in English. Is he a selected client?

options.A: Yes, because he is above 62
options.B: Yes, because age alone is decisive for selected client status
options.C: No, because only one of the three criteria is met
options.D: No, because selected client status applies only to clients aged 70 and above

explanation: A selected client must meet any two of three criteria: aged 62 or older, not proficient in spoken or written English, and educational qualification below GCE O-level or N-level. Here only the age criterion is met, so he is not a selected client.

stem: A client is 65, has no O-level qualification and reads English poorly. The firm documents an assessment showing she has extensive investment experience. What is the effect under FAA-G14?

options.A: She becomes a selected client only for life policies
options.B: Selected client status is determined solely by the product type
options.C: She remains a selected client because three criteria are met
options.D: The documented assessment of adequate investment experience can displace selected client treatment

explanation: The definition applies unless a documented assessment shows adequate investment experience. Without that documentation she would be a selected client, since she meets more than two of the criteria.

stem: Under FAA-G14, what is the effective date of a transaction for a life policy?

options.A: The latest of the dates the policy is issued, takes effect, or cover commences
options.B: The earliest of the dates the policy is issued or cover commences
options.C: The date the application is signed by the client
options.D: The date the first premium is received

explanation: For a life policy the effective date is the latest of the date the policy is issued, the date it takes effect and the date cover commences. For other investment products it is the date the application is accepted by the product manufacturer.

stem: For a unit trust purchase, when is the effective date of the transaction under FAA-G14?

options.A: The date the client signs the application
options.B: The date the application is accepted by the product manufacturer
options.C: The date units are allotted to the client's account
options.D: The date the supervisor completes his review

explanation: For investment products other than life policies, the effective date is the date the application is accepted by the product manufacturer. The latest-of-three test applies only to life policies.

stem: How often must the ISA Unit perform post-transaction checks under FAA-G14, and what must each check comprise?

options.A: Every month, comprising a client survey only
options.B: Annually, comprising a documentation review only
options.C: Every calendar quarter, comprising a documentation review and a client survey on each sampled transaction
options.D: Every calendar quarter, comprising either a documentation review or a client survey

explanation: Post-transaction checks are performed every calendar quarter and must include both a documentation review and a client survey on each sampled transaction. One does not substitute for the other.

stem: A client does not respond to the post-transaction phone survey. After how many unsuccessful call attempts may the survey be closed, and what is the effect on the representative?

options.A: Five attempts, and the transaction is voided
options.B: Three attempts, and an infraction is recorded against the supervisor
options.C: Two attempts, and the representative is graded down
options.D: Three attempts, and the representative is not penalised for the client's non-participation

explanation: A phone survey may be closed after three unsuccessful call attempts, and the representative is not penalised for a client's non-participation. A written survey may be closed after one month and an electronic survey after two weeks.

stem: Which of these is a Category 1 infraction under the balanced scorecard framework?

options.A: Falsifying a client's responses in the fact-find
options.B: Submitting documentation one day after the internal deadline
options.C: A late filing of an internal activity report
options.D: A typographical error in a client's address

explanation: Falsifying client responses is among the Annex 3 Category 1 examples, alongside insufficient fact-finding, unsuitable recommendations, non-disclosure of key features and risks, misleading statements, pre-signed blank forms, harassment and allowing unauthorised persons to advise. Category 1 infractions have a material impact on clients' interests, while administrative lapses generally fall under Category 2.

stem: What distinguishes a Category 1 infraction from a Category 2 infraction?

options.A: Category 1 arises only from pre-transaction checks
options.B: Category 1 involves a material impact on clients' interests
options.C: Category 1 applies only to supervisors
options.D: Category 1 relates only to documentation completeness

explanation: The dividing line is materiality to clients' interests. Administrative lapses generally sit in Category 2, and the categories apply to representatives as well as supervisors.

stem: A representative is assigned grade E for a quarter. Which set of measures applies under FAA-G14?

options.A: A written warning and re-training, with no restriction on supervisory roles
options.B: Close supervision by his own supervisor, accompaniment on three closed sales and full-scale checks for one month
options.C: Close supervision overseen by the CEO or a designate other than his supervisor, accompaniment on at least five closed sales, full-scale checks on every transaction for at least three months, and no supervisory or managerial role for at least one year
options.D: Immediate termination of his appointment as a representative

explanation: Grade E triggers close supervision with oversight by the CEO or a designate other than his own supervisor, accompaniment on a minimum of five closed sales, full-scale checks by the ISA Unit on every transaction for a minimum of three months, and a bar from any supervisory or managerial role for at least one year.

stem: For the purposes of the grade E accompaniment requirement, what counts as a closed sale?

options.A: Any client contact recorded in the firm's system
options.B: Any prospecting meeting arranged by the representative
options.C: A meeting where a product brochure is presented
options.D: A transaction involving fact-find, needs analysis, recommendation and client acceptance

explanation: A closed sale requires the full cycle of fact-find, needs analysis, recommendation and client acceptance. Accompanying five prospecting meetings does not satisfy the requirement.

stem: A supervisor is graded Unsatisfactory in two consecutive quarters. What follows under FAA-G14?

options.A: He must not hold a supervisory or managerial role for at least one year from the second consecutive grade
options.B: He must not hold a supervisory role for at least three years
options.C: He is barred permanently from supervisory roles
options.D: No restriction applies provided his own supervisor is graded satisfactorily

explanation: Two consecutive Unsatisfactory quarters bar a supervisor from any supervisory or managerial role for at least one year from the second grade. Note the contrast with a representative, whose one-year bar is triggered by a single grade E.

stem: A supervisor is graded Unsatisfactory and his own direct supervisor is graded Unsatisfactory in the same quarter. How should oversight be arranged?

options.A: The ISA Unit assumes the supervisory role
options.B: A higher-tier supervisor performs the role
options.C: An external consultant must be appointed
options.D: Oversight is suspended until the next quarter's grades

explanation: Where the direct supervisor is also Unsatisfactory in the same quarter, a higher-tier supervisor performs the role. The firm should also review the adequacy of oversight and may reduce the number of representatives under him or impose a recruitment moratorium.

stem: When conducting reference checks on a prospective representative, what balanced scorecard information should an FA request?

options.A: The last grade from the immediately preceding quarter
options.B: All grades ever assigned to the individual
options.C: The individual's last four grades within the past 10 years
options.D: The last four grades within the past 3 years

explanation: The request covers the individual's last four balanced scorecard grades within the past 10 years, and the responding FA should disclose them, including both sets where the individual served as both representative and supervisor.

stem: An individual served as both a representative and a supervisor at his former firm. What should the responding FA disclose on a reference check?

options.A: A single averaged grade combining both roles
options.B: Only the representative grades, as supervisory grades are confidential
options.C: Only the supervisory grades, as they are more senior
options.D: Both sets of grades

explanation: Where the individual served in both capacities, both sets of grades should be disclosed. Averaging or withholding either set would defeat the purpose of the check.

stem: From 1 January 2016, what must supervisors do before documentation is submitted to product manufacturers under FAA-G14?

options.A: Review all documentation and the basis of every recommendation, except for specified rollovers
options.B: Review only transactions involving selected clients
options.C: Review only transactions where the client declined advice
options.D: Review a random sample of at least 10% of recommendations

explanation: Pre-transaction checks require supervisors to review all documentation and the basis of every recommendation before submission, with an exception for rollovers of dual currency investments or structured notes relating to equities or commodities.

stem: An infraction is detected during a pre-transaction check. How does it affect the representative's balanced scorecard grade?

options.A: It is factored in only if the client complains
options.B: It is not factored into the balanced scorecard
options.C: It is factored in and also reduces the supervisor's grade
options.D: It is factored in at half weighting

explanation: Infractions found at the pre-transaction stage are not factored into the balanced scorecard grade or remuneration. Only post-transaction findings count. Records of these checks are kept for at least five years.

stem: A time-sensitive product has no free-look or cancellation period and the pre-transaction check was not completed before the effective date. By when must it be completed?

options.A: By the end of the next calendar quarter
options.B: Within one month
options.C: Within 5 business days
options.D: Within 14 calendar days

explanation: Checks not completed before the effective date must be completed within the free-look or cancellation period, or within 5 business days for time-sensitive products that have no such period.

stem: Which research falls outside the scope of Guidelines FAA-G13 on conflicts of interest?

options.A: A report on broad economic trends and asset allocation
options.B: A report comparing two named unit trusts
options.C: A report on a specific corporate bond issue
options.D: A report recommending a specific listed company's shares

explanation: FAA-G13 covers research analyses or reports on clearly identifiable investment products. General economic or asset allocation research is excluded. Internal policies under the Guidelines must be approved by senior management.

stem: Which arrangement breaches the analyst separation expectations in FAA-G13?

options.A: Analysts attending firm-wide training sessions
options.B: Research reports being reviewed and approved by the corporate finance function before publication
options.C: Analysts being paid from the firm's overall profits
options.D: Analysts reporting to a head of research

explanation: Research analysts should be functionally separated from sales, trading, dealing and corporate finance, and reports should not be reviewed or approved by those functions. Being paid out of general firm profits is not itself objectionable.

stem: A financial adviser offers a prospective corporate client favourable research coverage in exchange for an underwriting mandate. What is the position under FAA-G13?

options.A: Acceptable if disclosed in the research report
options.B: Acceptable if the analyst genuinely holds that view
options.C: Prohibited, as favourable coverage must not be offered as consideration for business
options.D: Acceptable if approved by senior management

explanation: Offering favourable coverage as consideration for business is prohibited, as is basing analyst compensation on specific transactions of the sales, trading or corporate finance functions.

stem: A research report carries a statement that the financial adviser 'may or may not have an interest' in the securities mentioned. Does this satisfy FAA-G13?

options.A: Yes, if the report is distributed only to institutional clients
options.B: Yes, if the analyst signs a separate declaration
options.C: Yes, provided it appears on the first page
options.D: No, boilerplate statements of that kind are insufficient

explanation: Conflicts must be disclosed in writing in a clear and prominent manner. A generic statement that the adviser may or may not have an interest does not meet the standard.

stem: For how long must records of the bases of research recommendations be kept?

options.A: Not less than 5 years from publication
options.B: Not less than 7 years from publication
options.C: Not less than 1 year from publication
options.D: Not less than 3 years from publication

explanation: Records of the bases of recommendations must be kept for not less than 5 years from publication.

stem: Before offering an insurer's life policy online without advice, what must a financial adviser also do under FAA-G15?

options.A: Restrict sales to clients who have passed a CKA
options.B: Make available that insurer's equivalent direct purchase insurance product on its online direct channel
options.C: Provide a telephone advisory service free of charge
options.D: Obtain MAS approval for the online channel

explanation: FAA-G15 expects the equivalent DPI to be offered on the same online direct channel. Offering only the full-priced policy online is not sufficient. The Guidelines took effect on 31 March 2017.

stem: A client buys a life policy online with no advice provided. Which safeguard still applies under FAA-G15?

options.A: None, since no advice is given and the client accepts the risk
options.B: Only the provision of the policy wordings
options.C: Prominent statements or pop-ups covering the nature of the product, the free-look period and the absence of advice
options.D: Only the requirement to obtain the client's identification particulars

explanation: The absence of advice does not remove the safeguards. The client must receive the FAA-N16 paragraph 37(b) documents plus full policy wordings, acknowledge the Annex A items, and be shown prominent statements that the policy is not a savings account or deposit, that premiums may not be recovered on early termination, that some benefits are not guaranteed, that a 14-day free-look applies, that he may request an explanation, and that he should consider suitability himself.

stem: An online application is accepted subject to an exclusion and a premium loading. What does FAA-G15 require?

options.A: The application must be referred to a representative for advice
options.B: The client must be given a further 14 days to reconsider beyond the free-look
options.C: Nothing further, as acceptance terms are set by the insurer
options.D: The conditional acceptance must be highlighted to the client

explanation: Conditional acceptance, such as exclusions or premium loadings, must be highlighted to the client so that he understands the cover he is actually buying.

stem: Which tools does Annex B of FAA-G15 expect online channels to direct clients towards?

options.A: The CPF Insurance Estimator, the MoneySense Budget Calculator and comparefirst.sg
options.B: Any commercial insurance comparison website
options.C: The insurer's own illustration engine only
options.D: An independent actuarial consultant

explanation: Annex B points clients to the CPF Insurance Estimator, the MoneySense Budget Calculator and comparefirst.sg to help them assess their own needs.

stem: Why are monthly renewable group term policies generally not expected to fall within FAA-G15?

options.A: Because they are not life policies
options.B: Because they carry no long-term commitment
options.C: Because they are sold only to corporations
options.D: Because they are exempt investment products

explanation: The carve-out rests on the absence of long-term commitment in a monthly renewable group term policy. Ordinary individual term policies remain within scope.

stem: Under the ACMF framework implemented by FAA-G16, how does a relevant foreign entity operate in Singapore?

options.A: By appointing a Singapore-resident director
options.B: By obtaining its own Singapore financial adviser's licence
options.C: As an exempt financial adviser under section 23(1)(f) of the FAA, through an approved arrangement under Regulation 32CB
options.D: By registering as a branch with ACRA only

explanation: The foreign entity operates as an exempt FA under section 23(1)(f) of the FAA through an approved Regulation 32CB arrangement with a host Singapore Entity or Hosting Platform Operator. It does not hold its own Singapore licence.

stem: When was the ASEAN Capital Market Professional Mobility Framework MOU signed, and when did it take effect?

options.A: Signed 1 January 2019, effective 31 March 2017
options.B: Signed 23 May 2002, effective 1 October 2011
options.C: Signed 1 April 2017, effective 1 April 2018
options.D: Signed 11 October 2018, effective 1 January 2019

explanation: The MOU was signed on 11 October 2018 and took effect on 1 January 2019.

stem: Which products are Specified ASEAN capital markets products under the ACMF Pass?

options.A: Listed shares, bonds including sukuk, and CIS units
options.B: Life policies and health insurance
options.C: Exchange-traded derivatives and futures
options.D: Structured deposits and dual currency investments

explanation: The ACMF Pass covers listed shares, bonds including sukuk, and units in collective investment schemes. Derivatives and life policies are not included.

stem: What corporate track record must a foreign entity have to participate in the ACMF arrangements under FAA-G16?

options.A: A minimum three-year track record
options.B: A minimum five-year track record
options.C: A minimum ten-year track record
options.D: No track record requirement, provided it is financially sound

explanation: The foreign entity must have a minimum five-year corporate track record, be financially sound, and be licensed and supervised by a Recognised ACMF member. The participating regulators are Thailand's SEC, the SC in Malaysia and the SEC in the Philippines.

stem: Under CMG-G02, what licensing regime applies to a digital advisory business?

options.A: A dedicated robo-adviser authorisation regime administered by MAS
options.B: No licensing is required if the service is fully automated
options.C: The existing SFA or FAA licensing regimes, since licensing is technology-agnostic
options.D: A sandbox exemption renewable every two years

explanation: There is no separate authorisation regime for digital advisers. Licensing is technology-agnostic, so digital advisers are licensed under the existing regimes. CMG-G02 is issued under section 321 of the SFA and section 64 of the FAA.

stem: An FA digital adviser relies on the Fund Management Exemption to rebalance client portfolios of collective investment schemes. What must it do each time it rebalances?

options.A: Obtain MAS approval for the rebalancing
options.B: Nothing further, as the one-time authorisation covers all rebalancing
options.C: Obtain fresh written authorisation from the client
options.D: Notify the client before every rebalancing

explanation: The exemption requires one-time prior written client authorisation, written disclosure of scope, fees and notice period, and notification before every rebalancing. The one-time authorisation alone is not enough.

stem: Under the Dealing Exemption in CMG-G02, an FA digital adviser may pass client orders to brokers for specified products. Which product is excluded?

options.A: Over-the-counter derivatives
options.B: Corporate bonds
options.C: Collective investment scheme units
options.D: Listed shares

explanation: The Dealing Exemption applies to specified products other than OTC derivatives, and applies regardless of whether the client accepted the recommendation.

stem: What restriction applies to FA digital advisers in relation to client assets?

options.A: They may hold client assets provided an independent custodian audits them annually
options.B: They must not handle client moneys or assets or operate omnibus accounts
options.C: They may hold client moneys up to S$50,000 per client
options.D: They may operate omnibus accounts if disclosed in the prospectus

explanation: FA digital advisers must not handle client moneys or assets, and must not operate omnibus accounts. The relaxed admission criteria in CMG-G02 relate to retail fund management applicants, not to holding client assets.

stem: Which condition forms part of the relaxed admission route for a retail fund management applicant lacking a 5-year track record or S$1 billion AUM?

options.A: At least half the board must be independent directors
options.B: The adviser must manufacture the underlying collective investment schemes itself
options.C: Portfolios must comprise only CIS that are in-substance Excluded Investment Products, with an independent post-authorisation audit at the end of the first year
options.D: The adviser must maintain paid-up capital of S$1 million

explanation: The route requires key individuals with fund management and technology experience, portfolios comprising only CIS that are in-substance EIPs, an independent post-authorisation audit at the end of the first year, that the adviser does not manufacture the underlying CIS, and that the tools are fully automated.

stem: A digital adviser outsources development of its advisory algorithm to a technology vendor. Who remains responsible for its governance?

options.A: MAS, which reviews the algorithm before launch
options.B: The technology vendor, under the outsourcing agreement
options.C: The compliance officer alone
options.D: The Board and Senior Management, who remain ultimately responsible

explanation: The Board and Senior Management are responsible for governance and supervision of the algorithms and remain ultimately responsible even where development is delegated.

stem: Which control does CMG-G02 expect over a digital adviser's algorithm?

options.A: Knock-out questions to eliminate unsuitable clients, and the ability to suspend advice when an error or bias is detected
options.B: Daily manual re-checking of every recommendation by a human adviser
options.C: Publication of the algorithm's source code
options.D: Annual re-authorisation of the algorithm by MAS

explanation: Controls should include knock-out questions to screen out unsuitable clients, a means to suspend advice where an error or bias is detected, and compliance checks on the algorithm reviewed by an independent qualified human adviser.

stem: A fully-automated digital adviser relies on the FAA-N16 exception from collecting full client information. What must it still collect?

options.A: Nothing, as the exception removes all information gathering
options.B: The client's financial objectives and risk tolerance
options.C: The client's full employment history
options.D: The client's tax residency and estate plans

explanation: The exception from paragraph 11(c) to (i) never removes the need to collect the client's financial objectives and risk tolerance, and the CKA and CAR requirements still apply.

stem: Does the balanced scorecard framework apply to a fully-automated digital adviser with no representatives advising clients directly?

options.A: Yes, with the algorithm graded in place of a representative
options.B: Yes, applied to the compliance officer
options.C: No, it does not apply where no representatives advise clients directly
options.D: Yes, applied to the Board as a whole

explanation: The balanced scorecard framework does not apply where no representatives advise clients directly, since there is no representative sales conduct to grade.

stem: A client is prospected at a shopping mall roadshow and buys a mortgage reducing term assurance policy. Does the FSG-G02 call-back safeguard apply?

options.A: No, because roadshows are outside the scope of FSG-G02
options.B: Only if the client is aged over 62
options.C: No, because MRTA is a simple life policy ancillary to a loan
options.D: Yes, because MRTA is not exempt from the call-back safeguard

explanation: Simple life policies ancillary to loans are exempt from the call-back safeguard, but mortgage reducing term assurance is expressly not exempt. FSG-G02 took effect on 1 April 2017.

stem: What proportion of retail marketing arrangements must be covered by mystery shopping and site visits each year under FSG-G02?

options.A: At least half
options.B: All of them
options.C: A sample determined by the financial adviser
options.D: At least a quarter

explanation: Mystery shopping and site visits must cover at least half of all arrangements each year. The twelve safeguards also include a register of arrangements, upfront disclosure of identity, training, good compliance records, and remuneration not significantly higher than other channels.

stem: What is the legal status of the Code on Collective Investment Schemes?

options.A: Statutory, so a breach is automatically a criminal offence
options.B: Non-statutory, so a breach is not itself a criminal offence, but it may be relied on in civil or criminal proceedings to establish or negate liability
options.C: A purely internal MAS policy with no external effect
options.D: An industry association standard with no MAS involvement

explanation: The Code is issued by MAS under section 321 of the SFA and binds managers, approved trustees, VCC directors and VCC custodians. It is non-statutory, but MAS can revoke or suspend authorisation under section 286 or recognition under section 287 over a breach, and a trustee can lose its section 289 approval.

stem: Which changes were introduced by the 1 October 2011 revision of the CIS Code?

options.A: The removal of the trustee independence test
options.B: The abolition of performance fees
options.C: The permissible investments list, derivative and counterparty safeguards, standardised performance fees, fund naming principles, and the ban on simulated past performance data
options.D: The introduction of the VCC framework

explanation: The Code was first issued on 23 May 2002 and last revised on 23 May 2023. The 1 October 2011 revision brought in the permissible investments list, derivative and counterparty safeguards, standardised performance fees, fund naming principles, and the ban on simulated past performance data.

stem: When does the CIS Code guidance treat a trustee as failing the independence test?

options.A: Where any person holds 5 percent or more of both entities
options.B: Where the trustee and manager share a registered office
options.C: Where the trustee earns more than half its revenue from one manager
options.D: Where any person holds 20 percent or more of the trustee's shares and also 20 percent or more of the manager's or its related corporations' shares

explanation: The trustee must be independent of the manager and deal at arm's length. Independence fails on the 20 percent cross-shareholding test, which also applies to a VCC custodian's independence from the VCC and the manager.

stem: Within what period must a trustee report a breach of section 289(3) of the SFA to MAS?

options.A: Within 3 business days of awareness
options.B: Within 14 days of awareness
options.C: Within 1 month of awareness
options.D: At the next semi-annual report

explanation: A breach of section 289(3) must be reported to MAS within 3 business days of the trustee becoming aware of it.

stem: When must semi-annual and annual accounts and reports be sent to participants of a collective investment scheme?

options.A: Within 1 month and 2 months respectively
options.B: Within 2 months of period end and 3 months of financial year end respectively
options.C: Within 3 months and 6 months respectively
options.D: Within 30 days for both

explanation: Semi-annual accounts and reports go to participants within 2 months of period end, and annual accounts and reports within 3 months of the financial year end.

stem: A participant who receives reports electronically asks for a hardcopy. What must happen?

options.A: No hardcopy need be provided once electronic delivery is elected
options.B: The hardcopy must be provided within 3 business days at a reasonable fee
options.C: The hardcopy must be provided within 2 weeks at no cost, and electronic reports must stay posted for at least 12 months
options.D: The hardcopy must be provided within 1 month at the participant's cost

explanation: Electronic reports must remain posted for at least 12 months, and a participant requesting a hardcopy must receive it within 2 weeks at no cost.

stem: Which of the following is prohibited for the manager of a collective investment scheme?

options.A: Transacting with third parties at arm's length
options.B: Acting in accordance with the constituent document
options.C: Obtaining best execution under Notice SFA 04-N16
options.D: Acting as counterparty to an OTC derivative that the scheme invests in

explanation: The manager must not act as counterparty to an OTC derivative the scheme invests in. It must act per the constituent document and in participants' best interest, transact at arm's length, and obtain best execution.

stem: A manager uses a scheme's shareholding to place its own nominees on an issuer's board. What is the position under the CIS Code?

options.A: Prohibited, as the manager must not exercise significant influence over an issuer's management through the scheme
options.B: Permitted if the trustee consents
options.C: Permitted if disclosed to participants
options.D: Permitted if it improves the issuer's governance

explanation: The manager must not exercise significant influence over the management of an issuer through the scheme, regardless of disclosure or trustee consent.

stem: When may scheme monies be invested in securities of the manager's related corporations?

options.A: Never, in any circumstances
options.B: Where those securities are constituents of an independently constructed reference benchmark
options.C: Where the trustee gives written consent
options.D: Where the investment is under 10 percent of NAV

explanation: Investment in the manager's own securities or those of related corporations is prohibited unless they are constituents of an independently constructed reference benchmark.

stem: A scheme places surplus cash on deposit with a bank that is a related corporation of the manager. Is this prohibited lending?

options.A: Yes, all dealings with related corporations are prohibited
options.B: Yes, because deposits are a form of lending
options.C: No, bank deposits do not count as lending for this purpose
options.D: No, provided the deposit is under 5 percent of NAV

explanation: Lending scheme monies to related corporations is prohibited, but bank deposits do not count as lending. Real estate also cannot be bought from the manager or its related corporations unless Appendix 6 permits it.

stem: An external agency rates a bond A while the manager's internal assessment rates it BBB. Which rating governs?

options.A: The average of the two
options.B: Whichever rating the trustee accepts
options.C: The external rating of A
options.D: The internal rating of BBB, as the lowest rating applies

explanation: There must be no sole or mechanistic reliance on rating agencies. The manager maintains internal credit assessment standards, and where external and internal ratings differ the lowest rating applies.

stem: Within what period must redemption proceeds normally be paid under the CIS Code?

options.A: T+7 business days
options.B: T+10 business days
options.C: T+3 business days
options.D: T+4 business days

explanation: Redemption proceeds must be paid within T+7 business days, where T is the day a complete redemption request is received by the dealing cut-off. Property funds follow Appendix 6 and hedge funds follow their prospectus.

stem: When are redemption proceeds deemed to have been paid?

options.A: When the units are cancelled
options.B: When the account is credited or a cheque is mailed
options.C: When the participant confirms receipt
options.D: When the redemption request is accepted

explanation: Proceeds are deemed paid when the participant's account is credited or a cheque is mailed.

stem: How much notice must be given to MAS and participants before a significant change to a collective investment scheme takes effect?

options.A: At least 3 business days
options.B: At least 14 days
options.C: At least 1 month
options.D: At least 3 months

explanation: Significant changes require at least 1 month's notice to MAS and participants before taking effect. Unforeseeable events such as suspensions are notified as soon as practicable instead.

stem: A manager increases a scheme's charges by 0.15 percent of NAV, which remains within the cap in the trust deed. What is required?

options.A: Approval by an extraordinary resolution of participants
options.B: Notification within 3 business days after the change
options.C: Nothing, as the increase is within the trust deed cap
options.D: Notification to MAS and participants at least 1 month before it takes effect

explanation: A substantial increase in other charges, meaning 0.1 percent or more of NAV, is a significant change requiring one month's notice. The notice applies even where the fee stays within the trust deed cap.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a significant change requiring one month's notice?

options.A: A routine change in the scheme's registered mailing address
options.B: A change in investment objective or approach
options.C: Replacement of the manager or trustee
options.D: A change to or from a feeder structure

explanation: Significant changes include a change in investment objective or approach, fee increases, a substantial increase in other charges of 0.1 percent or more of NAV, replacement of the manager or trustee, and a change to or from a feeder structure.

stem: May a manager retain cash or commission rebates arising from scheme transactions?

options.A: Yes, up to 10 percent of the commission
options.B: No, the manager must not retain such rebates
options.C: Yes, if the trustee approves
options.D: Yes, if disclosed in the prospectus

explanation: The manager must not retain cash or commission rebates from scheme transactions.

stem: Which benefit can never qualify as a permissible soft dollar benefit?

options.A: Portfolio analysis software
options.B: Research that assists investment advice to the scheme
options.C: Travel, accommodation and entertainment
options.D: Market data services

explanation: Travel, accommodation and entertainment never qualify. Soft dollars may be retained only if they assist investment advice to the scheme, best execution is achieved and there is no churning.

stem: Which expense may properly be paid out of a collective investment scheme?

options.A: Commission paid to distributors for new subscriptions
options.B: Advertising the scheme in newspapers
options.C: Sponsorship of a marketing roadshow
options.D: Prospectus preparation, printing, lodgement and distribution costs

explanation: Marketing and promotion expenses cannot be paid from the scheme, but prospectus preparation, printing, lodgement and distribution costs can.

stem: A manager sub-manages 15 percent of a scheme's NAV abroad. What threshold must it meet?

options.A: The manager together with its related corporations must already manage at least S$500 million of discretionary funds in Singapore
options.B: The manager must have at least S$1 billion in assets under management globally
options.C: No threshold applies below 20 percent of NAV
options.D: The manager alone must manage at least S$100 million in Singapore

explanation: Where more than 10 percent of NAV is sub-managed abroad, or more than 10 percent is invested in foreign-registered schemes, the manager together with its related corporations must already manage at least S$500 million of discretionary funds in Singapore.

stem: How often may a performance fee crystallise under the CIS Code?

options.A: On every dealing day
options.B: No more than once a year
options.C: No more than once a quarter
options.D: Monthly, if disclosed

explanation: Performance fees must be equitable to all participants, calculated after all other payments, and crystallise no more than once a year.

stem: A scheme charges a base fee of 1.5 percent and uses a fulcrum fee structure. What is the permitted range of the fulcrum fee?

options.A: 0 percent to 1.5 percent
options.B: 0.75 percent to 2.25 percent
options.C: 0 percent to 3.0 percent
options.D: 1.5 percent to 3.0 percent

explanation: The fulcrum fee moves symmetrically with performance against the benchmark and is bounded between zero and 200 percent of the base fee. With a base fee of 1.5 percent, the range is 0 percent to 3.0 percent.

stem: When is a high water mark reset?

options.A: Whenever the benchmark is outperformed
options.B: Whenever a performance fee crystallises
options.C: At the start of each financial year
options.D: Only when NAV reaches a new historical high at the end of a performance period

explanation: The high water mark is reset only when NAV reaches a new historical high at the end of a performance period, and it resets whether or not a fee actually crystallises. The fulcrum fee and high water mark are the only two methods allowed without prior MAS consultation.

stem: Which term is prohibited in the name or description of a collective investment scheme?

options.A: Capital protected
options.B: Balanced
options.C: Global
options.D: Income
