explanation: The terms capital protected and principal protected are prohibited in any name or description. A scheme name must also not be undesirable or misleading, and must not imply it is not a CIS by calling itself a plan or account.

stem: A manager wishes to use 'fund-of-funds' in a scheme's name. When is this acceptable?

options.A: In no circumstances
options.B: Where the scheme invests substantially all its assets in five or more underlying funds
options.C: Where the scheme holds at least two underlying funds
options.D: Where the scheme invests at least half its assets in other funds

explanation: Fund-of-funds in the name is acceptable only where the scheme invests substantially all its assets in five or more underlying funds.

stem: Which activity may a collective investment scheme carry out?

options.A: Granting guarantees
options.B: Underwriting new issues
options.C: Short selling through financial derivatives under Appendix 1 sections 4 and 5
options.D: Lending monies directly to third parties

explanation: Schemes must not lend monies directly, grant guarantees, or underwrite. Short selling is permitted only through financial derivatives under Appendix 1 sections 4 and 5.

stem: What are the minimum dealing and publication requirements for a collective investment scheme?

options.A: Deal daily, and publish the unit value weekly
options.B: Deal at least quarterly, and publish the unit value monthly
options.C: Deal at the manager's discretion, with no publication requirement
options.D: Deal at least one dealing day a month, and publish the unit value at least once every dealing day

explanation: A scheme must deal at least one dealing day a month and publish the unit value at least once every dealing day.

stem: A manager wishes to suspend dealing because the underlying holdings have become illiquid. What is the position?

options.A: Illiquidity alone may not justify suspension; suspension is only for exceptional circumstances in participants' best interest
options.B: Illiquidity is always sufficient grounds for suspension
options.C: Suspension is permitted for up to 6 months on any ground
options.D: Suspension requires prior MAS approval in every case

explanation: Suspension is only for exceptional circumstances in participants' best interest, and illiquidity alone may not justify it. Suspension must be notified to participants and MAS immediately with reasons and must end within 21 days unless the trustee is satisfied an extension serves participants, with weekly trustee review.

stem: Rounding differences arise from unit pricing and allotment in a collective investment scheme. Who receives them?

options.A: The trustee, to be held on trust
options.B: The scheme, to which they must be credited
options.C: They are distributed to participants as a cash rebate
options.D: The manager, as compensation for administration

explanation: Rounding differences from unit pricing or allotment are credited to the scheme rather than kept by the manager.

stem: A valuation error of 0.8 percent of NAV per unit occurs. One participant's shortfall is S$18. What must the manager do?

options.A: Compensate neither, as the error is under 1 percent
options.B: Compensate the participant but not the scheme
options.C: Compensate the scheme, while the participant falls within the S$20 de minimis
options.D: Charge the compensation cost to the scheme

explanation: Where the error is 0.5 percent or more of NAV per unit, the scheme must always be compensated. A participant owed S$20 or less falls within the de minimis. Compensation costs cannot be charged to the scheme.

stem: A valuation error is below 0.5 percent of NAV per unit, and the manager decides to compensate one vocal participant. What follows?

options.A: The manager must first obtain MAS approval
options.B: The compensation may be charged to the scheme
options.C: Nothing, as compensation below the threshold is voluntary and may be selective
options.D: If the manager compensates one participant it must compensate all on the same basis

explanation: Below 0.5 percent no compensation is required, but if the manager compensates one participant it must compensate all on the same basis. The error must still be reported to MAS and the trustee as soon as practicable, with every affected valuation date revalued.

stem: Within what period must a breach of the Part I or II guidelines be reported to MAS?

options.A: Within 3 business days of awareness
options.B: Within 14 days of awareness
options.C: Within 1 month of awareness
options.D: At the next semi-annual report

explanation: Breaches of the Part I or II guidelines must be reported to MAS within 3 business days of awareness. Breaches must be rectified as soon as practicable, with no transactions that increase the breach.

stem: A spread limit is exceeded purely because of a ratings downgrade, and the manager rectifies it within 2 months. What is the reporting position?

options.A: It must still be reported within 3 business days
options.B: No report is needed, as passive breaches rectified within 3 months are not reportable
options.C: It must be reported at the next annual report
options.D: It must be reported only if participants suffer loss

explanation: Passive breaches caused by price movement, redemptions, corporate capital changes, benchmark weight reduction or a ratings downgrade need no report if rectified within 3 months. The grace period is extendable only if the trustee agrees it serves participants, subject to monthly review.

stem: What is the core spread of investments limit for a single entity under Appendix 1 of the CIS Code?

options.A: 35 percent of NAV
options.B: 5 percent of NAV
options.C: 10 percent of NAV
options.D: 20 percent of NAV

explanation: The core limit is 10 percent of NAV in a single entity, rising to 20 percent for a group of entities.

stem: A scheme holds government paper rated BBB. What single entity limit applies, and what cap applies per single issue?

options.A: 20 percent of NAV, with a 10 percent cap per single issue
options.B: No limit, with a 35 percent cap per single issue
options.C: 10 percent of NAV, with no per-issue cap
options.D: 35 percent of NAV, with a 20 percent cap per single issue

explanation: Government, agency or supranational paper rated at least BBB or Baa raises the single entity limit to 35 percent of NAV with a 20 percent cap per single issue. Paper rated at least AA or Aa has no single entity limit.

stem: A corporate bond held by a scheme is unrated. What spread limit applies to it?

options.A: 5 percent of NAV
options.B: 20 percent of NAV
options.C: 35 percent of NAV
options.D: 10 percent of NAV

explanation: Unrated or below investment grade corporate debt is cut to 5 percent of NAV. A downgrade below a qualifying rating pulls the limit straight back to the standard level, and concentration is separately capped at 10 percent of any single entity's outstanding shares.

stem: What is the cap on a scheme's global exposure to financial derivatives?

options.A: 50 percent of NAV at all times
options.B: 100 percent of NAV at all times
options.C: 150 percent of NAV at all times
options.D: 200 percent of NAV on average over a year

explanation: Global exposure to financial derivatives must not exceed 100 percent of NAV at all times, measured by the Commitment Approach or, with prior MAS consultation, a VaR Approach.

stem: What parameters apply to the VaR Approach for measuring derivative exposure?

options.A: Relative VaR capped at 1 times the reference portfolio's VaR, absolute VaR at 30 percent of NAV, using a 1-day holding period
options.B: No fixed parameters, as the manager may set its own model
options.C: Relative VaR capped at 1.5 times the reference portfolio's VaR, absolute VaR generally at 20 percent of NAV, using 99 percent one-tailed confidence, a 1-month holding period and a 1-year observation period
options.D: Relative VaR capped at 2 times the reference portfolio's VaR, absolute VaR at 10 percent of NAV, using 95 percent confidence

explanation: Relative VaR is capped at 1.5 times the reference portfolio's VaR and absolute VaR generally at 20 percent of NAV, using 99 percent one-tailed confidence, a 1-month holding period and a 1-year observation period.

stem: Back-testing of a scheme's VaR model produces 11 exceptions. Which zone is this and what must the manager do?

options.A: Amber zone, requiring a change of model within 12 months
options.B: Green zone, with no action required
options.C: Yellow zone, requiring investigation and remedies to be reported to MAS
options.D: Red zone, requiring positions to stop and be wound down

explanation: Back-testing exceptions are zoned Green at 0 to 4, Yellow at 5 to 9 requiring investigation and remedies to MAS, and Red at 10 or more requiring positions to stop and wind down. Exceptions are notified to MAS within 3 business days.

stem: Under the SFA, false trading and market rigging transactions are prohibited by which section?

options.A: Section 197
options.B: Section 199
options.C: Section 201
options.D: Section 218

explanation: False trading and market rigging fall under s.197. False or misleading statements fall under s.199, manipulative and deceptive devices under s.201, and insider trading by connected persons under s.218.

stem: The employment of manipulative and deceptive devices in connection with dealing in securities is prohibited under which SFA section?

options.A: Section 197
options.B: Section 199
options.C: Section 201
options.D: Section 202

explanation: Manipulative and deceptive devices are prohibited under s.201. Section 197 covers false trading and market rigging, s.199 covers false or misleading statements, and s.202 covers dissemination of information about illegal transactions.

stem: A trader based overseas manipulates the price of securities quoted on a Singapore exchange. Which statement best describes his position under the SFA?

options.A: He is outside the reach of the SFA because he acted outside Singapore
options.B: He is only liable if he is a Singapore Citizen
options.C: He is only liable under the law of the country where he acted
options.D: He can be caught by the SFA because acts outside Singapore that affect Singapore's markets are covered

explanation: Section 196 gives the market conduct provisions extraterritorial effect: conduct outside Singapore that affects Singapore's markets is caught, as is conduct in Singapore affecting foreign markets. Nationality is not the deciding factor.

stem: What is the defining characteristic of a wash sale?

options.A: The trade is executed at a price far above the market
options.B: The transaction involves no change in the beneficial ownership of the securities
options.C: The buy and sell orders come from two colluding parties
options.D: The trade is executed after market hours

explanation: A wash sale is a purchase or sale that involves no change in beneficial ownership, creating a false appearance of active trading. Orders placed by two colluding parties at substantially the same price and time are matched orders, a related but distinct practice.

stem: In an insider trading prosecution against a person connected to the corporation, what advantage does the prosecution have?

options.A: A rebuttable presumption that the person knew the information was price-sensitive and not generally available
options.B: No need to prove the person possessed the information at all
options.C: A presumption that the person intended to profit from the trade
options.D: The connected person bears the burden of proving the information was false

explanation: For connected persons there is a rebuttable presumption of knowledge that the information was price-sensitive and not generally available. The prosecution must still show the person possessed the information and traded.

stem: For insider trading by a person NOT connected to the corporation, the prosecution must prove that the person:

options.A: Was an officer of the corporation within the past 6 months
options.B: Obtained the information directly from a director
options.C: Knew the information was not generally available and was price-sensitive
options.D: Held at least 5% of the corporation's shares

explanation: Against a non-connected person, the prosecution must prove actual knowledge that the information was not generally available and, if generally available, would materially affect the price. No connection to the corporation needs to be shown.

stem: Under s.215 SFA, information announced by a listed company becomes 'generally available' when:

options.A: The announcement is drafted and approved by the board
options.B: It has been made known in a manner likely to bring it to investors' attention and a reasonable period for dissemination has elapsed
options.C: At least one analyst has published a report on it
options.D: The company's directors have all been informed

explanation: Information is generally available once it is made known in a manner likely to bring it to the attention of investors and a reasonable period for it to be disseminated has passed. Internal board approval alone does not make information public.

stem: A dealing representative executes a buy order for a client without knowing that the client possesses inside information. Which provision protects the representative?

options.A: Section 218, because he is a connected person
options.B: Section 309, the hawking exemption
options.C: Section 197, because no false appearance was created
options.D: Section 230, which exempts a licence holder or representative executing a client's order without knowledge of the inside information

explanation: Section 230 exempts a CMS licence holder or its representative who merely executes a client's order without knowledge of the inside information. The client who traded on the information remains liable.

stem: In the insider trading enforcement example cited in the study text, the civil penalty imposed was:

options.A: S$2.9 million
options.D: S$11.7 million

explanation: The cited case resulted in a civil penalty of S$2.9 million. Civil penalties are court-imposed monetary sanctions that MAS can seek as an alternative to criminal prosecution.

stem: The prohibition on securities hawking under s.309 SFA does NOT apply to offers made to:

options.A: Retail clients aged above 62
options.B: Existing clients of the dealer
options.C: Institutional investors and accredited investors
options.D: Clients who have signed a risk disclosure form

explanation: Offers to institutional investors and accredited investors under ss.304 and 305 are exempt from the hawking prohibition. Offers to ordinary retail clients arising from unsolicited meetings or calls remain prohibited.

stem: A short sale is described as 'naked' or uncovered when the seller:

options.A: Sells more than 5% of the company's issued shares
options.B: Has neither borrowed the securities nor arranged to borrow them at the time of sale
options.C: Fails to mark the order as a short sell
options.D: Sells securities he has borrowed from another broker

explanation: An uncovered or naked short sale is made without owning the securities and without any borrowing arrangement in place at the time of sale. Selling borrowed securities is a covered short sale.

stem: If a seller fails to deliver securities to settle a trade on the exchange, what happens?

options.A: The trade is automatically cancelled with no consequences
options.B: The buyer must source the securities himself
options.C: MAS suspends trading in the counter
options.D: CDP conducts a buying-in against the failing seller at the seller's cost

explanation: The Central Depository conducts a buying-in, purchasing the securities in the market on behalf of the defaulting seller and at his cost, to ensure the trade settles.

stem: The requirement to mark sell orders as short sells when they are placed is imposed by:

options.A: Section 137ZJ SFA
options.B: Section 137ZK SFA
options.C: Section 309 SFA
options.D: Regulation 45 SFR (Licensing and Conduct of Business)

explanation: Section 137ZJ requires short sell orders to be marked when placed, while s.137ZK requires reporting of short positions above the prescribed threshold. Regulation 45 deals with securities borrowing and lending collateral.

stem: Under Regulation 45 of the SFR (Licensing and Conduct of Business), a borrower of specified products must provide the lender with collateral of at least:

options.A: 50% of the market value of the borrowed products
options.B: 70% of the market value of the borrowed products
options.C: 100% of the market value of the borrowed products
options.D: 120% of the market value of the borrowed products

explanation: Collateral of at least 100% of the market value of the borrowed specified products must be provided. The requirement does not apply where the lender is an accredited, expert or institutional investor.

stem: Which of the following is a duty owed by a representative to his CLIENTS?

options.A: Whistle-blowing on colleagues' misconduct
options.B: Preserving the confidentiality of information and ensuring suitability of recommendations
options.C: Refusing all compensation other than salary
options.D: Affirming the fitness and propriety of other representatives

explanation: Duties to clients include loyalty, prudence and care, fair dealing, suitability, fair presentation of performance, and confidentiality. Whistle-blowing is a duty owed to the employer.

stem: A representative is offered a fee by a third party for work that may conflict with his employer's interests. He may accept it only if:

options.A: The fee is below S$500
options.B: He declares it in his next tax return
options.C: The work is done outside office hours
options.D: He obtains written consent from all parties involved

explanation: Additional compensation that may create a conflict with the employer's interest can only be accepted with written consent from all parties involved. The amount and timing of the work do not remove the conflict.

stem: The CPF Board administers the CPF under which ministry?

options.A: Ministry of Finance
options.B: Ministry of Manpower
options.C: Ministry of Health
options.D: Ministry of Social and Family Development

explanation: The CPF Board operates under the Ministry of Manpower. The scheme itself commenced on 1 July 1955.

stem: An employee aged 40 earns a monthly ordinary wage of S$5,000. Under the rates effective 1 Jan 2024, how much is deducted from his wage as his own (employee) CPF contribution?
explanation: For employees aged 55 and below the employee contribution rate is 20%, so 20% x S$5,000 = S$1,000. S$850 would be the employer's 17% share and S$1,850 would be the combined 37%.

stem: Under the CPF contribution rates effective 1 Jan 2024, the TOTAL (employer plus employee) contribution rate for a worker aged above 60 to 65 earning above S$750 a month is:
explanation: The total rate for above 60 to 65 is 22% (11.5% employer + 10.5% employee). 31% applies to above 55 to 60, 37% to age 55 and below, and 16.5% to above 65 to 70.

stem: A self-employed person must make compulsory CPF contributions to which account, and under what condition?

options.A: Ordinary Account, if income exceeds S$50 a month
options.B: Special Account, if income exceeds S$6,000 a year
options.C: All three accounts, regardless of income
options.D: MediSave only, if net trade income exceeds S$6,000 a year

explanation: Self-employed persons are only required to contribute to MediSave, and only when their yearly net trade income exceeds S$6,000. Contributions to the other accounts are voluntary.

stem: What is the maximum annual tax relief a member can claim for cash top-ups made to his OWN Special or Retirement Account?
explanation: Since 2022 the relief is up to S$8,000 per year for top-ups to the member's own account, with a separate S$8,000 for top-ups to loved ones. S$16,000 is the combined maximum, and S$7,000 was the old limit.

stem: A 40-year-old member has S$50,000 in his Ordinary Account and S$40,000 in his Special Account. How much EXTRA interest does he earn in a year under the extra interest scheme?
explanation: Members below 55 earn an extra 1% on the first S$60,000 of combined balances, with the OA capped at S$20,000. So (S$20,000 OA + S$40,000 SA) x 1% = S$600. Using the full S$50,000 OA would wrongly ignore the S$20,000 cap.

stem: Before opening a CPFIS account, a new investor must first:

options.A: Set aside the Full Retirement Sum
options.B: Obtain his employer's consent
options.C: Buy a Dependants' Protection Scheme policy
options.D: Complete the Self-Awareness Questionnaire (SAQ)

explanation: From 1 Oct 2018, new CPFIS investors must complete the Self-Awareness Questionnaire. He must also be at least 18, not an undischarged bankrupt, and can only invest OA above S$20,000 and SA above S$40,000.

stem: The Basic Retirement Sum for the 2026 cohort is S$110,200. What is the Full Retirement Sum for that cohort?
explanation: The FRS is 2 times the BRS, so 2 x S$110,200 = S$220,400. The other figures are the FRS for the 2024, 2025 and 2027 cohorts respectively.

stem: From 2025, the Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) is set at:

options.A: 2 times the Basic Retirement Sum
options.B: 4 times the Basic Retirement Sum
options.C: 3 times the Basic Retirement Sum
options.D: 5 times the Basic Retirement Sum

explanation: From 2025 the ERS was raised from 3 times to 4 times the BRS, allowing members to top up for higher CPF LIFE payouts. The FRS remains 2 times the BRS.

stem: A member is automatically included in CPF LIFE if he is a Singapore Citizen or PR who:

options.A: Was born in 1958 or after and has at least S$60,000 in his Retirement Account when payouts are due to start
options.B: Has reached age 55 with any Retirement Account balance
options.C: Was born before 1958 and has at least S$40,000 at age 55
options.D: Has set aside the Enhanced Retirement Sum

explanation: Auto-inclusion requires being born in 1958 or later and having at least S$60,000 in the Retirement Account when payouts are due to start. Members not auto-included may still apply to join.

stem: Which CPF LIFE plan is the default plan for members who do not choose one?

options.A: Basic Plan
options.B: Escalating Plan
options.C: Standard Plan
options.D: Flexi Plan

explanation: The Standard Plan, which pays level monthly payouts, is the default. The Escalating Plan starts lower and rises 2% yearly, while the Basic Plan is a legacy plan whose payouts fall when combined balances drop below S$60,000.

stem: From age 55, what amount can a member withdraw from his CPF unconditionally, even if he cannot set aside his retirement sum?

options.D: 20% of his retirement savings

explanation: A member can withdraw up to S$5,000 unconditionally from age 55. The additional withdrawal of up to 20% of retirement savings (less the S$5,000) is only available from age 65 for those born in 1958 or after.

stem: From 1 Jan 2025, the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme provides dollar-for-dollar matching of cash top-ups up to:

options.A: S$600 per year with no lifetime cap
options.B: S$1,000 per year with a S$10,000 lifetime cap
options.C: S$3,000 per year with a S$30,000 lifetime cap
options.D: S$2,000 per year with a S$20,000 lifetime cap

explanation: From 1 Jan 2025 the matching cap is S$2,000 per year with a S$20,000 lifetime limit, and the upper age limit is removed. The previous cap was S$600 per year.

stem: The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) applicable to a member is fixed for life when the member:

options.A: Reaches age 65
options.B: Reaches age 55
options.C: Starts CPF LIFE payouts
options.D: Makes his first MediSave withdrawal

explanation: The BHS (S$71,500 in 2024) is adjusted yearly but becomes fixed for a member once he turns 65. It is not tied to age 55 or to CPF LIFE payouts.

stem: Under CareShield Life, a claimant qualifies for payouts when he is unable to perform at least:

options.A: 2 of the 6 activities of daily living
options.B: 4 of the 6 activities of daily living
options.C: 3 of the 6 activities of daily living
options.D: All 6 activities of daily living

explanation: Severe disability means being unable to perform at least 3 of the 6 ADLs (washing, dressing, feeding, toileting, mobility, transferring). CareShield Life covers cohorts born in 1980 or later.

stem: Under the Dependants' Protection Scheme, the maximum sum assured for a member aged 58 is:
explanation: DPS provides cover of up to S$70,000 until age 60, stepping down to S$55,000 from above 60 to 65. DPS is administered solely by Great Eastern Life.

stem: The Home Protection Scheme (HPS) is compulsory for a member who:

options.A: Buys any private property with a bank loan
options.B: Owns an Executive Condominium
options.C: Rents out his HDB flat
options.D: Uses his CPF savings to pay the monthly instalments on his HDB flat

explanation: HPS is a mortgage-reducing term insurance for public housing and is compulsory when CPF savings are used for the monthly instalments. Private properties, ECs and privatised HUDC flats are not covered by HPS.

stem: A CPF member dies without making a CPF nomination. What happens to his CPF savings?

options.A: They are transferred to the Public Trustee's Office for distribution under intestacy law, which can take up to 6 months and incurs a fee
options.B: They are distributed according to his will
options.C: They are forfeited to the CPF Board
options.D: They are paid immediately to his next-of-kin within 17 working days

explanation: CPF savings do not form part of the estate and cannot pass under a will; without a nomination they go to the Public Trustee's Office, taking up to 6 months with a fee charged. The roughly 17 working day timeline applies only where a valid nomination exists.

stem: Which statement best captures the relationship between ethics and compliance?

options.A: Compliance and ethics are the same thing expressed differently
options.B: Compliance follows the letter of the law, while ethics honours the spirit behind it - an act can be legal yet unethical
options.C: Ethics applies only where no regulations exist
options.D: Compliance is voluntary while ethics is legally enforced

explanation: Compliance means observing the letter of the rules; ethics goes further and honours their spirit. Conduct can satisfy every regulation and still be unethical, which is why compliance alone is not enough.

stem: In Charles H. Green's trust equation, which factor REDUCES trust as it increases?

options.A: Credibility
options.B: Reliability
options.C: Intimacy
options.D: Self interest

explanation: The equation is Trust = (Credibility + Reliability + Intimacy) / Self Interest. Because self interest is the denominator, more apparent self-interest means less trust, while credibility, reliability and intimacy all add to trust.

stem: Which three factors are ADDED together in the numerator of the trust equation?

options.A: Credibility, reliability and intimacy
options.B: Honesty, competence and profit
options.C: Credibility, self interest and empathy
options.D: Reliability, compliance and loyalty

explanation: The numerator of the trust equation is credibility plus reliability plus intimacy. Self interest is not added; it divides the total, lowering trust as it grows.

stem: In the 18 months to June 2020, the civil penalties imposed through MAS enforcement actions amounted to:

options.A: S$3.4 million
options.B: S$2.9 million
options.C: S$11.7 million
options.D: S$6.2 million

explanation: Civil penalties in that period totalled S$11.7 million. The S$3.4 million figure was for financial penalties and compositions, S$2.9 million was a single insider trading civil penalty example, and S$6.2 million relates to the fake policies fraud case.

stem: The study text underlines the importance of ethics in financial services partly because the industry:

options.A: Employs more workers than any other sector
options.B: Contributes more than 15% of Singapore's GDP and runs on clients' trust in promises of future benefits
options.C: Is exempt from MAS supervision
options.D: Guarantees returns on all products sold

explanation: Financial services contribute over 15% of Singapore's GDP with more than 15,000 financial institutions, and the business fundamentally rests on trust: clients pay money today for promised future benefits.

stem: A representative tells himself 'everyone pads their production numbers, so it is fine if I do too'. This is an example of:

options.A: Confirmation bias
options.B: Moral motivation
options.C: Peer supervision
options.D: Rationalisation

explanation: Inventing excuses such as 'everyone does it' to justify wrongdoing is rationalisation. It preserves self-image but does not make the conduct any less wrong.

stem: According to the text, human behaviour is typically driven by:

options.A: A mix of self-interested, affection-based and moral motivations
options.B: Self-interest alone
options.C: Whatever the law requires and nothing more
options.D: The single strongest financial incentive available

explanation: People rarely act from one motive; self-interest, affection for others and moral motivation operate together. Ethical failure tends to occur when self-interest overwhelms the other motivations.

stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the four characteristics of a professional described in the text?

options.A: Mastery of a particular subject matter
options.B: Reliability
options.C: Maximising personal commission on every sale
options.D: A spirit of loyalty to fellow representatives

explanation: The four characteristics are mastery of subject matter, reliability, management of self-interest, and a spirit of loyalty to fellow representatives. Maximising one's own commission is the opposite of managing self-interest.

stem: Which of the following is a recognised hallmark of a profession?

options.A: A code of ethics enforced by a governing authority
options.B: Guaranteed high income for members
options.C: The absence of entry examinations
options.D: Freedom from any professional societies

explanation: Professions are marked by prolonged academic study, barriers to entry, independence, public recognition, a governing authority, professional societies and a code of ethics. High income is not a defining hallmark, and open entry with no examinations is the opposite of a barrier to entry.

stem: The minimum entry and examination requirements for appointed representatives are set out in:

options.A: MAS Notice FAA-N03
options.B: MAS Notice FAA-N16
options.C: MAS Guidelines FAA-G11
options.D: MAS Notice FAA-N26

explanation: FAA-N26 prescribes the minimum entry and competency (examination) requirements. FAA-N16 covers recommendations, FAA-N03 covers information to clients and product disclosure, and FAA-G11 contains the fair dealing guidelines.

stem: Regarding the handling of clients' money, a professional representative should:

options.A: Collect cash premiums personally to save the client time
options.B: Not collect cash directly from clients
options.C: Hold client cash for up to 30 days before forwarding it
options.D: Deposit client cash into his own account and transfer it monthly

explanation: Clients expect proper handling of money, which means the representative should not collect cash directly from clients; premiums should flow to the insurer. Holding or banking client cash personally creates obvious risks and conflicts.

stem: Under s.27(1) FAA, a representative may act for more than one principal only if:

options.A: He obtains MAS approval each calendar year
options.B: Both principals give verbal consent
options.C: The principals are related corporations
options.D: He limits himself to two principals

explanation: The one-principal rule allows an exception only where the principals are related corporations. The rule exists to ensure close supervision and clarity of responsibility for the representative's conduct.

stem: The one-principal rule for representatives exists mainly to achieve:

options.A: Close supervision of the representative and clarity of responsibility for his conduct
options.B: Higher commissions for the principal
options.C: A wider product range for clients
options.D: Reduced training costs across the industry

explanation: The objectives of the one-principal rule are close supervision of the representative and clear allocation of responsibility for his conduct to a single principal.

stem: Under s.2(1) FAA, which person falls within the definition of a 'representative'?

options.A: Only a person who has completed at least ten advisory transactions
options.B: Only salaried employees of a bank
options.C: Only persons who hold a CMS licence in their own name
options.D: A person who acts as, or holds himself out as, a representative in respect of a financial advisory service

explanation: The definition covers a person acting as a representative in respect of any financial advisory service or holding himself out as doing so. Actually completing transactions, employment structure or holding one's own licence are not the tests.

stem: Which of the following is one of the LIA's stated core values?

options.A: Profitable
options.B: Proactive
options.C: Competitive
options.D: Aggressive

explanation: The LIA core values are Unified, Professional, Ethical, Fair, Open and honest, and Proactive. Profitability, competitiveness and aggressiveness are not among them.

stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven principles of ethical behaviour?

options.A: Objectivity
options.B: Confidentiality
options.C: Diligence
options.D: Profitability

explanation: The seven principles are Integrity, Objectivity, Competence, Fairness, Confidentiality, Professionalism and Diligence. Profitability is a business goal, not an ethical principle.

stem: The word 'integrity' derives from the Latin 'integer', which means:

options.A: Truthful in speech
options.B: Obedient to authority
options.C: Whole, entire and undiminished
options.D: Free from debt

explanation: 'Integer' means whole, entire and undiminished, so integrity denotes wholeness and consistency of character in public and private dealings, not merely truthful speech.

stem: A representative researches only articles that support the fund he already intends to recommend and ignores contrary data. This illustrates:

options.A: Confirmation bias
options.B: The Golden Rule
options.C: Due diligence
options.D: Twisting

explanation: Noticing or seeking only information that confirms an existing belief is confirmation bias, a cognitive bias that undermines objectivity. It differs from a conflict of interest, which arises from misaligned incentives.

stem: The two main obstacles to objectivity identified in the text are:

options.A: Poor grammar and inadequate training
options.B: Cognitive bias and conflict of interest
options.C: Low pay and long hours
options.D: Client ignorance and market volatility

explanation: Objectivity is undermined by cognitive bias - notably confirmation bias - and by conflicts of interest. Both distort advice away from the facts and the client's actual circumstances.

stem: A client asks his insurance representative for detailed tax structuring advice outside the representative's expertise. The competent and ethical response is to:

options.A: Give his best guess to preserve the relationship
options.B: Decline to help and end the relationship
options.C: Charge a higher fee for the extra work
options.D: Act only within his own expertise and refer the client to a suitable expert

explanation: Competence requires acting only within one's own expertise and referring the client to other experts for matters outside it. Guessing breaches competence; refusing all help serves the client poorly.

stem: The principle of fairness includes treating:

options.A: All clients identically regardless of circumstances
options.B: Only paying clients with respect
options.C: Like things in like ways and giving each party what is due
options.D: The largest clients first

explanation: Fairness means treating like things in like ways, applying the Golden Rule, and giving each party what is due - across clients, the principal, colleagues and the industry. Identical treatment of unlike situations is not fairness.

stem: Under the PDPA 2012, an organisation that breaches data protection obligations faces a financial penalty of up to:

options.A: S$1 million or 10% of gross annual Singapore turnover, whichever is higher
options.B: S$5,000 per breach
options.C: S$100,000 in total
options.D: 2 years' suspension of business

explanation: Organisations face penalties of up to S$1 million or 10% of gross annual Singapore turnover, whichever is higher. The fine of up to S$5,000 and/or up to 2 years' jail applies to individuals, not organisations.

stem: The classic failure of diligence described in the text is:

options.A: Referring clients to other experts
options.B: Over promising and under delivering
options.C: Documenting recommendations too thoroughly
options.D: Responding to clients too quickly

explanation: Diligence demands prompt, thorough service with painstaking due care - the opposite of over promising and under delivering. Thorough documentation and quick responses are diligence in action, not failures.

stem: Churning is best described as:

options.A: Recommending a diversified portfolio review each year
options.B: Selling policies below the market premium
options.C: Advising a client to hold his policies to maturity
options.D: Inducing a client to terminate policies after a short period and switch to similar products for fresh commissions

explanation: Churning is getting the client to drop policies early and buy similar replacements, generating commissions for the representative with no real benefit to the client. Annual reviews and holding to maturity are legitimate practices.

stem: In the Straits Times case of 5 Oct 2015 cited in the text, the key sign of unethical selling was that the divorcee was sold a policy whose:

options.A: Annual premium of about S$40,000 exceeded her annual income
options.B: Sum assured was below S$10,000
options.C: Term exceeded 100 years
options.D: Premiums were payable only in foreign currency

explanation: After depositing about S$350,000 in divorce settlement money, the client was sold a policy with an annual premium of about S$40,000 - more than her annual income - a plainly unaffordable and unsuitable sale.

stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the four obstacles to ethical decision making?

options.A: Corrupted character
options.B: Giving in to temptation
options.C: Excessive government regulation
options.D: Rationalization

explanation: The four obstacles are corrupted character, lack of moral perception, giving in to temptation, and rationalization. Regulation is external to the individual's decision making and is not one of the obstacles.

stem: A representative genuinely does not notice that recommending a product for its higher commission raises any ethical issue at all. This obstacle is called:

options.A: Corrupted character
options.B: Lack of moral perception
options.C: Giving in to temptation
options.D: Peer pressure

explanation: Lack of moral perception is failing to recognise that a situation even involves an ethical issue. It differs from seeing the issue and yielding to temptation, and from a settled corrupted character.

stem: Telling oneself 'the client is wealthy, he can afford the loss' before making an unsuitable sale is an example of:

options.A: Needs analysis
options.B: Objectivity
options.C: Fair dealing
options.D: Rationalization

explanation: Constructing a plausible-sounding excuse to justify unethical conduct is rationalization. It lets the person act wrongly while preserving his self-image, but does not change the wrongness of the act.

stem: In a churning transaction, who typically benefits and who typically loses?

options.A: The representative gains commissions while the client gains no real benefit and often suffers loss
options.B: The client gains better coverage while the representative earns nothing
options.C: Both parties benefit equally from the replacement
options.D: The insurer profits while both representative and client lose

explanation: Churning generates fresh commissions for the representative, while the client incurs new charges and surrender losses for a product no better than the one terminated.

stem: A practice is unethical but does not breach any statute. How should a representative treat it?

options.A: It is still a breach of ethics, because unethical behaviour is broader than illegal behaviour
options.B: It is acceptable if the client does not object
options.C: It is acceptable if the supervisor approves it
options.D: It is acceptable, since only illegal conduct carries consequences

explanation: Unethical behaviour is broader than illegal behaviour. Many of the listed practices may never attract prosecution yet still breach the ethical standards expected of a representative.

stem: Which of the following areas is covered by the listed types of unethical behaviour by representatives?

options.A: Choosing not to pursue further qualifications
options.B: Improper handling of client money and documents
options.C: Failing to meet an annual sales target
options.D: Declining to service a low-value client

explanation: The listed unethical behaviours span misrepresentation of products, unsuitable recommendations, improper handling of client money and documents, and placing personal interest above the client's.

stem: The text distinguishes two types of conflict of interest. They are conflicts that a representative:

options.A: Discloses and conflicts that he conceals
options.B: Has with clients and conflicts he has with MAS
options.C: Finds himself in (built into the arrangement) and conflicts he creates through his own actions
options.D: Can insure against and conflicts he cannot

explanation: A conflict may be built into the business arrangement the representative finds himself in, or it may be created by his own actions. Disclosure is a way of managing conflicts, not a way of classifying them.

stem: Which of the following is one of the five misalignments of interests identified in the text?

options.A: Between MAS and the courts
options.B: Between the financial institution and multiple clients
options.C: Between two unrelated insurers
options.D: Between the client and his own family

explanation: The five misalignments are: representative vs client; institution-representative-client; institution vs client; representative vs multiple clients; and institution vs multiple clients. Regulators, courts and family members are not parties in this framework.

stem: Involuntary cross-selling occurs when a client:

options.A: Must buy a bundled product he does not want in order to obtain the product he does want, or is placed into a disadvantageous default option
options.B: Voluntarily buys two products after comparing alternatives
options.C: Asks the representative to recommend an additional product
options.D: Buys the same product from two different insurers

explanation: The two forms of involuntary cross-selling are forced bundling and disadvantageous defaults. Cross-selling that the client freely chooses after comparison is legitimate.

stem: A representative persuades a client to surrender an existing policy and buy a similar one from a DIFFERENT insurer, mainly to earn commissions. This practice is called:

options.A: Churning
options.B: Hawking
options.C: Cross-selling
options.D: Twisting

explanation: Replacement with a policy from another insurer is twisting; replacement with a policy from the same insurer is churning. Both are commission-driven abuses of the client's trust.

stem: The feature that distinguishes churning from twisting is:

options.A: The size of the sum assured
options.B: Whether the client signed a consent form
options.C: Whether the replacement policy comes from the same insurer or another insurer
options.D: Whether the policy is participating or non-participating

explanation: Churning replaces a policy with one from the same insurer, while twisting replaces it with one from another insurer. The commission motive and harm to the client are common to both.

stem: The 'vanished premiums' problem in life insurance illustrations led the NAIC to issue its Life Insurance Illustrations Model Regulation in:
explanation: The NAIC issued the Life Insurance Illustrations Model Regulation in 1995 to curb misleading projections, after policies marketed on the promise that premiums would 'vanish' failed to perform as illustrated.

stem: The duties owed under the fiduciary standard are:

options.A: Care, Loyalty, Obedience and Good Faith
options.B: Speed, Accuracy, Volume and Profit
options.C: Disclosure, Documentation, Diligence and Delivery
options.D: Know your client, needs analysis, documentation and review

explanation: The fiduciary standard is principles-based and requires acting in the client's best interest through the duties of Care, Loyalty, Obedience and Good Faith. Know your client, needs analysis and documentation belong to the rules-based suitability regime under FAA-N16.

stem: The requirement to have a reasonable basis for recommendations is found in:

options.A: Section 27 FAA
options.B: Section 230 SFA
options.C: Section 309 SFA
options.D: Section 36 FAA

explanation: Section 36 FAA requires a reasonable basis for recommendations, supported by FAA-N16's requirements of knowing your client, needs analysis and documentation. Section 27 FAA is the one-principal rule, and ss.230 and 309 SFA deal with insider trading defences and hawking.

stem: Under the suitability regime, a Customer Knowledge Assessment (CKA) is required before a retail client transacts in:

options.A: Any life insurance policy
options.B: Listed Specified Investment Products
options.C: Unlisted Specified Investment Products
options.D: Singapore Government Securities

explanation: The CKA applies to unlisted Specified Investment Products, while a Customer Account Review applies to listed SIPs. Plain life policies and government securities do not trigger the CKA.

stem: Why is a 'suitable' recommendation not necessarily in the client's best interest?

options.A: Suitability only applies to clients above age 62
options.B: Several products may all be suitable, and the representative could pick the one paying him the highest commission
options.C: Suitability is judged only after the policy matures
options.D: Best interest and suitability are legally identical standards

explanation: The suitability standard is satisfied by any product that fits the client's needs and profile, so a representative can meet it while still choosing the suitable product that pays him the most. The fiduciary best-interest standard demands more.

stem: Which of the following is one of the six manifestations of conflict of interest?

options.A: A change in the product provider's fund manager
options.B: Delay in issuing a policy document by the insurer
options.C: Failure to execute a client's instruction
options.D: An error in the client's contact particulars

explanation: The six manifestations are biased advice, involuntary cross-selling, excessive trading through churning and twisting, failure to execute, insufficient or misleading disclosure, and violation of privacy or confidentiality. Failure to execute is a conflict manifestation, not merely poor service.

stem: A representative repeatedly switches a client between similar policies to generate fresh commission. Which manifestation of conflict of interest is this?

options.A: Insufficient or misleading disclosure
options.B: Involuntary cross-selling
options.C: Violation of privacy or confidentiality
options.D: Excessive trading, through churning and twisting

explanation: Repeated switching to generate commission is excessive trading, described as churning and twisting, and is one of the six manifestations of conflict of interest.

stem: What does dealing fairly with clients mean?

options.A: Treating each client appropriately according to his circumstances
options.B: Giving every client the same product recommendation
options.C: Charging every client the same fee
options.D: Treating every client identically regardless of circumstances

explanation: Fair does not mean equal. Fair treatment can legitimately differ between clients, and identical treatment of clients with different needs can itself be unfair.

stem: An adviser recommends the identical portfolio to a 25-year-old with no dependants and a 60-year-old nearing retirement, on the basis that treating them the same is fair. Is this correct?

options.A: Yes, provided both clients consent
options.B: No, identical treatment of clients with different needs can itself be unfair
options.C: Yes, provided the portfolio is a balanced one
options.D: Yes, uniform treatment is the essence of fair dealing

explanation: Fair dealing requires treatment appropriate to each client's circumstances. Applying one recommendation to two very different profiles is not fair dealing.

stem: Which of the following is one of the three core fair dealing principles?

options.A: Standardising commission rates across the industry
options.B: Maximising client returns
options.C: Management of conflicts of interest, including third-party compensation
options.D: Minimising the number of products offered

explanation: The three core principles are clear allocation of roles and responsibilities, transparency, and management of conflicts of interest including third-party compensation.

stem: A firm discloses every conflict of interest in writing but takes no steps to manage them. Does this amount to fair dealing?

options.A: Yes, provided clients acknowledge the disclosures
options.B: Yes, provided the conflicts are immaterial
options.C: Yes, disclosure discharges the obligation
options.D: No, transparency is only one of three principles and conflicts must also be managed

explanation: Transparency is one of three principles. Disclosure alone, without clear allocation of responsibilities and active management of conflicts, does not amount to fair dealing.

stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the six key areas of product transparency?

options.A: The representative's ranking in the sales league table
options.B: Features and special features
options.C: Performance and benefit
options.D: Fees and charges

explanation: The six areas are features, performance, benefit, risk, fees and charges, and special features. The representative's own sales targets or league position is not one of them.

stem: Under MAS Guidelines FAA-G11 on Fair Dealing, where does responsibility for delivering fair dealing outcomes sit?

options.A: With MAS as the supervisor
options.B: With the Board and Senior Management of the financial institution
options.C: With front-line representatives alone
options.D: With the compliance officer alone

explanation: FAA-G11 places responsibility for delivering fair dealing outcomes squarely on the Board and Senior Management, not only on front-line staff.

stem: Which of the following is one of the five fair dealing outcomes?

options.A: Fees are the lowest in the market
options.B: Clients achieve positive investment returns
options.C: Products offered are suitable for the target client segments
options.D: Representatives meet their sales targets

explanation: The five outcomes are that fair dealing is central to the corporate culture, that products are suitable for the target client segments, that representatives are competent and give quality advice, that clients receive clear, relevant and timely information, and that complaints are handled independently, effectively and promptly.

stem: A firm resolves complaints quickly, but they are handled by the same sales manager who supervised the sale. Which fair dealing outcome is not met?

options.A: Outcome 1, on corporate culture
options.B: Outcome 2, on product suitability
options.C: Outcome 4, on clear and timely information
options.D: Outcome 5, which requires complaints handling that is independent, effective and prompt

explanation: Outcome 5 requires all three qualities. Speed alone does not satisfy it where the handling lacks independence from the sale.

stem: Which of the following is a compulsory step in an ethically sound sales process?

options.A: Explaining the downside risk of the product
options.B: Comparing the product against every competitor's offering
options.C: Providing a written performance projection
options.D: Arranging a meeting with the product manufacturer

explanation: The six steps are gaining the client's attention, explaining the product structure, explaining the downside risk, clarifying the coverage components, explaining who bears the risk, and complying with all applicable rules. Downside risk is compulsory, not an optional extra.

stem: In a participating or investment-linked policy, who bears the risk of the non-guaranteed bonuses and investment returns?

options.A: The insurer
options.B: The client
options.C: The distributor
options.D: The risk is shared equally

explanation: The client bears the risk of non-guaranteed elements such as bonuses and investment returns. The insurer bears the risk of the guaranteed benefits.

stem: A representative tells a client that the projected bonuses on a participating policy are 'as safe as the guaranteed benefits because the insurer stands behind both'. Why is this wrong?

options.A: Because the insurer does not stand behind guaranteed benefits either
options.B: Because bonuses are guaranteed only after ten years
options.C: Because the client, not the insurer, bears the risk on non-guaranteed elements
options.D: Because bonuses are guaranteed by a government scheme

explanation: The insurer bears the risk on guaranteed benefits only. Non-guaranteed bonuses and investment returns are at the client's risk, and presenting them otherwise misstates who bears the risk.

stem: Which of the following is one of the three main pitfalls in the sales process?

options.A: Creating unrealistic expectations of returns
options.B: Using bogus qualifications
options.C: Scare tactics
options.D: Recommending unsuitable products

explanation: The three sales pitfalls are misrepresentation, recommending unsuitable products, and conflict of interest. Bogus qualifications, scare tactics and unrealistic expectations belong to the separate list of marketing pitfalls.

stem: What distinguishes fraud from misrepresentation?

options.A: Fraud requires intentional deception, while misrepresentation can be unintentional, negligent or arise from an omission
options.B: Fraud involves money, while misrepresentation involves only words
options.C: Fraud is civil while misrepresentation is criminal
options.D: There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable

explanation: Intent is the dividing line. A false statement made carelessly is still misrepresentation and can attract liability even without any intention to deceive.

stem: A representative omits to mention a policy exclusion, genuinely believing it to be unimportant. What is the position?

options.A: No liability arises, as there was no intention to deceive
options.B: It may still amount to misrepresentation, since an omission can give rise to liability
options.C: It amounts to fraud, since the exclusion was material
options.D: Liability arises only if the client later claims under the exclusion

explanation: Misrepresentation can arise from an omission and does not require intent. The absence of an intention to deceive prevents it from being fraud, but it does not remove liability.

stem: Which of Holley's information disclosure strategies corresponds to caveat emptor?

options.A: The Mutual Benefit Rule
options.B: The Maximal Information Rule
options.C: Minimal Information
options.D: The Fairness Rule

explanation: Minimal Information corresponds to caveat emptor, or buyer beware. The five strategies run from Minimal Information through Modified Minimal Information, the Fairness Rule and the Mutual Benefit Rule to the Maximal Information Rule.

stem: Which of Holley's strategies involves disclosing the most information to the client?

options.A: Modified Minimal Information
options.B: The Fairness Rule
options.C: The Mutual Benefit Rule
options.D: The Maximal Information Rule

explanation: The Maximal Information Rule discloses the most. The text suggests going further still with a Mutual Benefit Rule Plus.

stem: How must a conflict of interest be disclosed under MAS Notice FAA-N03?

options.A: In writing to the client
options.B: Only if the client asks
options.C: By notification to MAS rather than the client
options.D: Verbally at the point of sale

explanation: FAA-N03 requires written disclosure to clients, covering conflicts of interest, the representative's status and remuneration, and product information. A verbal mention is not sufficient.

stem: Which of the following is a marketing pitfall rather than a sales pitfall?

options.A: Conflict of interest
options.B: Using bogus qualifications or designations
options.C: Misrepresentation
options.D: Recommending an unsuitable product

explanation: The three marketing pitfalls are bogus qualifications or designations, scare tactics such as doomsday examples, and creating unrealistic expectations of returns or benefits.

stem: A representative explains that a critical illness could cost a client his savings, using published treatment cost data. Is this a scare tactic?

options.A: Yes, unless a doctor is present
options.B: Yes, any discussion of illness costs is a scare tactic
options.C: No, presenting realistic risk information is not a scare tactic
options.D: Yes, unless the client asked about critical illness first

explanation: Scare tactics involve exaggerated doomsday scenarios. Presenting realistic, evidenced risk information is a legitimate part of explaining a need.

stem: Under item 3.3 of the LIA Code of Life Insurance Practice, within what period should a new policy document be delivered to the policyholder?

options.A: Within 30 days from the client's first premium payment
options.B: Within 3 months from policy issuance
options.C: Within 14 days from policy issuance
options.D: Within 30 days from policy issuance

explanation: Delivery should occur within 30 days from policy issuance. The duty comes from the LIA Code rather than from the FAA, and the period runs from issuance rather than from payment.

stem: What distinguishes persuasion from coercion?

options.A: Persuasion gives reasons and respects the client's freedom to choose, while coercion pressures or threatens the client into a decision
options.B: Persuasion is used with new clients and coercion with existing ones
options.C: Persuasion is verbal while coercion is written
options.D: There is no meaningful difference in a sales context

explanation: The dividing line is the client's freedom to say no. Persuasion is a legitimate interacting skill; remove that freedom and it becomes coercion, which is unethical.

stem: A client telephones angrily about a policy he feels was mis-sold. What should the representative do first?

options.A: Determine the facts by reviewing the file
options.B: Recognise the client's feelings
options.C: Propose a solution immediately
options.D: Refer the client to the complaints department

explanation: The four steps run in order: recognise the client's feelings, empathise and apologise, determine the facts, and find a solution. Jumping straight to the facts is the classic mistake.

stem: Which sequence correctly describes the four steps for handling a conflict with a client?

options.A: Determine facts, recognise feelings, empathise, find a solution
options.B: Find a solution, determine facts, empathise, recognise feelings
options.C: Recognise feelings, empathise and apologise, determine the facts, find a solution
options.D: Empathise, find a solution, recognise feelings, determine the facts

explanation: Feelings are addressed first, then the facts, then the solution. The order matters because a client who does not feel heard will not engage with the facts.

stem: Which of the following counts as a complaint?

options.A: Only a complaint escalated to a supervisor
options.B: Only a written expression of dissatisfaction
options.C: Only a justified expression of dissatisfaction
options.D: Any oral or written expression of dissatisfaction, whether justified or not

explanation: A complaint need not be in writing and need not be justified. Every complaint should be taken seriously and handled through a problem-solving approach.

stem: At what intervals should reviews be conducted after a sale?

options.A: At 3 months, 12 months and 18 months
options.B: At 6 months and annually thereafter
options.C: Only at the policy anniversary each year
options.D: At 1 month, 6 months and 12 months

explanation: Reviews should be conducted at around 3 months, 12 months and 18 months, and should be carried out by a qualified representative.

stem: A representative arranges for the client service office to conduct all post-sale reviews on his behalf. Is this acceptable?

options.A: Yes, provided the client is informed
options.B: No, the reviews should be carried out by a qualified representative
options.C: Yes, for clients with policies below a certain sum assured
options.D: Yes, provided the office keeps records

explanation: Post-sale reviews are the representative's job. Routing them to the client service office does not discharge the duty.

stem: According to Dr Thomas Gordon, what are the conditions for good listening?

options.A: Note-taking, questioning and summarising
options.B: Authority, confidence and persistence
options.C: Acceptance, empathy and genuineness
options.D: Agreement, patience and silence

explanation: Gordon identified acceptance, empathy and genuineness on the part of the listener. Agreement with the speaker is not among them.

stem: What is the prime objective of fact-finding and needs analysis?

options.A: To confirm the client's ability to pay premiums
options.B: To document the client's investment risk profile
options.C: To identify the products the client is most likely to buy
options.D: To identify needs, quantify the total amount required for each, take stock of existing provisions, and establish the shortfall

explanation: The objective runs from identifying needs, through quantifying each need and taking stock of existing provisions, to establishing the shortfall that remains to be covered.

stem: A client needs S$800,000 of death cover and already holds S$500,000 of in-force term insurance. What shortfall should the recommendation address?
explanation: Existing provisions must be deducted from the quantified need, giving S$800,000 less S$500,000 = S$300,000. Recommending the full quantified need would double-count cover the client already has.

stem: Which three requirements does MAS Notice FAA-N16 impose on the advisory process?

options.A: Client identification, risk profiling and portfolio rebalancing
options.B: Know your client, needs analysis, and documentation of the basis of recommendations
options.C: Disclosure of remuneration, product information and conflicts of interest
options.D: Fact-finding, product comparison and post-sale review

explanation: FAA-N16 governs the advisory process through know your client, needs analysis and documentation of the basis of recommendations. Disclosure to clients is dealt with in FAA-N03.

stem: Which product is excluded from the LIA Minimum Standard for the Life Insurance Advisory Process under circular MU 20/15?

options.A: Whole life policies
options.B: Investment-linked policies
options.C: Personal accident insurance
options.D: Critical illness policies

explanation: MU 20/15 applies to life policies and accident and health policies, but personal accident insurance is excluded. The standard was effective no later than 1 April 2015.

stem: Which of the following is a formal section of the prescribed Advisory Form?

options.A: The insurer's underwriting decision
options.B: The representative's commission schedule
options.C: The client's medical report
options.D: The supervisor's review

explanation: The Advisory Form covers general information, know your client, needs analysis, recommendations, replacement of policy, declarations, and the supervisor's review. The supervisor's review is a formal section, not an optional internal step.

stem: A client is 65 years old, proficient in spoken and written English, and educated to university level. Must he be accompanied by a Trusted Individual?

options.A: No, because he meets only one of the three criteria
options.B: Yes, because age alone is decisive
options.C: No, because a Trusted Individual is never mandatory
options.D: Yes, because he is aged 62 or above

explanation: A Trusted Individual is required where the client meets any two of the three criteria: aged 62 or above, not proficient in spoken or written English, and educated to secondary level or below. Meeting one criterion alone does not trigger the requirement.

stem: Which of the following disqualifies a person from acting as a Trusted Individual?

options.A: Being employed outside the financial industry
options.B: Being aged 17
options.C: Holding a GCE O Level certificate
options.D: Being a friend rather than a relative of the client

explanation: The Trusted Individual must be at least 18, educated to at least GCE N or O Level, proficient in English, and trusted by the client. There is no requirement to be a relative.

stem: Under the common planning rules of thumb, up to what ages is support typically provided for children?

options.A: Age 18 for both sons and daughters
options.B: Age 21 for both sons and daughters
options.C: Age 25 for sons and age 22 for daughters
options.D: Age 22 for sons and age 25 for daughters

explanation: The rule of thumb supports sons up to age 25 and daughters up to age 22. The two ages differ, and the separate 8-year rule of thumb applies to dependent parents.

stem: Which life expectancy assumptions are commonly used in needs quantification?

options.A: 75 for females and 80 for males
options.B: 85 for both
options.C: 70 for both
options.D: 80 for females and 75 for males

explanation: The common planning assumptions are a life expectancy of 80 for females and 75 for males, alongside a rule of thumb of about 8 years of support for dependent parents.

stem: How many of the Customer Knowledge Assessment criteria must a client satisfy to pass?

options.A: Any one of the three
options.B: Any two of the three
options.C: All three
options.D: At least two, unless the client is over 62

explanation: Passing requires only one of the three criteria: a diploma or higher qualification in a listed relevant field, at least 6 transactions in collective investment schemes or ILPs in the last 3 years, or at least 3 consecutive years of relevant working experience in the past 10 years.

stem: When must Section 4a of the Advisory Form, on the Investment Risk Profile, be completed?

options.A: For every client, without exception
options.B: For products with a cash value
options.C: Only for clients who fail the Customer Knowledge Assessment
options.D: Only for clients aged 62 or above

explanation: Section 4a on the Investment Risk Profile must be completed for products with a cash value.

stem: To roughly what proportion of income is disability income cover typically limited?

options.A: 100 percent
options.B: About 50 percent
options.C: About 75 percent
options.D: About 90 percent

explanation: Disability income insurance typically replaces about 75 percent of income rather than the full amount, so that the incentive to return to work is preserved.

stem: A client has assets of S$180,000 and liabilities of S$215,000. What does this indicate?

options.A: A neutral position, since liabilities are long term
options.B: A net asset position of S$395,000
options.C: A net asset position of S$35,000
options.D: A negative net asset position, meaning the client is effectively bankrupt

explanation: Net asset position equals assets minus liabilities, here S$180,000 less S$215,000 = negative S$35,000. A negative figure means the client is effectively bankrupt.

stem: Which of the following is one of the seven areas covered in fact-finding?

options.A: The client's existing insurance
options.B: The client's credit card spending by merchant
options.C: The client's preferred insurer
options.D: The client's political affiliation

explanation: The seven areas are life stage, employment, dependants, financial position, existing insurance, investment profile and priorities.

stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes the balance sheet from the income statement?

options.A: Both are point-in-time statements prepared on the same date
options.B: The balance sheet records only cash movements while the income statement records only accruals
options.C: The balance sheet covers a period while the income statement is a point-in-time snapshot
options.D: The balance sheet shows assets, liabilities and net worth at a specific point in time while the income statement shows income against expenditure over a period

explanation: The statement of net worth is a snapshot at a specific date. The statement of cash flows covers a period, usually one year. Reversing the two is a classic error.

stem: A client buys an antique car purely in the expectation that it will appreciate in value. How should it be classified?

options.A: An investment asset, because it is held for capital gain
options.B: It is excluded from the balance sheet entirely
options.C: A personal asset, because cars are for consumption
options.D: A liquid asset, because it can be sold at auction

explanation: Classification depends on why the asset was acquired and how it will be used. Held for capital gain, the antique car is an investment asset, even though a car used for daily transport would be a personal asset.

stem: A client holds a money market fund that he has earmarked for retirement in 20 years. How is it best classified?

options.A: A liquid asset, because money market funds are near-cash
options.B: An investment asset, because it is held for a long-term objective
options.C: A personal asset, because it is for his own future consumption
options.D: A liability, because it is committed to a future purpose

explanation: Intention governs classification. A money market fund kept for retirement is an investment asset rather than a liquid asset, even though the instrument itself is near-cash.

stem: A self-employed client with irregular income asks how large his emergency fund should be. What does the text recommend?

options.A: 3 months of expenses
options.B: 6 months of expenses
options.C: 12 months of expenses
options.D: 24 months of expenses

explanation: The standard guideline is at least 3 to 6 months of expenses, but a person with irregular income should aim for 12 months.

stem: A freelance designer has monthly expenses of S$3,500 and irregular income. Applying the guideline for irregular income earners, what emergency fund should she target?
explanation: Irregular income calls for 12 months of expenses. 12 x S$3,500 = S$42,000. The figure of S$10,500 reflects 3 months and S$21,000 reflects 6 months, which are the standard rather than the irregular-income guideline.

stem: A client pays a monthly mortgage instalment of S$2,000, of which S$1,400 is interest and S$600 is principal. By how much does the reported liability fall this month?

options.B: It does not change until the loan is fully repaid

explanation: Liabilities are reported at outstanding principal, so only the S$600 principal portion reduces the liability. The S$1,400 interest is an expense in the income statement and does not reduce the balance owed.

stem: How should assets be reported on a statement of net worth?

options.A: Always at original cost, for consistency
options.B: At current fair market value, though hard-to-value assets may conservatively be shown at original cost
options.C: At insured replacement value
options.D: At the value net of any related loan

explanation: Assets are reported at current fair market value. Where an asset is hard to value, showing it conservatively at original cost is acceptable. Related loans appear separately as liabilities rather than being netted off.

stem: A client has total assets of S$310,000 and total liabilities of S$131,000. What is his net worth?
explanation: Net worth = total assets - total liabilities = S$310,000 - S$131,000 = S$179,000. Adding the two figures instead of subtracting gives S$441,000, which is a common slip.

stem: A client owns a S$1.2 million condominium and drives a S$300,000 car, but owes S$1.45 million across his mortgage and car loan. What does this illustrate?

options.A: That personal assets should be excluded from net worth
options.B: That liabilities are only counted once they fall into arrears
options.C: That expensive assets always indicate high net worth
options.D: That a person with expensive assets can still have a low net worth if heavily geared

explanation: Net worth here is S$1,500,000 - S$1,450,000 = S$50,000. Expensive assets say nothing about net worth until the liabilities against them are deducted.

stem: A client's annual inflows are S$90,000 and outflows are S$78,000. What is his net cash flow, and what does it mean?

options.A: A surplus of S$12,000, though its disposition is reflected in assets, liabilities and net worth
options.B: A surplus of S$168,000
options.C: A deficit of S$12,000 requiring immediate borrowing
options.D: A surplus of S$12,000 that is necessarily available as spendable cash

explanation: Net cash flow = S$90,000 - S$78,000 = S$12,000, a surplus. A surplus is not automatically spendable cash, because it may already have been directed into savings, investments or debt repayment.

stem: What can a cash surplus be used for?

options.A: Only additional consumption
options.B: Savings, investments or debt reduction
options.C: Only repayment of debt, as a matter of prudence
options.D: Nothing, because it is an accounting figure with no practical use

explanation: A surplus can fund savings, investments or debt reduction. Where it went is reflected in the assets, liabilities and net worth on the balance sheet.

stem: A client holds liquid assets of S$24,000 and has monthly expenses of S$4,000. What is his liquidity ratio?

options.B: 4 months
options.C: 6 months
options.D: 0.17 months

explanation: Liquidity ratio = liquid assets / monthly expenses = S$24,000 / S$4,000 = 6 months, which sits at the top of the 3 to 6 month guideline. The ratio is expressed in months, not as a percentage.

stem: A client has liquid assets of S$30,000 and net worth of S$150,000. What is his liquid assets to net worth ratio, and does it meet the guideline?

options.A: 20%, which fails the at-least-50% guideline
options.B: 15%, which exactly meets the guideline
options.C: 5 months, which meets the guideline
options.D: 20%, which meets the at-least-15% guideline

explanation: S$30,000 / S$150,000 = 0.20, or 20%. The guideline for this ratio is at least 15%, so it is met. The 50% guideline belongs to the investment assets to net worth ratio.

stem: A client saves and invests S$9,600 out of a total income of S$96,000. What is his savings ratio and how does it compare with the guideline?

options.A: 10%, exactly at the minimum guideline
options.B: 10%, below the minimum guideline of 15%
options.C: 9.6%, below the minimum guideline
options.D: S$9,600, which cannot be expressed as a ratio

explanation: Savings ratio = savings and investments / total income = S$9,600 / S$96,000 = 10%, which meets the guideline of at least 10%.

stem: A client has total liabilities of S$220,000 and total assets of S$400,000. What is his debt-to-asset ratio and does it meet the guideline?

options.A: 55%, which meets the guideline of at most 50%
options.B: 55%, which exceeds the guideline of at most 50%
options.C: 45%, which meets the guideline
options.D: 182%, which exceeds the guideline

explanation: S$220,000 / S$400,000 = 0.55, or 55%. The guideline is at most 50%, so this client is more geared than the benchmark suggests he should be.

stem: A client makes annual loan payments of S$21,000 against annual take-home pay of S$60,000. What is his debt service ratio?

options.A: 2.9 times, indicating insolvency
options.B: 28.6%, comfortably within the guideline
options.C: 35%, exactly at the guideline maximum
options.D: 35%, exceeding the guideline maximum of 30%

explanation: Debt service ratio = annual loan payments / annual take-home pay = S$21,000 / S$60,000 = 35%, which is exactly the guideline maximum. Note the denominator is take-home pay, not gross income and not total assets.

stem: Which figure belongs in the denominator of the debt service ratio?

options.A: Monthly expenses
options.B: Total assets
options.C: Total liabilities
options.D: Annual take-home pay

explanation: The debt service ratio puts annual loan payments over annual take-home pay. Putting liabilities over assets gives the debt-to-asset ratio instead, which is a different measure.

stem: A client has investment assets of S$120,000 and net worth of S$200,000. What is his investment assets to net worth ratio and does it meet the guideline?

options.A: 60%, meeting the guideline of at least 50%
options.B: 60%, failing the guideline of at least 75%
options.C: 167%, meeting the guideline
options.D: 40%, failing the guideline

explanation: S$120,000 / S$200,000 = 60%, against a guideline of at least 50%. This ratio should increase as a person ages and accumulates toward retirement.

stem: A client has net worth of S$179,000 and total assets of S$310,000. What is his solvency ratio?
explanation: Solvency ratio = net worth / total assets = S$179,000 / S$310,000 = 0.577, or 57.7%. The figure of 42.3% is the debt-to-asset ratio, and the two necessarily sum to 100%.

stem: A client's debt-to-asset ratio is 42%. What is his solvency ratio?

options.D: It cannot be determined without the net worth figure

explanation: The solvency ratio is the complement of the debt-to-asset ratio, so the two sum to 100%. 100% - 42% = 58%, and no further information is needed.

stem: What does it mean when a client's liabilities exceed his assets?

options.A: His liquidity ratio must also be negative
options.B: His debt service ratio automatically exceeds 35%
options.C: His net worth is zero and his solvency ratio is 100%
options.D: His net worth is negative and he is technically insolvent

explanation: Where liabilities exceed assets, net worth is negative and the person is technically insolvent. The liquidity and debt service ratios measure different things and do not follow automatically.

stem: A financial adviser wants to know how much a client has accumulated as at 31 December. Which statement should he look at?

options.A: The balance sheet, because it is a point-in-time statement of net worth
options.B: Either, because both report the same information
options.C: Neither, because accumulation is measured only by the savings ratio
options.D: The income statement, because it summarises the year

explanation: Accumulation as at a specific date is a point-in-time question, which the balance sheet answers. The income statement would tell him about income against expenditure over the year instead.

stem: A client has no dependants, no debt and ample savings, but a whole life policy would suit his risk profile. What do the two basic principles of recommendation require?

options.A: Do not recommend it, because need comes first and he has no need for it
options.B: Recommend it with a reduced sum assured
