options.C: Recommend it only if he asks about life insurance
options.D: Recommend it, since it is suitable for his profile

explanation: The two principles are to recommend products only if the client needs them, and to recommend only the most suitable products given his circumstances. Need comes first, so even a suitable product should not be recommended where there is no need.

stem: Which of the following must a representative be able to explain as part of product knowledge?

options.A: The insurer's internal reinsurance arrangements
options.B: The 14-day free-look provision
options.C: The insurer's solvency ratio calculation
options.D: The actuarial reserving basis

explanation: The product knowledge checklist covers range, purpose, nature, cash value and bonuses, special features, benefit triggers, risks and who bears them, distribution costs and charges, duration of cover, premium terms, consequences of non-payment, the 14-day free-look provision, and medical and non-medical limits.

stem: Which of the following is a 'special feature' a representative should be able to explain?

options.A: The distributor's commission structure
options.B: The fund manager's remuneration
options.C: Convertibility and guaranteed renewability
options.D: The insurer's dividend policy to shareholders

explanation: Special features include matters such as convertibility and guaranteed renewability, which materially affect the value of the contract to the client.

stem: Why is insurance described as creating an immediate estate?

options.A: Because premiums are refunded on death
options.B: Because the policy can be sold immediately for its face value
options.C: Because the cash value equals the sum assured from inception
options.D: Because the full sum assured is payable on the insured event even if only one premium has been paid

explanation: Insurance pays the full sum assured from day one, whereas savings take time to accumulate and stop at death or disability. That is why insurance is the most suitable product for protection needs.

stem: How often should clients aged 55 or above review their insurance plans?

options.A: Every 2 to 3 years, to ensure they remain affordable
options.B: Every 5 years
options.C: Only when a claim arises
options.D: Every year without exception

explanation: Clients aged 55 or above should review their insurance plans every 2 to 3 years so that the plans remain affordable as circumstances change.

stem: What coverage does the Basic Financial Planning Guide recommend for death and total permanent disability, and for critical illness?

options.A: 10 times annual income for death and 5 times for critical illness
options.B: 9 times annual income for death and TPD, and 4 times annual income for critical illness
options.C: 4 times annual income for death and TPD, and 9 times annual income for critical illness
options.D: 5 times annual income for both

explanation: The multiples are 9 times annual income for death and total permanent disability, and 4 times annual income for standard critical illness. Reversing them is a common error.

stem: What cover does the Dependants' Protection Scheme provide?

options.A: A flat S$55,000 to age 70
options.B: Up to S$55,000 until age 60 and up to S$70,000 from above 60 to 65
options.C: Up to S$70,000 until age 60 and up to S$55,000 from above 60 to 65
options.D: A flat S$70,000 to age 65

explanation: DPS provides up to S$70,000 of cover until age 60 and up to S$55,000 from above 60 to 65. It is automatically extended to citizens and PRs aged 21 to 65 on their first CPF working contribution.

stem: A client earns S$5,000 a month before CPF, and S$4,000 after deducting his CPF contributions. Applying the affordability guide, what is the most he should spend on insurance protection?
explanation: The 15 percent cap is measured on income after deducting CPF contributions, so 15 percent of S$4,000 = S$600. Bundled products may exceed 15 percent as they contain both investment and protection elements.

stem: Applying the Guide, how much of income should be invested for retirement and other financial goals?

options.A: At least 10 percent
options.B: At least 15 percent
options.C: Exactly 15 percent
options.D: At most 10 percent

explanation: The Guide sets a floor of at least 10 percent of income for investing, alongside a ceiling of at most 15 percent for insurance protection. Both are measured on income after deducting CPF contributions.

stem: Who bears a cost when a policy lapses early?

options.A: Only the representative, who loses commissions
options.B: All three: the client, the representative and the insurer
options.C: Only the client, who loses cover and premiums
options.D: Only the insurer, which absorbs the initial costs

explanation: Early lapses hurt everyone. The client loses cover and premiums, the representative loses goodwill and commissions, and the insurer absorbs the initial costs.

stem: What is a rider?

options.A: A clause excluding certain risks from cover
options.B: A standalone policy sold alongside another policy
options.C: A special provision attached to a basic policy that adds benefits not in the basic contract
options.D: An endorsement that reduces the sum assured

explanation: A rider, or supplementary benefit, adds benefits to a basic policy. It cannot stand alone and must ride on a basic policy such as a term or whole life plan.

stem: Which of the following is a common rider?

options.A: Free-look provision
options.B: Grace period
options.C: Incontestability clause
options.D: Waiver of premium

explanation: Common riders include waiver of premium, TPD, critical illness, term, payor benefit, guaranteed insurability option, accidental death benefit, accidental death and dismemberment, and hospital cash benefit riders. The others listed are standard policy provisions rather than riders.

stem: A client with two young children cannot afford to address all his identified needs at once. What should generally be met first?

options.A: Protection needs
options.B: Investment for wealth accumulation
options.C: Legacy planning
options.D: Retirement savings

explanation: Where there are dependants, protection needs should generally be met first. The representative's role is to help the client prioritise rather than to sell everything at once.

stem: A young client wants permanent cover but cannot yet afford it. What is a suitable approach?

options.A: Recommend a smaller whole life policy that leaves a large protection gap
options.B: Recommend a convertible term policy that can be converted later when finances improve
options.C: Advise him to buy nothing until he can afford permanent cover
options.D: Recommend an investment-linked policy with minimum protection

explanation: A convertible term policy provides the cover now at a lower cost and allows conversion to permanent cover later, usually without fresh evidence of health.

stem: A client wants his CPF savings to pass to his sister on his death and has named her in his will. Is that sufficient?

options.A: No, CPF savings can only pass to a spouse or children
options.B: Yes, a will governs all assets including CPF savings
options.C: No, CPF savings are not distributed by will and require a separate CPF nomination
options.D: Yes, provided the will is registered with the CPF Board

explanation: CPF savings fall outside the estate distributed by will and require a separate CPF nomination. Legacy planning also covers a Lasting Power of Attorney and an Advance Care Plan.

stem: A client has failed the Customer Knowledge Assessment and, after repeated explanation, still cannot articulate the product's critical features. What should the adviser consider?

options.A: Recommending a different product from the same category
options.B: Proceeding with a smaller investment amount
options.C: Obtaining a signed waiver from the client
options.D: Aborting or declining the sale

explanation: Where the adviser doubts that the client understands critical product features, particularly a client who has failed the CKA, the right course is to consider aborting or declining the sale.

stem: With what should a systematic presentation of a recommendation begin?

options.A: The purpose of the product, meaning the need it meets
options.B: The projected returns
options.C: The insurer's financial strength rating
options.D: The premium payable

explanation: The presentation starts with the purpose of the product, then moves through its nature including tax position, risk elements, benefits and limitations, options, reasons for the recommendation, comparison against the Basic Financial Planning Guide, the policy illustration, distribution costs and charges, and the 14-day free-look provision.

stem: Which element of the policy illustration must be explained when presenting a recommendation?

options.A: Only the non-guaranteed benefits
options.B: Both the guaranteed and the non-guaranteed benefits
options.C: Neither, as the illustration speaks for itself
options.D: Only the guaranteed benefits

explanation: The policy illustration must be explained in terms of both guaranteed and non-guaranteed benefits, alongside disclosure of distribution costs and charges.

stem: A representative uses the term 'surrender value' in a presentation. What should he do?

options.A: Refer the client to the policy contract for the definition
options.B: Assume the client understands, as it is a common term
options.C: Explain the term, since common insurance terms still need explaining
options.D: Replace it with a technical actuarial definition

explanation: Products must be explained in language the client can comfortably understand. Where terms such as surrender value or bonuses are unavoidable, they must be explained, and understanding should be checked as the presentation proceeds.

stem: Which LIA publication provides a comprehensive list of insurance terms in simple language?

options.A: The Product Highlights Sheet
options.B: The Basic Financial Planning Guide
options.C: The Code of Life Insurance Practice
options.D: Your Guide to Life Insurance

explanation: LIA's Your Guide to Life Insurance provides a comprehensive list of insurance terms explained in simple language.

stem: A client is unsure whether a past medical consultation is a material fact. What should the representative advise?

options.A: Disclose it, since the default where materiality is doubtful is disclosure
options.B: Ask the insurer informally before deciding
options.C: Note it separately for the representative's own file only
options.D: Omit it, as minor consultations are rarely material

explanation: Where either party doubts whether a fact is material, the client should be advised to disclose it. He must also be warned that he or his beneficiaries might receive nothing under the policy if a material fact is not disclosed.

stem: Under the LIA Guidelines, which document comes first in the prescribed sequence given to a prospective buyer?

options.A: The Bundled Product Disclosure
options.B: The Cover Page
options.C: The Policy Illustration
options.D: The Product Summary

explanation: The sequence is the Cover Page, then the Policy Illustration, then the Product Summary, then the Bundled Product Disclosure, together with Your Guide to Life Insurance and Your Guide to Health Insurance as applicable.

stem: Where are distribution costs, including the commission payable to the representative, disclosed?

options.A: In the Product Summary
options.B: In the Product Highlights Sheet
options.C: In the Policy Illustration
options.D: In the Cover Page

explanation: Insurers must by law reveal all costs and charges, including distribution costs covering the representative's commission, and these are shown in the Policy Illustration rather than the Product Summary.

stem: For which product is a Product Highlights Sheet provided, and what does it describe?

options.A: For all life policies, describing the surrender values
options.B: For health insurance, describing the claims procedure
options.C: For term policies, describing the premium structure
options.D: For investment-linked policies, describing the key features and risks of the ILP sub-fund

explanation: The Product Highlights Sheet is provided for ILPs and describes the key features and risks of the ILP sub-fund. The Product Summary describes the features of the product being bought.

stem: Who signs the reference checklist at the end of the sales advisory process, and why?

options.A: The client, to verify he received the required information
options.B: The insurer's underwriter, to confirm acceptance
options.C: The representative, to confirm he gave the information
options.D: The supervisor, to confirm the file is complete

explanation: The client signs the reference checklist to verify that he received the FAA-N03 information, which covers general information about the representative and his status, remuneration, conflicts of interest, designated investment products, illustrations of past and future performance, and marketing materials.

stem: Which of the following is one of the four factors determining the timing and frequency of client reviews?

options.A: The representative's sales quota for the quarter
options.B: Product developments in the market
options.C: The insurer's financial year end
options.D: The client's payment method

explanation: The four factors are the client's personal circumstances, external developments, the products purchased by the client, and product developments in the market. New product launches are themselves a legitimate trigger for review.

stem: A client is due to retire in four months. When should the review ideally take place?

options.A: One year after retirement
options.B: Only if the client requests it
options.C: Just before retirement, so preparations can be made
options.D: Immediately after retirement, once the position is known

explanation: For retirement or redundancy, the review should ideally take place just before the event so that preparations can be made rather than reacting afterwards.

stem: Which of the following is a family change that should prompt a review?

options.A: The launch of a new long-term care product
options.B: A change in the insurer's bonus rates
options.C: A fall in equity markets
options.D: Taking on the care of an elderly parent

explanation: Family changes include marriage, birth, death of a spouse, inheritance, divorce and caring for an elderly parent. Bonus rates, market falls and product launches fall under external developments or product developments.

stem: Equity markets fall steeply. Why might this trigger a review for a client holding an investment-linked policy?

options.A: Because the underlying sub-funds may be equity-heavy
options.B: Because the free-look period reopens
options.C: Because the insurer must reissue the policy illustration
options.D: Because ILP premiums automatically increase after a market fall

explanation: A market fall triggers a review of ILPs because the underlying funds may be heavily invested in equities. Changes in CPF rules, such as contribution rates, are another external trigger.

stem: Why is it important to review a life policy that carries a conversion option?

options.A: Because conversion is compulsory at a set age
options.B: Because the option can usually be exercised without further evidence of health and is lost if forgotten
options.C: Because conversion always reduces the premium
options.D: Because the insurer will cancel the policy if the option is unused

explanation: Conversion options can usually be exercised without fresh evidence of health, which makes them valuable rights that lapse if overlooked. Policies written under trust should also be reviewed to keep beneficiaries current.

stem: What is the review trigger for an investment-linked policy?

options.A: Reassessment of the free-look period
options.B: Recalculation of the surrender charge
options.C: Possible fund switches, based on the fund performance report and policy statement
options.D: Annual renewal of the underwriting terms

explanation: ILPs should be reviewed for possible fund switches using the fund performance report and policy statement. Health insurance is reviewed at annual renewal and for adequacy of cover.

stem: Which new product development is described as offering protection against chronic ill health?

options.A: Convertible term insurance
options.B: Hospital cash benefit riders
options.C: Capital-guaranteed investment-linked policies
options.D: Long-term care insurance

explanation: Long-term care insurance offers protection against chronic ill health. Capital-guaranteed ILPs may suit clients who want to lock in returns while protecting the initial investment.

stem: What is the general position on replacement of insurance policies?

options.A: It should normally be discouraged, and any replacement recommendation should be acknowledged and agreed by the representative's supervisor
options.B: It requires MAS approval in every case
options.C: It is prohibited outright
options.D: It should be encouraged where a newer product exists

explanation: Replacement should normally be discouraged, and supervisor acknowledgement and agreement is required to mitigate unethical selling.

stem: Which of the following does a client lose or restart when an existing life policy is replaced?

options.A: Only the surrender value of the old policy
options.B: The incontestability clause, the waiting period and the suicide clause all re-set, and accumulated reversionary bonuses are lost
options.C: Only the accumulated reversionary bonus
options.D: Nothing, provided the new policy has the same sum assured

explanation: Replacement re-sets three clauses, being incontestability, the waiting period and the suicide clause, and the accumulated reversionary bonus of the replaced policy is lost. Replacement is rarely cost-free.

stem: Who launched the Basic Financial Planning Guide on 7 October 2023?

options.A: The CPF Board alone
options.B: The Life Insurance Association alone
options.C: MAS together with the Association of Banks in Singapore, the Association of Financial Advisers Singapore and the Life Insurance Association
options.D: MAS together with the CPF Board and the Ministry of Finance

explanation: The Guide was launched by MAS with ABS, AFAS and LIA. The CPF Board is not one of the launch partners. The Guide is publicly available on the MoneySense website and, from January 2024, comes in six customised formats for different life stages.

stem: Which pair correctly states the direction of the Guide's spending and investing rules of thumb?

options.A: Spend exactly 15 percent and invest exactly 10 percent
options.B: Spend at most 10 percent on insurance protection, and invest at least 15 percent
options.C: Spend at least 15 percent on insurance protection, and invest at most 10 percent
options.D: Spend at most 15 percent on insurance protection, and invest at least 10 percent

explanation: The 15 percent figure is a maximum for insurance protection and the 10 percent figure is a minimum for investing. The directions are opposite, which is a common trap.

stem: How many months of expenses does the Guide recommend setting aside for emergencies?

options.A: 3 to 6 months
options.B: 6 to 9 months
options.C: 12 months for everyone
options.D: 1 to 2 months

explanation: The Guide recommends at least 3 to 6 months of expenses for emergencies. Irregular income earners should hold 12 months of expenses.

stem: Why do Singapore Savings Bonds qualify as a place to hold emergency funds?

options.A: Because they pay the highest available interest rate
options.B: Because they are government-guaranteed and can be exited in any month without penalty
options.C: Because they can be pledged as collateral
options.D: Because they are exempt from tax

explanation: SSBs are government-guaranteed and redeemable in any month without penalty, which is what makes them suitable alongside savings accounts for emergency funds.

stem: Can a client's CPF savings serve as his emergency fund?

options.A: Yes, since CPF savings are risk-free
options.B: Yes, up to the amount in the Ordinary Account
options.C: No, because their use is tied to retirement, healthcare and housing
options.D: Yes, provided he is aged 55 or above

explanation: CPF savings cannot serve as emergency funds because their use is tied to retirement, healthcare and housing. Emergency funds also should not be placed in the stock market, and high-interest debts such as credit card bills should be paid off first.

stem: On what basis is the 4 times annual income critical illness multiple derived?

options.A: A 2-year recovery period
options.B: The average cost of cancer treatment in Singapore
options.C: Four years of mortgage repayments
options.D: A 5-year recovery period from a major illness before returning to work

explanation: The multiples come from LIA's Protection Gap Study. The critical illness figure assumes a 5-year recovery period before the insured returns to the workforce, while about 9 times annual income is what dependants need on death or permanent disability.

stem: A client earns S$60,000 a year. Applying the Guide's multiples, what death and total permanent disability cover and what critical illness cover are indicated?

options.A: S$540,000 and S$240,000 respectively
options.B: S$540,000 and S$540,000 respectively
options.C: S$300,000 and S$240,000 respectively
options.D: S$240,000 and S$540,000 respectively

explanation: Death and TPD cover is 9 x S$60,000 = S$540,000, and critical illness cover is 4 x S$60,000 = S$240,000.

stem: Which cohorts does CareShield Life cover?

options.A: All Singapore Citizens and PRs regardless of birth year
options.B: Those born in 1980 onwards, with older ElderShield policyholders able to opt in if they have not developed severe disability
options.C: Those born before 1980 only
options.D: Those aged 65 and above only

explanation: CareShield Life is the national long-term care insurance for cohorts born in 1980 onwards. Older ElderShield policyholders may opt in provided they have not developed severe disability.

stem: What is the severe disability trigger for CareShield Life payouts?

options.A: Inability to perform at least 1 of the 6 activities of daily living
options.B: Inability to perform at least 2 of the 6 activities of daily living
options.C: Inability to perform at least 3 of the 6 activities of daily living
options.D: Any hospitalisation exceeding 30 days

explanation: CareShield Life pays monthly support on severe disability, defined as the inability to perform at least 3 of the 6 activities of daily living. Premiums are fully payable by MediSave.

stem: How are MediShield Life premiums paid?

options.A: Fully payable in cash
options.B: Half by MediSave and half in cash
options.C: Deducted from the Ordinary Account
options.D: Fully payable by MediSave

explanation: MediShield Life premiums are fully payable by MediSave, as are CareShield Life premiums. MediShield Life covers all Singapore Citizens and PRs for large hospital bills and selected costly outpatient treatments such as cancer treatment and dialysis.

stem: Is a financial adviser firm required to use the Basic Financial Planning Guide?

options.A: No, its use is not a regulatory requirement and there is no penalty, though MAS strongly encourages firms to incorporate it
options.B: Yes, but only for clients aged 55 and above
options.C: No, and MAS discourages its use in the advisory process
options.D: Yes, it is a regulatory requirement with penalties for non-adoption

explanation: Use of the Guide is not a regulatory requirement and there is no penalty for not adopting it, but MAS strongly encourages FA firms to incorporate it into their advisory process.

stem: A representative shares the Basic Financial Planning Guide with a prospect before conducting a fact-find. Is this a breach?

options.A: Yes, because no advice may be given before a fact-find
options.B: No, because it is general advice, though a full financial needs analysis must still be completed before any transaction
options.C: Yes, unless the prospect signs an acknowledgement
options.D: No, and the Guide replaces the need for a financial needs analysis

explanation: Sharing the Guide before the full fact-find is not a breach because it constitutes general advice. The full financial needs analysis must still be completed before any transaction.

stem: What is the purpose of a Lasting Power of Attorney?

options.A: To record wishes for future health and personal care
options.B: To distribute CPF savings on death
options.C: To appoint trusted persons to decide on your behalf if you lose mental capacity
options.D: To distribute the estate on death

explanation: The Lasting Power of Attorney appoints trusted persons to make decisions during lost mental capacity. The Advance Care Plan records health and personal care wishes, the will distributes the estate, and the CPF nomination distributes CPF savings.

stem: Which instruments does the Guide suggest for short-term needs?

options.A: CPF retirement top-ups
options.B: Investment-linked policies
options.C: Exchange traded funds and unit trusts
options.D: Singapore Savings Bonds, T-bills and fixed deposits

explanation: For the short term the Guide points to Singapore Savings Bonds, T-bills and fixed deposits. For the long term it points to CPF retirement top-ups, exchange traded funds and unit trusts.

stem: What tax relief is available for cash top-ups to CPF Special or Retirement Accounts?

options.A: Up to S$8,000, including top-ups to parents' accounts
options.B: Up to S$8,000, excluding top-ups to parents' accounts
options.C: Up to S$16,000 for the individual's own account only
options.D: No tax relief is available for cash top-ups

explanation: Cash top-ups to CPF Special or Retirement Accounts enjoy up to S$8,000 in tax relief, and this includes top-ups made to parents' accounts.

stem: A 58-year-old client wants to monetise his property. Which options does the Guide identify?

options.A: Pledging the flat against a securities margin account
options.B: The Silver Housing Bonus, the Lease Buyback Scheme, or renting out a room or the flat
options.C: A reverse mortgage from a licensed moneylender
options.D: Transferring the flat to his children

explanation: Those aged 55 or above can monetise property via the Silver Housing Bonus, the Lease Buyback Scheme, or renting out a room or the whole flat.
